title: Reorganize types and add consistency tests
body:
Resolves #83 and the first part of #84 

The added tests compare our interface definitions against our variable definitions to ensure that:
1. For every interface, a "runtime type" variable of the same name exists
2. For every field (in every interface), the same field name and type is defined in the corresponding "runtime type" variable's field

As part of this, the types have been reorganized:
- to be in dependency order (eg: if interface A relies on interface B, A has been moved before interface B)
- primitive types (eg: bytes, uint64, etc) have been moved into their own file
- attestation types have been moved into their own file

Also, all `var` runtime types have been turned into `const`s.

title: WIP Node services - Brainstorm
body:
WIP/brainstorming on organization of the various BeaconNode services.

Some questions:
- Is this the right direction to push? Are these the right level of granularity to start with?
  - I've been looking at [prysm's node](https://github.com/prysmaticlabs/prysm/blob/master/beacon-chain/node/node.go) and [ethereumjs' node](https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-client/blob/master/lib/node.js) and [ethereumjs' service](https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-client/blob/master/lib/service/ethereumservice.js) for ideas

- Are we missing any important services?
I didn't copy prysm's services exactly, because 1. I didn't really see what each service was there for, 2. we may have different needs. But for the sake of brainstorming, do we need eg: a sync service, an operations service? (both are prysm services not represented explicitly here)

- How do we best handle dependencies / data sharing/passing between various services?
You may notice, some of the services instantiated in BeaconNode (intuitively-speaking) should rely in some way on other services (eg: "the beacon chain relies on the db")
I think we want rough guidelines/patterns for how data is passed/shared that help us keep our services reasonably decoupled and help us stay sane as the codebase grows
  eg: do we
    - pass global object into each service's constructor?
    - pass dependent services into each service's constructor? (this seems to be how prysm operates)
    - emit events listened to at the 'node' or another level outside the service? (this seems like it could jibe well with how js works, but requires more detail)

body:
RPC module, some methods stubbed out (probably incomplete too).

The module is split into three submodules for extensibility:
- api - this is where the actual beacon-chain logic goes. So far, we've added an interface, the standard api, and a mock api (for testing)
- protocol - this is currently where the JSON-RPC-specific logic lives. The JSONRPC class is agnostic to the underlying server, so we can use it for json-rpc over tcp, http, ws, node MessageChannel, etc.
- transport - this is where logic specific to a certain transport goes. Currently only a websocket transport exists.

This should include every endpoint a validator needs for block proposal and attesting.

title: Add ProgressiveMerkleTree implementation
body:
- Move `verifyMerkleBranch` to `src/util/merkleTree.ts`
- Add `ProgressiveMerkleTree` implementation
  - follows the logic of the deposit contract
  - the tree only stores the latest non-default branch in the merkle tree (we take advantage of the fact that most of the tree is successive hashes of zeroed data)
  - this tree is append-only,  `push`ing a new item into the tree returns a `proof` (`bytes32[]`)
  - the `proof`, along with the `root`, `index`, and inserted `item` can be verified w/ `verifyMerkleBranch`
  - the tree can return the `count` of items in the tree (used to get the `index` of an item to-be-inserted or a just-inserted item) and the `root` of the tree
  - `clone` a tree to create a duplicate tree

title: Refactor networking module
body:
Refactored the networking/p2p module to integrate rpc.
This is working, but some features are still missing, to be built out in a future PR for the sync module. Eg: emitting request events and topic events from the top level networking object.

Important files:
- `src/network/interface.ts` - the top-level networking interface and peer interface. The peer interface gives promisified request/response methods for each request type. The sync module will use these (and emitted events) to hook into rpc/gossipsub
- `src/network/libp2p/nodejs/bundle.ts` - the base libp2p configuration for nodejs
- `src/network/libp2p/rpcController.ts` - handles establishing new rpc streams with new peers, maintaining a list of peer objects, maintaining a list of outstanding requests/responses.
- `src/network/libp2p/peer.ts` - peer object that wraps a rpc stream
- `src/network/libp2p/network.ts` - implementation of the networking interface. it keeps track of a libp2p object, a gossipsub/floodsub object and a rpcController object, and uses those to implement the necessary methods.

title: Syncing WIP
body:
This pull request is currently a WIP as there are still things that do not work the way they should. Currently initial syncing and regular sync "work". But "work" here is used very loosely. 
It "works" because it syncs. But it does so very inefficiently because the block processing queue and syncing is flawed as @mpetrunic described in standup. 
What happens is that if before the block processing queue finishes processing the blocks in the queue and a new block is received through gossip, we will ask for all the blocks in range (most recently processed, newly gossiped block) even if we already have them.

title: SSZ Rewrite
body:
- SSZ rewritten using Type classes, SSZ operations attached as methods to classes.
eg: `serialize(Type, value)` is now `Type.serialize(value)`
- SSZ type classes include two (soon three) implementations
  - they can operate on "structural" data, ie: the data structures we've been using (`Object`s, `Array`s, etc)
  - they can operate on "tree" data, ie: a `Tree` from the `@chainsafe/persistent-merkle-tree` repo
```typescript
const structuralState: BeaconState = config.types.BeaconState.structural.defaultValue();
const treeState: BeaconState = config.types.BeaconState.tree.defaultValue();
config.types.BeaconState.equals(structuralState, treeState) === true;
```
  - the 'handlers' for each implementation are attached to the type under `Type.structural`, `Type.tree`, and `Type.byteArray`, Code available for these implementations available under `ssz/src/backings`
  - basic types have only a single implementation, code available under `ssz/src/types/basic`
- Non-structural data is wrapped in an ES6 `Proxy` to give a structural interface (getters/setters/iteration/ownKeys)
  - eg: 
```typescript
// treeState implements the BeaconState interface! (even though it is actually a Tree)
const treeState: BeaconState = config.types.BeaconState.tree.defaultValue();
treeState.slot = 5;
for (const validator of treeState.validators) {...}
```
- `ssz-type-schema` is gone, no longer used. Instead, the types are more tightly coupled to ssz operations. types can be found in `ssz/src/types`, and additionally in `ssz/src/backings/structural` and `ssz/src/backings/tree`.
- `eth2.0-types` have been updated to suit
  - Typescript types have changed, this significantly effects code downstream, eg: in the state transition, as the new types are not as expressive as the old types
    - `Array`s replaced with `Vector`, `List` (see `ssz/src/interface.ts` for definitions)
    - `BitVector`/`BitList` (from `@chainsafe/bit-utils`) replaced with `Vector<boolean>` and `List<boolean>` -- no more `bit-utils`, it is no longer used
    - `Bytes32`/`BytesX` replaced with `ByteVector`.
      - A `Uint8Array` can be returned by doing `valueOf()` on a `ByteVector`. Unfortunately, this must be explicitly cast to `Uint8Array` for now. eg: `bvector.valueOf() as Uint8Array`
    - `Uint8Array` is used directly (as opposed to `Buffer`) as input/output for hashing, etc.
    - lower case primitive names have been changed to uppercase for consistency and closer alignment with spec, eg: `bytes32` -> `Bytes32`

current benchmarks of various operations done on validator registry of 10k validators:
```
iterate - structural x 190,399 ops/sec ±0.51% (98 runs sampled)
iterate - tree x 74.05 ops/sec ±0.64% (67 runs sampled)

get validator - structural x 44,796,868 ops/sec ±1.63% (89 runs sampled)
get validator - tree x 469,510 ops/sec ±1.96% (84 runs sampled)

get validator property - structural x 39,335,530 ops/sec ±1.47% (89 runs sampled)
get validator property - tree x 241,673 ops/sec ±6.50% (74 runs sampled)

set validator - structural x 187,899 ops/sec ±5.51% (73 runs sampled)
set validator - tree x 9,461 ops/sec ±12.51% (74 runs sampled)

set validator property - structural x 20,798,474 ops/sec ±1.77% (88 runs sampled)
set validator property - tree x 108,128 ops/sec ±3.97% (82 runs sampled)

serialize - old x 18.07 ops/sec ±2.16% (48 runs sampled)
serialize - structural x 44.96 ops/sec ±0.61% (56 runs sampled)
serialize - tree x 14.96 ops/sec ±1.97% (38 runs sampled)

hashTreeRoot - old x 3.02 ops/sec ±5.00% (12 runs sampled)
hashTreeRoot - structural x 3.97 ops/sec ±3.06% (14 runs sampled)
hashTreeRoot - tree x 5,403 ops/sec ±1.36% (80 runs sampled)
```

title: Fork choice: make sure head() have correct justified/finalized epoch like the store
body:
## Goal
+ Close #637 
## Approach
+ Maintain justified & finalized epochs in our "store"
+ Maintain justified & finalized epochs in our node
+ Change weighing system taking justified & finalized epochs of best target into account
+ When adding block, if it causes any best targets to be epoch conflict, we do "soft unlink" by setting `bestChild=null`, this causes those best targets unreachable from the justified root
+ When adding block, relink if those best target's epochs now correct (and previously it's not)

title: Block process stream
body:
I would like some feedback on this block processing stream proposal before I start writing tests and modifying rest of codebase
Block lifecycle is:
network/api -> chain -> blockProcessStream - > validate -> process -> postProcess
                                                                                          \
                                                                                             -> blockPool-> blockProcessStream
After we process block, we will notify block pool which will put blocks waiting for that parent back on process stream.

Pros:
- very much testable code so we can cover a lot of scenarios with unit tests
- clean modular code
- parallel validate/process/post processes

Cons:
- it seems like during sync every block except first will end up in block pool before being process
   - it because there is a great chance most block will go trough validate before block process starts
   - naive idea to mitigate it is to combine validate and process function into one but we will end up with huge function again and we wouldn't be able to discard some blocks while waiting for process operations

resolves #694

title: Merge opPool and db
body:
Remove `OpPool`, in favor of consolidating "op pool functionality" in the `Repository`s associated with pending operations.
More clearly distinguish the purposes of various `IBeaconDb` `Repository`s.

The `OpPool` module has always been fraught with an identity crisis.
What is its purpose? What differentiates it from other data that's stored?

In practice, the `OpPool` module acted as a subset of the `IBeaconDb` with additional methods on several of the `Repository`s.

I think this distinction between `OpPool` `Module`s and `BeaconDb` `Repository`s is not actually helpful, and the additional level of indirection is just a complicating factor to understanding the codebase. We can remove a bunch of duplicate code and simplify the code by unifying these modules.

title: Fix up eth1 processing
body:
Resolves https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/855

`IBeaconDb` has been modified to store deposits and eth1 data.
EthersEth1Notifier now processes eth1 blocks, starting at `depositContract.deployedAt`, maintaining the follow distance, parsing deposit events and eth1 data from each block and storing in `IBeaconDb`.

new `IBeaconDb` properties:
- `depositData` - `DepositData` indexed by deposit index. Data stored pending chain processing (as part of the 'op pool'.
- `depositDataRoot` - `Root<DepositData>` indexed by deposit index. Deposit data roots are stored permanently, and a `TreeBacked` list of deposit roots (the deposit tree) is maintained in memory for fast deposit processing when creating blocks. (this tree replaces our previous `db.depositDataRootList`)
- `eth1Data - `Eth1Data` indexed by timestamp. In `EthersEth1Notifier`, because historical eth1 state is not fetchable from providers, the deposit count and deposit root is calculated, not from the deposit contract, but from the `IBeaconDb`. (this replaces the eth1 block cache we had before)

new `Repository` methods:
- `firstKey`, `firstValue`, `firstEntry`
- `lastKey`, `lastValue`, `lastEntry`

new `IBeaconTypes` type:
- `DepositEvent` - `DepositData` with index (TODO: once ssz is updated, we can replace `EthersEth1Notifier#parseDepositEvent` with `DepositEvent.fromJson(_,{case: "snake"})`)

Eth1 voting was updated:
- We no longer fetch candidate eth1data from a `IEth1Notifier` eth1 block cache
- instead, we fetch `Eth1Data`, stored in `IBeaconDb`, filtered to the candidate voting range
- code moved to `chain/factory/block`

title: Add state cache
body:
Generally, this PR allows much of the chain processing to happen in memory, rather than fetching/storing to disk. Fork choice, recent states, unfinalized block(summary) tree are all in memory, while unfinalized blocks remain stored to disk.
Ideally this addition will be followed up with a backup/restore procedure to store/restore the unfinalized block summary and recent state cache on teardown/bootup.

- Add `forkChoice.getBlockSummaryAtSlot` - this lets us get rid of the (incorrect) Bucket.blockSlotRef slot -> blockRoot mapping. Instead, `forkChoice.getBlockSummaryAtSlot` exposes the whole BlockSummary, indexed by slot, as seen by the fork choice head.
- Add `chain.getBlockAtSlot` - use `forkChoice.getBlockSummaryAtSlot` to fetch a block, indexed by slot, from the database, works for both unfinalized or finalized blocks. This lets us get rid of `db.block.getBySlot` which relied on Bucket.blockSlotRef
- Remove `db.chain` and related - no longer store head information in db, instead, rely on `chain.forkChoice`
- Add `db.stateCache` and `db.stateArchive`, remove `db.state` - Instead of storing all states to disk, indexed by root, store finalized states to disk in `db.stateArchive`, indexed by epoch, store all unfinalized states in `db.stateCache`, indexed by root.
Note: state cache has a similar API to `Repository`, but is synchronous
Note: state cache and state archive return and rely on `TreeBacked<BeaconState>`, not just `BeaconState`.
- Fetch latest finalized state from disk on startup, store new finalized state to disk on finalized checkpoint event, clear old finalized states from cache on finalized checkpoint event. This can be improved by pruning the stateArchive so we don't store every newly finalized state.

title: Add prettier as an eslint plugin
body:
### Rationale

A code formating tool homogenizes style across contributors, which help new ones match the repo style and stay consistent.

The setup in this PR runs prettier as an eslint plugin. In CI, formatting errors will be shown in the `lint` stage. Most of the issues found by the prettier plugin can be fixed with the `lint:fix` script. Alternatively prettier can be run directly across the entire repo with
```
./node_modules/.bin/prettier --write 'packages/**/*.{ts,md}'
```

Locally, contributors may choose to run it manually, before committing with a git hook (i.e. husky), or incorporating it into their IDE and trigger it every save.

I've selected the settings in `.prettierrc.js` config that generated the smallest git diff, so they had the widest adoption in the codebase. Specific settings that were contentious and may be discussed are:
- [`trailingComma`](https://prettier.io/docs/en/options.html#trailing-commas): `"es5"` - Print trailing commas when multi-line and valid in ES5 (objects, arrays, etc.).
- [`arrowParens`](https://prettier.io/docs/en/options.html#arrow-function-parentheses): `"always"` - Always include parens. Example: `(x) => x`. 
>*from prettier docs*: 
>At first glance, avoiding parentheses may look like a better choice because of less visual noise. However, when Prettier removes parentheses, it becomes harder to add type annotations, extra arguments or default values as well as making other changes. Consistent use of parentheses provides a better developer experience.

### How to incorporate

To incorporate the formatter I would recommend waiting for a moment with no open PRs, since it will generate a big diff (as of opening this PR `599 files changed, 5729 insertions(+), 6242 deletions(-)`).

As we're not sure the correctness of EpochContext here, I propose we switch back to the legacy way of calculating state root. This doesnt happen very frequently at runtime so I think we don't have to worry about the performance here.

```
    deposit   Submits a deposit to an Eth1 validator...
  wallet
    create    Creates a new HD (hierarchical-deterministic) EIP-2386 wallet
    list      Lists the names of all wallets
```

All major directories are one level deep of the global `rootDir` path. This account directory structure is very similar to `ethdo` and `ighthouse`'s, expect that this one mixes account data with db data.
```

├── keystores
│   └── 0x871cb1c0b1e6b67473003ccfbdf9532d3b0d29bf51b07df6a3fae2ba25526d18e67a119babd44aa3b22b9bc4ef16f71f

│       ├── 000003.log
│       ├── CURRENT
│       ├── LOCK
│       ├── LOG

└── wallets
    └── 05939fbd-923a-4559-b41f-2e43ad8fd80b
        └── 05939fbd-923a-4559-b41f-2e43ad8fd80b
```

### Other minor changes
- Clean CLI export style to prevent the use of 'as any' casting. Type-safety = :smile: 
- CLI now prints help when no command is provided and it's required.
- CLI now recommends possible command names if no command is matched
- Added welcome message in help of the root command
```
🌟 Lodestar: Ethereum 2.0 TypeScript Implementation of the Beacon Chain
```

### Next steps
- Provide more options to broadcast a deposit data, i.e. connect to Metamask, IPC, Ledger?
- Support non-HD wallets

title: once/on patch, eth1vote optimization, pubkey cache change, attestation optimizations
body:
Collection of Altona optimizations/hotfixes

- once/on patch (not mine)
- eth1vote optimization
  - previously it hashed the eth1 data of the block over and over again, for each comparison. Super slow. Conver to tree backed, to cache hash-tree-root, and have much faster counting
- pubkey cache hack, index bound safety
  - the pubkeys don't change for eth1 data, unless a bad majority vote is made by an attacker and accepted by the local node.
  - added some safety checks, we don't want not-yet-existing pubkeys of a different beacon fork (but the same eth1 chain) to mess up the transition logic
     - optimized indices check in the attestation processing too

Edit, more optimization:
- convert the block to a tree-backed block. The amount of times the block is merkleized, its parts are merkleized, and how large parts end up in the state (attestation bitfields), hash-tee-root caching is too important.
- Optimize get-indexed-attestation. Don't unnecessarily copy. Don't use a Set when it's unique anyway. In-place sort the (small-ish) list of participants.
- Cut off eth1 vote logic when half of the period is not reached yet. No majority vote can exist before then, thus no state change anyway.

title: bugfix: justification based on unslashed target-attesting balance
body:
The spec justification rules read as:
```python
    matching_target_attestations = get_matching_target_attestations(state, previous_epoch)  # Previous epoch
    if get_attesting_balance(state, matching_target_attestations) * 3 >= get_total_active_balance(state) * 2:
```
`get_attesting_balance` does something special: it filters out slashed validators, and floors it to a minimum of 1 effective balance increment.
```python
def get_total_balance(state: BeaconState, indices: Set[ValidatorIndex]) -> Gwei:
    """
    Return the combined effective balance of the ``indices``.
    ``EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT`` Gwei minimum to avoid divisions by zero.
    Math safe up to ~10B ETH, afterwhich this overflows uint64.
    """
    return Gwei(max(EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT, sum([state.validators[index].effective_balance for index in indices])))

def get_attesting_balance(state: BeaconState, attestations: Sequence[PendingAttestation]) -> Gwei:
    """
    Return the combined effective balance of the set of unslashed validators participating in ``attestations``.
    Note: ``get_total_balance`` returns ``EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_INCREMENT`` Gwei minimum to avoid divisions by zero.
    """
    return get_total_balance(state, get_unslashed_attesting_indices(state, attestations))
```

This was missed in the optimized `eth2fastspec` variant (fixed it in v0.0.5), and got into Lodestar.

In Altona testnet this caused the code to make an incorrect justification in the transition of skip slots from 71933 to 71938.

I will review the edge case further, and try to introduce testing in the spec-tests for this. For now, this fix can be used to sync continue to sync Altona, Lodestar almost made the head already :+1: 


 with minimum of 1 increment

title: genesis and skip slots case in finalized checkpoint check
body:
Based on this testnet error:
```
2020-07-10 05:49:24  [SYNC]             warn: Received block parent root doesn't match our head head=0x7cb6a152924d493d6119407b732461d2addee6ec833b38fe169119d576db1dcd, headSlot=76069, blockParent=0x6f0f0920aa5d299df1245d925a2f2152c2550226c246ea24f169fcedc72ec700, blockSlot=76071
(node:201339) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: TypeError: Cannot read property 'message' of null
    at BeaconReqRespHandler.shouldDisconnectOnStatus (/home/proto/projects/lodestar/packages/lodestar/lib/sync/reqResp/reqResp.js:214:130)
    at async BeaconReqRespHandler.onStatus (/home/proto/projects/lodestar/packages/lodestar/lib/sync/reqResp/reqResp.js:184:9)
    at async ReqResp.<anonymous> (/home/proto/projects/lodestar/packages/lodestar/lib/sync/reqResp/reqResp.js:74:18)
(Use `node --trace-warnings ...` to show where the warning was created)
```

As shared in discord:
> The problem is that the slot may be a skip slot
> And the block root may be from multiple epochs back even
> the epoch in the checkpoint is there to checkpoint the tail end of skip slots, even if there is no block

Changes:
- fix genesis case while we are at it
- cheap very common check against current finalized checkpoint first
- alternatively use head state for checking (mainnet config has a tree of 8000 or so roots to check against). This deals with skip-slots, it will return the most recent block for the given epoch.
- leave out the case for historical checking. There is no lookup for "latest finalized block root for epoch N", and looking up a block directly may return nil in case of a skip slot. To fix later, with DB changes to track finalized roots.

title: Refactor CLI option handling
body:
This PR tackles various improvements to simplify the CLI option handling that wer not splittable between smaller PRs.

1. Remove `canonicalOptions` usage

For yargs to parse options whose name is a JSON path, `canonicalOptions` was used to assign their first alias as their name within the yargs options object. Now instead of declaring options individually, they are defined in an object where JSON paths are allowed as keys. This approach is more transparent and "common", but it does not guarantee that the JSON path of the variable matches its expected type.

```ts
export const metricsOptions = {
  "metrics.enabled": {
    type: "boolean",
    default: false,
    group: "metrics",
  } as Options
}
```

2. Compute paths in the handler to remove "dynamic" options

Beacon options were defined as functions so they could be computed dynamically and compute fs subpaths with the options provided by the user. Now beacon paths are computed in the handler with `getBeaconPaths` so the options can be static, following the same approach as the `account` commands

```
$rootDir
 └── $beaconDir
     ├── beacon.config.json
     ├── peer-id.json
     ├── enr.json
     └── chain-db
```

3. Reorg options

There where duplicated options between various commands. Now shared options can be found in `src/options` with the following groups

```
src/options
├── beaconNodeOptions/
├── globalOptions.ts
└── paramsOptions.ts
```

- `beaconNodeOptions/` includes options strictly part of the `BeaconNodeOptions` type.
- `paramsOptions` are options dynamically generated from the spec file
- `globalOptions`: Global options.

4. Simplify default parsing

Convert all "config" yargs Options from using `default` to `defaultDescription`. Yargs Options has a defaultDescription property which in practice makes that value show in `--help` as if it was a default, BUT it's not an actual default so we can know in the handler which options have been actually set by the user and which not. Then, at the handler we can easily merge default config with config files with CLI config.

```js
options = mergeConfigOptions(options);
```

Which does a deepmerge of `defaultOptions` > `templateConfigFile` > `configFile` > `userOptions`

5. Un-nest options outside of `BeaconNodeOptions`

Options not part of the actual type `BeaconNodeOptions` are moved to the root level of `options`:
- `options.chain.name` > `options.preset`
- `options.chain.params` > `options.params`
- `options.network.peerIdFile` > `options.peerIdFile`
- `options.network.enrFile` > `options.enrFile`

```
Given 3 peers, we can query by interleaving way, assuming we want to get block 10 to 20 for regular sync:

Round 1 - fallback

Query bestPeer with start_slot=17, step=3
```

body:
Parallelizable effort to tackle https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/885. Sets `strictNullChecks = true` in a single package so eventually it can be set in the root tsconfig.

### Specific issues discussion

- **Cast empty arrays to ssz type List<T>**: We may want to have the ssz library export empty lists of functions that create type-safe empty lists to prevent unsafe casting.
- **Cast arrays to ssz type List<T>**: Is typecasting good enough here? Maybe it would make sense to have a casting function to do that more safely.
- **Assert Number is not undefined on top of Number.isSafeInteger**: Satisfy the tsc compiler
- **Add null to getCommitteeAssignment return signature**: Consumers of this method will be unsafe until they have `strictNullChecks = true`.
- **Ensure pubkeys array is not empty before reducing it**: Even if it never happens, let's make the tsc compiler happy. 
- **Ensure shuffling properties are not undefined before accessing them**: This required quite a lot of changes. Do these properties really have to be defined as maybe `undefined`? Why may they be undefined?

```bash
title: Organize similar e2e tests into a similar structure and naming
body:
There are 3 tests that progress the chain until a checkpoint:
- Run multi node multi thread interop validators (no eth1) until checkpoint
  - 4 nodes / 8 vc / 1 validator > until justifiedCheckpoint
- Run multi node single thread interop validators (no eth1) until checkpoint
  - 4 nodes / 8 vc / 1 validator > until justifiedCheckpoint
- Run single node single thread interop validators (no eth1) until checkpoint
  - 1 node / 8 vc / 8 validator > until justifiedCheckpoint
  - 1 node / 8 vc / 8 validator > until finalizedCheckpoint
  - 1 node / 1 vc / 32 validator > until justifiedCheckpoint

I've just made the naming more consistent among them and try to structure them similarly. It can be greatly improved from here.

Also, do we want to run all this test? What are their best configurations? Looking them in perspective, they don't seem super coherent. Maybe we can optimize them easily now.
```

title: Allow exiting process by force
body:
The current way of handling process signals causes almost always to create a zombie unexited process.
According to the docs https://nodejs.org/api/process.html#process_signal_events

> 'SIGTERM' and 'SIGINT' have default handlers on non-Windows platforms that reset the terminal mode before exiting with code 128 + signal number. If one of these signals has a listener installed, its default behavior will be removed (Node.js will no longer exit).

So by attaching a cleanup listener to SIGINT and never calling process.exit() afterwards the only option for the process to exit is if the event loop becomes empty. This would be ideal but it's a very difficult task to accomplish having so many components and dependencies. A single unresolved promise or listener would leave the process zombie.

This PR adds a second listener to SIGINT so that if the user hits CTRL+C twice the process will exit by force.

title: Separate fork choice
body:
Current Status:
- able to run the chain from genesis and restore from checkpoints
- tests untouched and likely failing

Big items:

- `StateContextCheckpointCache` has been internally refactored, and its public interface extended
  - add `pruneFinalized(cp: Checkpoint)` - will prune checkpoints from epochs before the finalized epoch
  - add `prune(finalized: Checkpoint, justified: Checkpoint)` - similar to `stateCache.prune` - if there are more epochs present than `MAX_EPOCHS`, will prune starting from the lowest epoch to the highest epoch, skipping the finalized and justified epochs.
  - add `getLatest(cp: Checkpoint): ITreeStateContext` - starting from `cp.epoch` and going backwards, searches the cache for hits with `cp.root`. "Finds the latest state context at the checkpoint where the checkpoint's root is cp.root" and the checkpoint's epoch is lte cp.epoch."
- `StateRegenerator` has been added - `src/chain/regen.ts`
  - it can regenerate states from blocks _that have already been processed_ , given `forkChoice`, `stateCache`, `checkpointStateCache`, and `db.blocks`
  - it intelligently attempts to perform the smallest amount of regeneration necessary to regen the requested state. To that end, it exposes three different methods.
  - it reuses some block processing machinery (`emitCheckpointEvent`, `runStateTransition`) so as to enable re-seeding the checkpoint cache
  - it throws a `RegenError` with well-defined error codes and types, this allows us to tighten the interface to disallow nulls.
  - it has one major TODO, it must queue requests instead of allowing multiple concurrent requests
  - `getPreState(block: BeaconBlock): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - the same as `getPreState` that we were using in our block processor. It can request a more recent checkpoint state if the block occurs after many skip-slots, skipping epoch transitions :) 
  - `getCheckpointState(cp: Checkpoint): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - returns the checkpoint state. It minimizes regeneration by first searching the checkpoint cache for checkpoint states with cp.root, which may then just be `processSlots`ed. Otherwise regens the 'ol-fashioned way', by state root.
  - `getState(stateRoot: Root): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - returns the state whose root is stateRoot. This is where the actual block replay happens. It iterates backwards thru the block tree from the requested state, to the first state that we have cached, (searching the checkpointStateCache as well!), then replaying the blocks that were iterated thru to the requested state, once a state has been found.
- Adds an optional `EpochProcess` object to `EpochContext`.
  - This object is used in epoch transitions to simplify validator balance counting. It holds flattened validators, validator statuses (whether they can attest, whether they've attested for important recent states, etc), total attested balances, etc.
  - This ends up being very useful for updating the fork choice balances.
  - We will find more uses for this after this PR, likely will be very nice to scrape for metrics re network participation.
- Block processing refactored slightly
  - `getPreState` is now handled by the `StateRegenerator`
  - `runStateTransition` and other utilities moved to `src/chain/blocks/stateTransition.ts`
- Block/state archival tasks refactored
  - they are now both triggered by the `forkChoice:finalized` event, the `forkChoice:pruned` event is no more.
  - we also prune state caches, triggered by the `checkpoint` event, but not in a task as its a one-liner
  - block archival no longer loads _all_ blocks in `block` repository into memory at once, instead streams
  - block archival strategy, run before fork choice pruning
    - stream all blocks in `block` repository, one by one
    - if the block is more recent than the finalized block, ignore
    - if the finalized block is a descendant of the block, store in the blockArchive
    - delete all un-ignored blocks
  - state archival now archives the finalized state from `checkpointStateCache` (these will be candidates for weak subjectivity :) )
- Add `@chainsafe/lodestar-fork-choice` package
  - split into two 'levels', protoArray, and forkChoice
  - protoArray - the block dag, not much else
  - forkChoice
    - provides an interface very close to the spec
    - includes an `IForkChoiceStore`, very similar to `Store` in the spec -- this is implemented in the lodestar package with knowledge of the `ChainEventEmitter`
    - stores votes, balances, queued attestations
  - Attestation weighting is completely different than before
    - Instead of feeding attestations in with weights attached per attestation, we feed in something like a `LatestMessage` from the spec.
    - attestations are reweighted all-at-once, using `forkChoice.updateBalances`. Using `epochContext.epochProcess`, this is fast, lots of the work was already done as part of epoch processing.
    - attestation reweighting is triggered by the `forkChoice:justified` event.

title: Refactor eth1 data for block production
body:
Refactors (enables) eth1 data for block production. The previous iteration had flaws and PR https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/1443 deactivated block production. This PR will to re-enable it.

#### Architecture overview

The architecture of this PR is heavily inspired by Lighthouse. There is a specific class for block production with a minimal interface meant to be called by the block production API for a given state. The logic to prepare both the eth1Data vote and the deposits with proofs is encapsulated in the class (moved from its previous location of `chain/factory/block`
```ts
export interface IEth1ForBlockProduction {
  getEth1DataAndDeposits(state: TreeBacked<BeaconState>): Promise<{eth1Data: Eth1Data; deposits: Deposit[]}>;
}
```

The class `IEth1ForBlockProduction` upon instantiation will fetch both deposits and blocks from an eth1 node at intervals. The class consumes two other classes who wrap the `db` module and handle read / write opts
- `Eth1BlockHeaderCache`: Eth1 block headers indexed by blockNumber
- `Eth1DepositsCache`: Eth1 deposit logs indexed by validator index + partial eth1 data (depositCount, depositRoot) indexed by blockNumber. The latter is derived from deposit logs exclusively.

#### Goals

All logic whenever possible is stored in pure utility functions which are unit tested without stubs. The classes should contain as little logic as possible and just connect the logic heavy function with internal state and data sources.

Database and data fetching concerns are split into different classes, brought together only in the main class `IEth1ForBlockProduction`.

`IEth1ForBlockProduction` starts its long-running process in the constructor, not requiring a `start` method. To stop and destroy the class, it accepts an `AbortSignal` as a constructor parameter. The signal will stop the main setInterval handle and also interrupt HTTP requests with the new httpEth1Client functions.

title: Disregard unfinalized blocks upon restart
body:

## Current flow
+ Upon restart, load and restore from block 73249 to block 110000 through block processor in order to populate state cache and fork choice

## New flow
+ Upon restart, disregard unfinalized blocks
+ Populate forkchoice from previous finalized slot until current finalized slot to make it head, this is quick
+ Only populate state cache with last finalized state
+ Don't even touch block processor in most cases
+ Initial sync start querying from block 73249

title: Separate fork choice
body:
part of #1517 

state regeneration saved for a separate PR
other updates already made in in #1537 and #1538

- Block processing refactored slightly
  - `runStateTransition` and other utilities moved to `src/chain/blocks/stateTransition.ts`
- Block/state archival tasks refactored
  - they are now both triggered by the `forkChoice:finalized` event, the `forkChoice:pruned` event is no more.
  - we also prune state caches, triggered by the `checkpoint` event, but not in a task as its a one-liner
  - block archival no longer loads _all_ blocks in `block` repository into memory at once, instead streams
  - block archival strategy, run before fork choice pruning
    - stream all blocks in `block` repository, one by one
    - if the block is more recent than the finalized block, ignore
    - if the finalized block is a descendant of the block, store in the blockArchive
    - delete all un-ignored blocks
  - state archival now archives the finalized state from `checkpointStateCache` (these will be candidates for weak subjectivity :) )
- Add `@chainsafe/lodestar-fork-choice` package
  - split into two 'levels', protoArray, and forkChoice
  - protoArray - the block dag, not much else
  - forkChoice
    - provides an interface very close to the spec
    - includes an `IForkChoiceStore`, very similar to `Store` in the spec -- this is implemented in the lodestar package with knowledge of the `ChainEventEmitter`
    - stores votes, balances, queued attestations
  - Attestation weighting is completely different than before
    - Instead of feeding attestations in with weights attached per attestation, we feed in something like a `LatestMessage` from the spec.
    - attestations are reweighted all-at-once, using `forkChoice.updateBalances`. Using `epochContext.epochProcess`, this is fast, lots of the work was already done as part of epoch processing.
    - attestation reweighting is triggered by the `forkChoice:justified` event.

title: Add state regenerator
body:
- `IStateRegenerator` interface has been added, along with implementations `StateRegenerator` and `QueuedStateRegenerator`, - `src/chain/regen/`
  - it can regenerate states from blocks _that have already been processed_ , given `forkChoice`, `stateCache`, `checkpointStateCache`, and `db.blocks`
  - it intelligently attempts to perform the smallest amount of regeneration necessary to regen the requested state. To that end, it exposes 4 different methods.
  - it reuses some block processing machinery (`emitCheckpointEvent`, `runStateTransition`) so as to enable re-seeding the checkpoint cache (using the emitted events)
  - it throws a `RegenError` with well-defined error codes and types, this allows us to tighten the interface to disallow nulls.
  - it queues requests, one regeneration allowed at a time
  - `getPreState(block: BeaconBlock): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - similar to `getPreState` that we were using in our block processor. It can request a more recent checkpoint state if the block occurs after many skip-slots, skipping epoch transitions :) 
  - `getCheckpointState(cp: Checkpoint): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - returns the checkpoint state. It minimizes regeneration by first searching the checkpoint cache for checkpoint states with cp.root, which may then just be `processSlots`ed. Otherwise regens the 'ol-fashioned way', by state root.
  - `getBlockSlotState(blockRoot: Root, slot: Slot): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - returns the block state at the requested slot. This is a lot like `getCheckpointState`, but more flexible, especially useful for dealing with the head state, eg: `regen.getBlockSlotState(forkChoice.getHeadRoot(), clock.currentSlot)`. This is nice, because in periods of skip slots, we will only process the checkpoint with the blockRoot once.
  - `getState(stateRoot: Root): Promise<ITreeStateContext>` - returns the state whose root is stateRoot. This is where the actual block replay happens. It iterates backwards thru the block tree from the requested state, to the first state that we have cached, (searching the checkpointStateCache as well!), then replaying the blocks that were iterated thru to the requested state, once a state has been found.

- Support for abort signals
- Better error handling. `packages/lodestar/test/e2e/eth1/jsonRpcHttpClient.test.ts` tests many error cases to produce useful messages

title: Gossip Validation Spec Compliance
body:
I've been going through the network spec (https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/blob/dev/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#global-topics) trying to verify that we are up-to-spec, and have found some holes in this that are fixed here.

```[IGNORE] The valid aggregate attestation defined by hash_tree_root(aggregate) has not already been seen (via aggregate gossip, within a verified block, or through the creation of an equivalent aggregate locally).```

- fixing this by calling addAggregateAndProof inside produceAggregateAndProof (so that it can be verified in the seenAttestationCache check during AggregateAndProof validation)

```[REJECT] The aggregator's validator index is within the committee -- i.e. aggregate_and_proof.aggregator_index in get_beacon_committee(state, aggregate.data.slot, aggregate.data.index).```

- we currently throw an error in getBeaconCommittee if `index >= slotCommittees.length`, which would bubble up to the gossip validation try/catch which returns an IGNORE, but we need to throw a REJECT.  I added try/catch to make sure we throw a REJECT when appropriate within the aggregationAndProof gossip validation.

```[IGNORE] attestation.data.slot is within the last ATTESTATION_PROPAGATION_SLOT_RANGE slots (within a MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY allowance) -- i.e. attestation.data.slot + ATTESTATION_PROPAGATION_SLOT_RANGE >= current_slot >= attestation.data.slot (a client MAY queue future attestations for processing at the appropriate slot).```

- we aren't currently using MAXIMUM_GOSSIP_CLOCK_DISPARITY, so I fixed this and consolidated the check into a common function that can be used for validating slots for both attestation and aggregateAndProof gossip validation.

```[REJECT] The current finalized_checkpoint is an ancestor of the block defined by attestation.data.beacon_block_root -- i.e. get_ancestor(store, attestation.data.beacon_block_root, compute_start_slot_at_epoch(store.finalized_checkpoint.epoch)) == store.finalized_checkpoint.root```
- we weren't checking for this, so i added a check for this

fixes #1544 
fixes #1573 
fixes #1572 

More to come, possibly.
I'm also going to check our unit/e2e tests and make sure we are running tests that check explicitly for the rules outlined for gossip validation in the network spec.

I would like to change some of the tests to where we aren't as many stubs and instead use some real-ish data (except maybe in places where we're trying to force values for conditions that we've already tested for with real-ish data), but if I go that route, I will do it in another PR.

title: Error logger formatting - proposal 2
body:
Extends https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/1609 with some opinionated decisions.

- Adds a placeholder implementation of a human-readable and a JSON logger. Can be configured with the logger option `format`
- Adds two "serialization" functions: `toJson(arg: unknown): Json` and `toString(json: Json): string`. These can then are used in the winston format functions. They never throw and I've added many test cases for most possible types.
- Adds a `LodestarError` which all custom errors should extend and which contains a `toObj` method. `toObj` returns the data that should be printed by the logger associated to that error. Extenders of `LodestarError` can customize that function if necessary.

#### Goals

- If a `LodestarError` is catched by external code it will have a message property with that error's code
- When a `LodestarError` is logged by our logger there will not be duplicate information
- Serializing a `LodestarError` in our logger is type-safe without castings
- Our logger will log external errors with their message property as well as all their metadata

title: Run lodestar with node directly not yarn
body:
I've found that `yarn` does a really bad job at handling child script signals. On CTRL+C it only forwards the first SIGINT and ignores the rest, breaking our graceful shutdown pattern. `npm` does propagate signals correctly but I would recommend users to run lodestar directly with node to prevent further issues.

Also Windows, MacOS, Linux handle CTRL+C differently so the simpler the better

#### Test

Try running
```
node --trace-deprecation ./packages/lodestar-cli/bin/lodestar beacon --testnet spadina
```
vs
```
yarn run cli beacon --testnet spadina
```
And look for this log https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/d9fcdad8a5ea6e43515bdd6e4ed1c4012eb7332b/packages/lodestar-cli/src/util/process.ts#L19 after hitting CTRL+C twice fast 

#### Solution

I propose to run the CLI bin file directly. In this PR I've added a softlink to it, but I'm open to better suggestions if any.

title: Deal with circular references
body:
In Zinken launch, a circular reference prevented the logger from showing an important error. 

```
(node:19660) UnhandledPromiseRejectionWarning: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at Object (<anonymous>)
    at baseGetTag (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:3067:51)
    at isFunction (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:11679:17)
    at isArrayLike (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:11359:58)
    at keys (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:13333:14)
    at /home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:4920:21
    at baseForOwn (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:2990:24)
    at mapValues (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/node_modules/lodash/lodash.js:13426:7)
    at toJson (/home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/src/json.ts:22:14)
    at /home/ubuntu/lodestar/packages/lodestar-utils/src/json.ts:22:40
```

This PR allows the toJson and toString methods to deal with circular references and not throw errors. 

Then, in case of circular references the logger will still print part of the original intended message. However, if a circular reference occurs, it typically will come from un-intended metdata so it's okay to omit it.

title: Use min-max surround to optimize slashing protection
body:
Use the algo from https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-surround#min-max-surround to detect surround votes in O(1) time.

Uses 5 repositories total:
- `slashingProtectionBlockBySlot`: To check block double vote in O(1), and fetch the first block (stream values with limit=1) to assert interchange format condition `block.slot > minBlock.slot`.
- `slashingProtectionAttestationByTarget`: To check attestation double vote in O(1)
- `slashingProtectionMinSpanDistance`: To check surrounding votes in O(1)
- `slashingProtectionMaxSpanDistance`: To check surrounded votes in O(1)
- `slashingProtectionAttestationLowerBound`: To assert the interchange format conditions `att.sourceEpoch >= minSourceEpoch`, `att.targetEpoch > minTargetEpoch`. Computed once on interchange import.

title: Add slashing protection and interchange format
body:
Refactors current slashing protection in the validator client to accommodate the interchange format as defined in https://hackmd.io/@sproul/Bk0Y0qdGD

The slashing protection refactor improves the current implementation by covering all possible surround vote cases. It does so with the min-max-surround algorithm https://github.com/protolambda/eth2-surround#min-max-surround in O(1) time. In total, this slashing protection module uses 5 repositories:
- slashingProtectionBlockBySlot: To check block double vote in O(1), and fetch the first block (stream values with `limit=1`) to assert interchange format condition `block.slot > minBlock.slot`.
- slashingProtectionAttestationByTarget: To check attestation double vote in O(1)
- slashingProtectionMinSpanDistance: To check surrounding votes in O(1)
- slashingProtectionMaxSpanDistance: To check surrounded votes in O(1)
- slashingProtectionAttestationLowerBound: To assert the interchange format conditions `att.sourceEpoch >= minSourceEpoch` and `att.targetEpoch > minTargetEpoch`. Computed once on interchange import.

The core logic for min-max-surround is tested with the same data used in Prysm's implementation. The interchange format is tested with a common set of spec-ed tests from https://github.com/eth2-clients/slashing-protection-interchange-tests 

#### Next steps
- Develop CLI commands to call import / export interchange functions

title: Add internal event emitter
body:
This is a solution to the following problem:
External (non-chain) handlers of `ChainEventEmitter` events can't be guaranteed that the proper side effects (internal to the chain) have been performed, at the time that the external handler is triggered.

This problem has been hinted at in #1655, where a new event is introduced, rather than relying on the existing events.
It's done for the following reasons:
1. the BlockPool is currently not part of the public IBeaconChain interface, so the sync can't retrieve the 'missing ancestor'
2. the sync can't really rely on the BlockPool being properly updated when the "error:block" event is fired/handled

Number 1. can be rectified fairly easily, either with a public method or public member on IBeaconChain
its 2. that this PR deals with.

The problem stems from the fact that multiple event handlers can be run concurrently (in the case that handlers are async / have async steps).
This means that external chain event handlers can be interwoven with internal chain event handlers in a way that exposes external handlers to an inconsistent chain state.

There are several ways to handle the problem, this is an attempt to systematically resolve it.

This PR adds an "internal event emitter" that is used to wire together chain submodules.
The chain's event handlers subscribe to this internal emitter.
These handlers perform various important side effects (eg: updating caches/db) that we want completed before external handers can run.
Once the chain's event handler finishes in its entirety (async function completes), the same event, with the same args is emitted from the public/external event emitter, where downstream consumers can attach event handlers.

title: OneRangeAhead Regular Sync
body:
resolves #1676 

At this time, we need to catch up with ~40000 slots in order to sync to head.

I intended to improve our naive strategy but it was too much change so decided to come up with a new one. Naive was good to start with anyway and we leave it there for backward reference.
+ In term of strategy, the difference is we fetch and process block range at the same time. We do this by fetch one range ahead and buffer it. It's like `Promise.all([fetcher.next(), processor.processUntilComplete())`
+ I separate the fetch to a fetcher - `BlockRangeFetcher` and processor to `BlockRangeProcessor`. The main sync class `ORARegularSync` acts as a controller.
+ It's easier to do unit test for each of them and maintain, I reproduced cases I got in the past in unit tests
+ Performance should be better since we either `fetch` or `process` in naive, now we do both at the same time

I tried syncing a couple of times and felt good about it. Not able to sync up to head (25000 max) bc of different issues:
+ Forkchoice getCanonicalBlockAtSlot()
+ Not enough sync peers
+ Sometimes network req/res still timeout

title: Reorg lodestar options & config handling
body:
### Goals

- Typesafe all options in the CLI. Ensure each arg has an option and that it matches an actual option in Lodestar
- Enable yargs strict options. If the user types `--api.rest.enabled2` the CLI will throw an "Unknown option" error
- Remove variable mutation. Mutations are bad. Mutations make the code really harder to maintain. Mutations must go.
- Deduplicate code
- Remove default exports in Lodestar's options. Properly name each option object and export as named

### Changes

Changes necessary to achieve the goals above

- Disable yargs parser dot-notation. It's a good idea but you get no static Typesafety and it has bugs with the strict options code that make both unsuitable.
- Manually map a doted CLI arg `"api.rest.enabled"` to an IBeaconNodeOptions object, to replace dot-notation. It's not that bad code-wise, and you get static typesafety.
- Refactor the init handler and how other commands use it to initialize things to remove mutation. Use a regular function approach that returns initialized variables for other commands to use.
- Re-do the CLI e2e test to not rely and a setTimeout to guess completed time + stubes. Added a `getLodestarCliTestRunner` utility with which you can run commands directly and await them
```ts
const lodestar = getLodestarCliTestRunner()
const walletNames = await lodestar(`account wallet list --rootDir ${rootDir}`
```
- Re-org testnet settings to reduce code duplication. Since a testnet's config will never change, keep its diff in the src, instead of fetching the config remotely.
- Use a `getBeaconConfig` function to get the config instead of relying on mutations in the init command
- Isolate config and options handling in separate utils. Unit test those.
- Unit test path parsers (getBeaconPaths, getAccountPaths)
- Remove mutation from the path parsers

Others / minor
- Remove the `account validator deposit` command. Fixes https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/1684
- Rename all CLI args to `args`. Previously they were mixed `options` and `args`
- Add `minConnections` option from updated libp2p dependency
- Improve the RecursivePartial type. The previous version caused issues with deeply nested types like network's discv5 options.
- Use synchronous fs methods to interact with small files = simpler code
- Fix init command description

title: Refactor node initialization
body:
This PR refactors the `BeaconChain`,  `BeaconNode`, and `ForkChoice` initialization.

Major changes:
- initialize an anchor state (either from file, db, or eth1)
  - the three different state initializations are refactored into functions, previously living in various chain methods
- `BeaconNode#init` is used to initialize a node from an anchor state
  - it creates all non-external submodules, wired together and started
  - the `BeaconNode` constructor simply attaches preconfigured submodules to the node as properties
- `BeaconChain` now is fully initialized in the constructor, no need for an asynchronous initialization, much simplified
  - chain requires a genesis/anchor state passed in the constructor, used to seed all chain submodules
  - chain no longer includes any Eth1Provider / GenesisBuilder code, its handled ^ when the anchor state is initialized
- `ForkChoice` is now subclassed - moves the fork choice initialization previously living as a chain method into the new constructor
  - this subclass can/will be extended to emit `forkChoice:head` and `forkChoice:reorg` events in a future PR
- as a result of this PR, the node now seems to stop cleanly, no longer hanging

title: Do not pass gossip aggregate and proof attestation to chain
body:
+ Gossip aggregate and proof attestations are not meant to process, they are meant  save to a pool to include in future blocks. According to the p2p spec: 
```
The beacon_aggregate_and_proof topic is used to propagate aggregated attestations (as SignedAggregateAndProofs) to subscribing nodes (typically validators) to be included in future blocks.
```

+ Another reason is a gossip aggregate and proof may not be included in any blocks. If we pass it to forkchoice, we may have different forkchoice head compared to other nodes.

+ I checked Prysm, it just save gossip aggregate and proofs to pool without processing them. Someone can check with Lighthouse to see if they process them or just save.

body:

+ During the big unfinality time of medalla, loading `block` db and persisting to `blockArchive` takes more or less 1h so we need to improve it

+ Implement `getBinary()`, `putBinary()` and `batchPutBinary()` accordingly
+ It's 10 times faster as tested in e2e

title: Implement CachedValidatorsBeaconState
body:
resolves #1789 

## Goal
+ In case of a slow state transition, looping through `validators` inside `TreeBacked` structure takes a significant time
+ Create CachedValidatorsBeaconState that cache a regular `validators` array after the 1st loop, use it in lodestar-state-transition only. Note that when processing epoch, we always have to do the loop to prepare EpochProcess.
+ When update/add a validator, update to both the cache and `TreeBacked<BeaconState>`
+ When loop/read, use the cached `validators` if we have it

## Trade off
+ We have to use `setValidator`, `addValidator`, `getValidator` api in state transition instead of accessing `validators` directly. I guess we can enforce it at compile time using `Omit<BeaconState, "validators">` or something if we want to.

## Performance gain with 100k validators as in Pyrmont/Medalla
+ Process 1st epoch: save 500ms - 600ms
+ From the 2nd epoch, it only takes around 1100ms per epoch (instead of >=2800ms)
+ When we have to process 16 validator exits as in the performance test, the time to process block is reduced from 6000ms to 1400ms
+ See more details in the performance tests of lodestar-beacon-state-transition

## Test
+ Passed spec tests
+ Synced Pyrmont successfully

## Memory
+ When we process a regular block it even does not create a cached validators
+ It short-live in state transition only then released

Although the performance is improved, I'd like to have everyone review to see if we have any potential issues with this approach. Thanks!

title: Add network test vectors
body:
The purpose of this PR is to ensure that our ReqResp code behaves exactly the same from version to version. Current unit tests only assert that the current encoder works with the current decoder, but doesn't guarantee correctness. This PR leverages the fact that our current code has been widely tested and interop-ed so it's treated as correct. I'm adding this now to safely incorporate my upcoming ReqResp code re-org.

Tests are structured resembling the eth2 spec tests, but are generated with our own code. Include three directories
- `network/spec-test/format`: write test vectors to FS, parse FS to test vectors logic
- `network/spec-test/generate`: create test vectors and store to FS. Should be run rarely run, i.e. when the spec changes and we are confident our code interops
- `network/spec-test/run`: read test vectors from FS and run them
- `network/spec-test/vectors`: test vectors

Currently this PR only includes tests for decoding a response given a stream of bytes. I will extend to response encoding, request encoding / decoding and errors if this structure is good with other repo mantainers

title: Speed up epoch transition using persistent vector
body:
resolves #1789, resolves #1878, and resolves #1761

+ Create a CachedValidatorsBeaconState that cache validators using persistent vector (see https://github.com/tuyennhv/persistent-ts/pull/1) and use it everywhere
+ Persistent vector is an immutable data structure, similar to the persistent-merkle-tree we used: it shares a lot of data across beacon state since validators are rarely changed and it has cheap `clone()`
+ Persistent vector loop speed is comparable to regular javascript array loop while it's slow if we loop through `TreeBacked<BeaconState>.validators`
+ When we want to mutate validators inside state, use `setValidator()` and `addValidator()` instead of accessing `validators` directly
+ Average epoch transition time in my local environment for Pyrmont sync was reduced from `3.5s-4.2s` to `1.2s-1.6s`. This should speed up the validator exit process too.
## Testing
+ Pyrmont: synced from slot 0 to head and stay synced for more than 4 hours (tested 2 times)
+ Don't see any memory differences during Pyrmont sync
+ Performance tests

|test|master|this branch|
|----|------|-----------|
|prepareEpochProcessState|1500|100|
|process block of 16 validator exits|6000|200|
|transition - 32 slots|2800|1100|
|transition - 64 slots|5300|2200|
|transition - 128 slots|11000|4300|

## TODO
+ Persistent vector was started from https://github.com/cronokirby/persistent-ts, we should consider having a separate repository for it or just have a separate package like in this PR

title: Network ReqResp modularization
body:
Refactors network reqResp code with the general goals of modularization and better maintainability. The overall logic is not changed with a few exceptions outlined below.

- Do not rely on events to handle reqResp responses. Instead, the Sync registers a `ReqRespHandler` to network's ReqResp instance
  - Allows keeping only the app-level logic in Sync: given a request, yield a response.
  - Error handling is done exclusively in network's ReqResp, any error on any method will return error to the requester and close the stream
```ts
type ReqRespHandler = (
  method: Method, 
  requestBody: RequestBody,
  peerId: PeerId
) => AsyncIterable<ResponseBody>
```
- De-deduplicate ssz-snappy codec logic. Allows to be recycled in requestEncode and responseEncode
  - Current organization allows to easily add another encoding strategy with minimal logic duplication
  - Use `LodestarError` style with rich documented errors
- Abstract response timeout handling in separate function `responseTimeoutsHandler` 
  - RESP_TIMEOUT waits for an entire response_chunk as indicated by the spec, instead of just a raw bytes chunk from libp2p
- Only log in the main response or request handler, other functions either return or throw
  - Reduces the modules that need to be passed around and simplifies flow control
- Document non-obvious code decisions and general function purpose with content from the p2p spec
- For ssz list requests, limits the number of responses collected to the requested amount. Prevents a malicious node from sending us infinite blocks and DOS us.

This branch is currently syncing Pyrmont in `lodestar-cloud-02` with a stable peer count. I has also synced Pyrmont on my local machine without issues.

Happy to jump on a call if more context is needed by a reviewer.

title: Initial sync as state machine
body:
Refactors initial sync with a heavily Lightouse inspired sync.

> TLDR: higher sync speeds - works as a state machine: easier testing, debugging and predictability

Record of successfully completing initial sync on cloud instances

- `lodestar-cloud-01`: Pyrmont on container `lodestar_lodestar_1`: 2 times
- `lodestar-cloud-02`: Mainnet on container `lodestar_lodestar_1`: 3 times

---

The Sync has two integral components:
### `Batch`
Represent a fix range of slots to fetch and process. A batch is a state machine that transitions through multiple status with public methods:
- `AwaitingDownload`: Initial state, or the batch has failed either downloading or processing, but can be requested again.
- `Downloading`: The batch is being downloaded
- `AwaitingProcessing`: The batch has been completely downloaded and is ready for processing
- `Processing`: The batch is being processed.
- `AwaitingValidation`: The batch was successfully processed and is waiting to be validated. It is not sufficient to process a batch successfully to consider it correct. This is because batches could be erroneously empty, or incomplete. Therefore, a batch is considered valid, only if the next sequential batch imports at least a block.

Tracking the status in this way simplifies a lot the logic to concurrently handle and download multiple batches at once. The `AwaitingValidation` also allow to handle infinitely long periods of completely skipped slots without issues.

Batches always start a slot 1 to ease committee forecasting when batch signature verification is ON.
```
 Epoch boundary |                                   |
  ... | 30 | 31 | 32 | 33 | 34 | ... | 61 | 62 | 63 | 64 | 65 |
       Batch 1       |              Batch 2              |  Batch 3
 ```
 
Batches also track the failed attemps which would allow sofisticate peer scoring in upcomming PRs. So far it's used to reduce the chance of re-requesting a batch to a peer with a failed attempt.
 
### `SyncChain`
 
Main driver that handles a map of `Batch`es. It uses an AsyncIterable `batchProcessor` to processes batches to be processed in order and only one at once. All the state necessary to chose the next to be downloaded batch and when syncing is done is derived from the batches. Plus `startEpoch` which tracks the latest validated epoch.
 
It interfaces with the sync manager through 3 methods only
 - `processChainSegment`
 - `downloadBeaconBlocksByRange`
 - `getPeersAndTargetEpoch`: Abstracts the peer handling logic upstream. Allows to sync manager to enforce minPeers even throughout the sync

`SyncChain` instead of `start()` `stop()` exposes a single `sync()` method that resolves when sync. It uses an abort signal for stopping.

`SyncChain` is able to detect that the sync has stalled with a recurring `maybeStuckTimeout`. It will print detailed data to help debugging and try to re-fetch new batches and reprocess pending. It also detects specific invalid internal state combinations and will nuke itself if those happen.

title: Namespace phase0 types
body:
This namespaces ssz types under `config.types.phase0` or `import {phase0} from "@chainsafe/lodestar-types";`
This allows us to always refer unambiguously to a specific version of a type.
It also allows us to add types for future HFs without breaking the 'backward compatibility' of the existing types.

This PR creates `IPhase0Params` and `IPhase0SSZTypes` and integrates them in the params and types libraries in a standard way.

Future HF params are expected to define new params and never update the value of a pre-existing param. `IBeaconParams` will be the union of all HF params.
(eg: `type IBeaconParams = IPhase0Params & IHFParams ....;`)

Future HF ssz types are expected to define new types and possibly update existing types (but only by adding additional fields to those types).
`IBeaconSSZTypes` will have a separate namespace for each HF that allows for unambiguously selecting a type at a specific version.
(eg: `type IBeaconSSZTypes = { phase0: IPhase0SSZTypes; hf: IHFSSZTypes };`)
These same namespaces are exported from the root of the `@chainsafe/lodestar-types` to access the typescript types.
(eg: `import {phase0, hf} from "@chainsafe/lodestar-types";`)

For improved ergonomics, a few tweaks have been made.
Primitive types are also available directly on `IBeaconSSZTypes` and are also exported from the roof of `@chainsafe/lodestar-types`. This list of un-namespaced types may only ever grow to include types that we _know_ will never change, to protect backwards compatibility.

Additionally, phase0 typescript types have been re-exported under phase0 exports in `@chainsafe/lodestar-beacon-state-transition`. This allows importing a single `phase0` object from `@chainsafe/lodestar-beacon-state-transition` to both access phase0 state transition functions AND phase0 typescript types.

title: Wrap errors in Range Sync Chain
body: Range Sync batches have state changing methods `processingSuccess()` and `processingError()`. Only one can be called after processing the batch, if both are called it would result in an error. With the current try / catch pattern, if `processingSuccess()` body throws, `processingError()` will be called too. This PR uses an error handling pattern common in Go and Rust where function calls return a tuple with (err, result). It's very useful here since then we can ensure to only call one of the batch state changing methods with an if.

title: Range sync refactor
body:
## TLDR

Implements Lighthouse's range sync which features:

- Able to go from synced to syncing dynamically depending on current connected peer status
- Resilient against malicious peers feeding a bad chain. Able to detect this case, keep track of the peers, report them and sync from another chain.
- Merges the initial sync + regular sync code.
- Able to sync multiple head chains at once.

#### `RangeSync`

Sync is triggered by adding and removing peers, so it's convenient to follow the logic from `addPeer` https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/03f356b35be94c51985dc1be87c1489da3d54790/packages/lodestar/src/sync/range/range.ts#L105

Key sensitive logic:
- [`updateChains`](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/dapplion%2Frange-sync-rebased/packages/lodestar/src/sync/range/utils/updateChains.ts): How to decide with SyncChain to sync from

----

Fixes https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/1921

title: Refactor gossip code
body:
Refactors gossip code and adds easier support for supporting future HFs

- A few general fork helpers, the `IForkInfo` interface, `config.getForkInfoRecord()`, and `computeForkNameFromForkDigest`
- Remove outer `Gossip` wrapper, all logic is on `Eth2Gossipsub`, a class that extends `Gossipsub`.
- Rework gossip topic typing, add type `GossipTopic` that supports referencing a topic in a friendly way
- Generally, validation functions and gossip event handlers are added on initialization, removed on destruction. (rather than added/removed during subscription/unsubscription)
- Subscription/unsubscription is toggled by starting/stopping the sync gossip handler, attestation collector, and interopSubnetTask
- Generally, `ForkDigest` event handlers can/should be replaced with `IForkName` event handlers.
  - in many cases, the way to handle events is known ahead of time in a per-fork manner
  - fork digest is not immediately useful, rather, its derivative of the fork version/name
  - since `genesisValidatorsRoot` is a constant, we can code in terms of `IForkName` and derive a `ForkDigest` if/when/where its needed
- Adds a few metrics:
![Screenshot from 2021-03-05 18-52-47](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1348242/110189394-902fcf80-7de4-11eb-96b8-4aecb87811e5.png)

title: Refactor peer managment
body:
Group all peer management functionality into a single class PeerManager. Current master segregates the functionality between tasks, network, and sync. PeerManager does:
- Perform handshake on peer connect, notify Sync only when peer is relevant. Ping and status peers every interval
- Mantain a set of peer by discovering + disconnecting according to conditions: targetPeers, minPeers, requested subnets. Groups logic to do so in testable pure functions

All ReqResp logic moved to network/reqResp so it can easily notify the PeerManager on incoming requests.

----

This PR is a spin-off from https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/2111 which is still unclear if it causes more memory and lag issues than master. I will A/B test this PR too to ensure it performs at least as well as master

---

#### `PeerManager`

PeerManager runs an internal `heartbeat` function which is a convenient start to follow its logic https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/03f356b35be94c51985dc1be87c1489da3d54790/packages/lodestar/src/network/peers/peerManager.ts#L119

title: Persist temp states to not lose sync progress
body:
**Motivation**

Currently, we store a state every 1024 epochs. At slow sync speeds of 4 slots / second, that's +2 hours of sync progress lost. Fixes https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/2048

![Screenshot from 2021-03-09 10-24-59](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/35266934/110448708-b6de5680-80c1-11eb-8527-5e56230df655.png)

**Proposed solution**

Store state more frequently, every 32 epochs. Then, after a successful store, keep only the first state every 1024 epochs and delete the rest. In normal conditions, only 0 or 1 states will be deleted. The resulting layout of store states will look like
```
    |         |       |    .
 x-1024*2  x-1024   x-32   x
```

title: beaconBlockByRange handler to work with BlockArchiver
body:
resolves #2127 

Most of the time a `beaconBlocksByRange` handler does not need to deal with BlockArchiver, just in edge case when both run at the same time with an overlapped range 

+ Add new methods to BlockArchive task to know its status: `getArchivingStatus()` which returns a last finalized slot and a finalizing slot (`null` if not running); and `waitUntilComplete()` to wait for a `run()` to be done
+ if `beaconBlocksByRange` handler found that `BlockArchiver` is running with an overlapped range, it'd wait for BlockArchiver to finish first before querying database (a `BlockArchiver.run` takes less than 300ms so I hope it's ok)

author: twoeths

title: Remove abortable source wrapper from response source
body:
There was a memory leak stemming from using `abortable-iterator` and neither fully draining the iterator nor aborting it.
`abortable-iterator` attaches an abort signal listener and only removes the listener after:
- the iterator is `{done: true}` OR
- the iterator is aborted

In our case, `collectResponses` `break`s out of the iterator after `maxResponses` # of iterations.
So every request was leaking a listener.


For now, remove the abortable source wrapper until we can figure out a better solution.

- Use abort interators and signals only if necessary

this PR fixes some extra errors caused by a miss-understanding of the implications in upstream communication of the `for .. of` iterator protocol. It adds more clarifying comments to justify the changes and aid maintainability.

title: Run postStateTransition function in a separate context
body: resolves #2179 + Running the `ChainEvent.block` (and others) async handlers in the same Promise of `stateTransition` sometimes cause a lot of states being retained in memory + The fix is to use `setImmediate` to run `postStateTransition` in a separate context. `setImmediate` is called before the next event loop so we have the event processed before we finish `runStateTransition` (thanks to `await sleep(0)` at the end of `runStatetransition`). Reference: https://nodejs.org/en/docs/guides/event-loop-timers-and-nexttick/#setimmediate-vs-settimeout ## Test with Pyrmont + master retains 615 MB of BeaconStateContext instances in memory (note: the dash `-` in `Distance` column means that the instance stays in memory forever) + this branch retains 77MB of BeaconStateContext instances in memory - almost no dash `-` in `Distance` column

title: Enable no-unsafe eslint rules
body:
Eslint v7 has 4 new rules very useful to guard against using `any` types inadvertently.

- Disallows assigning any to variables and properties ([no-unsafe-assignment](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/no-unsafe-assignment.md))
- Disallows calling an any type value ([no-unsafe-call](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/no-unsafe-call.md))
- Disallows member access on any typed variables ([no-unsafe-member-access](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/no-unsafe-member-access.md))
- Disallows returning any from a function ([no-unsafe-return](https://github.com/typescript-eslint/typescript-eslint/blob/master/packages/eslint-plugin/docs/rules/no-unsafe-return.md))

The purpose of this PR is gauge interest by Lodestar maintainers before actually working on the issues they raise. I've counted 800 lint errors of no-unsafe-* rules, mostly in tests accessing un-typed stubs

title: Gossip validation - log error metadata instead on logContext
body:
Follow up of https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/2199

Logging so much data about the incoming attestations and aggregates is not actionable. As a consumer of logs the most useful information is the error itself, with its attached metadata. For example for `FUTURE_SLOT` you'll get 
```
attestationSlot: Slot; latestPermissibleSlot: Slot;
```
which is more actionable that the hashTreeRoot of the aggregate. Also, computing the hashTreeRoot of attestations and aggregates is a non-trivial task that currently is done always, even when running in "production" mode, with logLevel >= info.

This PR changes from logging the entire error to only the `type` metadata, ommitting the unnecessary stack trace

title: Increase sim test stability
body:
**Motivation**

Multi-thread sim tests are very unstable due to wrong assumptions in our sync module. It is not able to handle nicely the genesis situation that occurs in precisely that sim test, causing nodes to fork and not reach justification together.

**Description**

This PR introduces two main changes:
- Adds a somewhat "dirty" hack to mark the sync as completed and start gossip if epoch = 0, and node has peers. This should be properly fixed eventually with https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/2111. Do you see any dangers with this condition? What other condition or event could we listen for to find genesis more reliably?
- Disable MDNS for all the sim tests and manually connect the nodes with each other. In the multi-thread test, p2p ports and peerIds are pre-computed and sent as worker data to all threads. Then nodes wait a bit and connect to each other. If the timing is correct nodes should be ready to receive inbound connections by the time they try to connect.

Minor issues:
- Added process.exit(1) if worker start sequence fails. Currently it would just throw and unhandled rejection and do nothing.
- Added a condition in network to skip trying to connect to subnet peers if discv5 is not available
https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/76da10ac8a485b3cc8f1f444a6ed0f873dd90b88/packages/lodestar/src/network/network.ts#L244-L245

This PR is a pre-requisite to merge https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/2142
