title: feat: count signed repeat proposals as proposer equivocations
body:
`should_apply_proposer_boost` and `is_proposer_equivocation` read proposer equivocations from `store.blocks`, so only valid blocks count. Nodes have to bound how many repeat proposals they fully validate, we import at most one alternate over gossip (#9805, #9795), and with that bound the view depends on arrival order. Given blocks A, B, C from one proposer with C invalid, nodes that see A and B first record the equivocation while nodes that see A and C first never learn that B exists, so the two groups disagree on the boost of the next block and on the equivocation reorg.

Counting signed blocks instead removes that. Two signature checks per proposer and slot are all a node ever does, and since siblings arrive in order the first two signed roots are always the most timely ones, so a two-root record per proposer and slot answers `should_apply_proposer_boost` exactly. Every effect of a junk signed sibling lands on the attacker's own slot, the next proposer sees the same early sibling as the attesters and reorgs a weak head as `get_proposer_head` already asks it to.

- fork choice keeps a record of signed block roots per slot and proposer with their PTC timeliness, capped at the first two, pruned below the finalized epoch
- `onBlock` records imported blocks, the new `onSignedBlockHeader` records blocks that were seen with a valid proposer signature but not imported
- `hasEquivocatingBlock` reads that record instead of scanning the proto array
- the gossip handler records every block whose proposer signature was verified, imported or not, with `isPtcTimely` evaluated at arrival

This deviates from the current spec text, which is why it is a draft. The spec change is a store field of signed sibling roots and their timeliness fed by a handler taking a signature-valid header, like `on_attester_slashing`, with the two fork choice functions reading it and the p2p spec noting that ignored repeat proposals feed it. Supersedes #10070.
author: nflaig

title: fix: prune cache entries of repeat proposals that are not imported
body:
Every block that reaches gossip validation seeds a block input, and on gloas a payload envelope input, before the checks run, and IGNORE keeps those entries until finalization or size pruning. Since #9805 only the first signature-verified repeat proposal of a proposer is imported, so any further one holds its full block in memory for nothing, and a proposer can send as many of those as it likes. This drops the entries of a repeat proposal that is not imported, sync re-downloads the block if a child or an attestation ever references it. The comment on the import gate now says what it actually is, the two-root cap in the seen cache is what bounds full imports over gossip to one alternate.

The dropped entry is removed with the block input cache's single-entry `remove` rather than `prune`, which follows the parent root and evicts every cached ancestor. A repeat proposal past the second one never had its signature verified, so with `prune` any peer could name a cached block as parent and evict it together with its downloaded data. The gossip REJECT path had the same walk for blocks that fail signature or proposer checks and is switched to `remove` as well.

The payload envelope input cache named its single-entry eviction `prune` too, which reads as if it walked ancestors like the block input cache's. It is renamed to `remove`, with its metric reason label, and `pruneBelowParent` stays the ancestor variant.

title: fix: verify the proposer signature before retaining unknown parent gossip blocks
body:
Gossip block validation checks the proposer signature only after the parent is known, and the handler caches the block and hands it to unknown parent sync on `PARENT_BLOCK_UNKNOWN`. A peer without any validator key can therefore make the node decode, hash, cache and sync-fetch arbitrary current-slot blocks with an unknown parent, at up to 10 MiB per message and with no penalty since the result is an IGNORE. This is the precondition behind ethereum-bounty/lodestar#22 and ethereum-bounty/lodestar#23.

- verify the proposer index against the pubkey registry and the proposer signature before the parent lookup, `verifyBlockProposerSignature` works without a state and the signing root reuses the cached block root, so this reorders existing work rather than adding any
- count a retained unknown parent block as its proposer's proposal for the slot, a second block from the same proposer is a `REPEAT_PROPOSAL` with the equivocation recorded instead of another retained block, and a repeat proposal whose parent is unknown is not imported and is pruned from the caches
- the sending peer gets the `Fatal` penalty the gossip validator applies to `PROPOSAL_SIGNATURE_INVALID` since #10059, an honest peer never forwards such a block, so a spamming peer is banned on the first one

A peer with no validator key now gets every block rejected and nothing retained. A peer with validator keys retains at most one block per key per slot and hands us slashable evidence with the second. The decode and hash cost of a message before it is rejected is unchanged and is the subject of a follow-up that bounds in-flight block gossip work per peer.

Builds on #10083.

title: feat: deduplicate finalized Gloas payload bodies
body:
**Motivation**

Reduce retained beacon-node disk usage by relying on the EL for finalized Gloas payload bodies. Transactions, withdrawals, and block access lists otherwise remain duplicated in LevelDB.

**Description**

- Enable `--chain.dedupePayloads` by default. Once payload inclusion is finalized and execution is validated, atomically replace the full hot envelope with compact metadata in a new archive bucket.
- Reconstruct envelopes through Engine API payload-body V2 requests by finalized execution block number, checking the original payload SSZ root before serving REST JSON/SSZ or ReqResp responses.
- Keep envelope metadata and execution requests local, so parent execution-request reads and column availability checks do not depend on the EL. Keep full and compact repositories separately typed.
- Preserve existing full archives and retain full envelopes when deduplication is disabled or execution validation is pending. Disabling the flag affects future archival writes; existing archives are not rewritten.

The EL must retain transactions, withdrawals, and block access lists for the history the beacon node serves. Scope is Gloas payload envelopes; pre-Gloas block storage is unchanged.

Related to #5671.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Code, tests, and this PR description were written primarily by OpenAI Codex, with human design direction and review.
author: wemeetagain

title: feat: de-duplicate execution payload from archived Gloas envelopes
body:
**Motivation**

Post-Gloas, every finalized `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` in the archive carries the full execution payload the EL already stores: transactions (~194 KB/block at current mainnet sizes), withdrawals and the block access list (~70 KiB), well over 500 GB/year of redundant CL disk. Closes #5671 for the Gloas scope; pre-Gloas blocks are unchanged.

Also relates to #9282: this covers the finalized archive; hot-db dedup and the interop test are follow-ups.

**Description**

- New `SignedExecutionPayloadHeaderEnvelope` in `@lodestar/types` (gloas): the payload replaced by its header, `transactions`, `withdrawals` and `blockAccessList` swapped for their roots at the same field positions, so it hashes identically to the full envelope and the builder signature verifies against the stored entry. ~1 KB per envelope, Lodestar-internal, never on the wire.
- `--chain.dedupePayloads` (default `true`): hot→cold migration archives execution-valid envelopes as header envelopes; still-optimistic ones, and everything with the flag off, are archived in full as bytes. Both share one bucket: full envelopes are stored as their hot bytes untouched, header envelopes behind a `0x00` prefix byte (a full envelope always starts with `0x64`, its `message` offset), so the flag can be toggled without resync and entries archived before this change stay readable.
- Reads rebuild header entries from `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV2` (new, Amsterdam), 32 hashes per call, each body verified against its stored root with the mismatching field reported, byte-identical to what was archived. `getParentExecutionRequests` reads the header entry directly, no EL call.
- By-range: the spec inherits BeaconBlocksByRange v2 semantics (consecutive, MAY be short), so the stream ends at the first entry the EL cannot serve (unknown hash, pruned BAL (null or zero-length), body root mismatch, or an EL failure) and answers `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` if nothing was served. By-root allows omission, so a mismatched envelope is left out and the rest served. REST keeps 500 on mismatch. EL down → `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` / 503. Misses are logged at debug; they are peer-triggered.
- No age floor: every header entry is attempted, the EL's BAL retention is the real limit (spec: MUST serve `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS`, MAY serve more). Deliberately the opposite of Teku's trim.
- Metrics: `beacon_payload_envelope_reconstruction_envelopes_total{result=ok|unavailable|mismatch}`, `…_mismatch_total{field}` and `…_engine_errors_total` (failed `engine_getPayloadBodiesByHashV2` round-trips), incremented in the single reconstruction path shared by by-range, by-root and REST. The `unavailable`/`ok` ratio measures how far past the EL's BAL retention peers are requesting.

**Known limitations**

- With an EL that prunes BALs at the EIP-7928 floor (~16 days), older range requests get `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. Spec-correct on our side; closing the gap between EL retention and the CL's `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` serving requirement is ethereum/EIPs#12347.
- Envelopes archived in full while the EL was still syncing are never converted later.
- The header envelope types are Gloas-specific; needs fork-aware types once EIP-8205's per-fork envelope lands. `headerEnvelope.test.ts` pins the field layout per fork so this fails loudly.

**Sizing**

| full envelope | header envelope | reduction | saved / yr |
| ------------- | --------------- | --------- | ---------- |
| ~267 KB       | ~1 KB           | >99%      | ~690 GB    |

**Testing**

`headerEnvelope.test.ts`, `envelopeMigration.test.ts`, `execution.test.ts` and `executionPayloadEnvelopes.test.ts` (real LevelDB, mocked EL): root equality with the full envelope, field layout per fork, round-trip, per-field mismatch, migration header/full/optimistic, byte-identity, batching, end-at-first-unservable, transient EL error, getter vs p2p mismatch behaviour, and the peer-facing handler mapping (short response after a served envelope, `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` on an unservable first entry or EL outage, by-root omitting a mismatched envelope while serving the rest).

**Motivation**

title: fix: bind IPv6 by default only if the host has a global IPv6 address
body:
## Motivation

A fresh v1.48.0 beacon node on sepolia or hoodi that runs in a Docker container without an IPv6 route finds zero peers. Discovery never sends a UDP packet.

`parseListenArgs` binds `::` when the user sets neither `--listenAddress` nor `--listenAddress6`. With an IPv6 socket bound, `@chainsafe/discv5` contacts every dual-stack ENR over IPv6 and does not fall back to IPv4 (`getSocketAddressMultiaddrOnENR`, same rule as sigp/discv5 `DualStack`). In a container without IPv6 connectivity every send to those peers fails.

Until v1.47.0 the built-in sepolia and hoodi bootnode lists contained IPv4-only EF bootnodes, which masked this. #10049 replaced them with the NodeOps fleet, which is dual-stack. The only IPv4-only entry left (a Teku node) does not answer. The v1.48.0 lists therefore contain no bootnode a default-configured IPv4-only container can reach. Mainnet still has IPv4-only bootnodes and is not affected.

Verified on a v4-only Docker host on sepolia with the fleet ENRs as `--bootnodes`:

| image | flags | result after 90s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| v1.48.0 | default | 0 peers, 0 ENRs decoded, 0 UDP packets sent |
| v1.48.0 | `--listenAddress 0.0.0.0` | syncing, hundreds of ENRs discovered |
| v1.48.0 | `--bootnodes <IPv4-only EF ENR>` | syncing |
| v1.47.0 | default | syncing (built-in IPv4-only EF bootnodes) |

## Description

Bind IPv6 by default only if the host has a global unicast IPv6 address. `hasGlobalIPv6Address` reads `os.networkInterfaces()` and accepts only addresses inside the IANA global unicast block `2000::/3`, minus the special-purpose prefixes allocated inside it that the IANA registry marks not globally reachable (IETF protocol assignments including Teredo, 6to4, documentation, SRv6 SIDs), through two `net.BlockList`s. Everything else (loopback, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, unique-local, link-local, site-local) falls outside `2000::/3`. An explicit `--listenAddress6` still forces IPv6 on. An explicit `--listenAddress` still turns the IPv6 default off, as before.

`parseListenArgs` takes the detection result as a second parameter so tests stay independent of the test host. Adds unit tests, updates the `--listenAddress6` description and the networking docs.

Validated with an image built from this branch on the same IPv4-only Docker host: default flags bind IPv4 only (`bindAddr4=/ip4/0.0.0.0/udp/...`, no `bindAddr6`) and discover peers on sepolia and hoodi; `--listenAddress6 ::` still binds IPv6 as before.

Lodestar warns at startup when it skips the IPv6 default for this reason. A persisted ENR loses its `ip6`/`udp6`/`tcp6`/`quic6` fields when no IPv6 listener is configured and no `--enr.*6` flag is given, so peers stop dialing a dead IPv6 endpoint and the beacon handler's `enrUpdate` gate is no longer blocked by a stale `ip6`.

The library-side fix, IPv4-first selection and fast failure on send errors in `@chainsafe/discv5`, is ChainSafe/discv5#341.

title: fix: prune execution payload envelopes with `chain.pruneHistory`
body: `--chain.pruneHistory` deletes finalized blocks older than `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` and archived states before the finalized epoch, but it never touches the execution payload envelope archive. On gloas the full `SignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` of every finalized block stays on disk forever, and since the envelope carries the transactions and the block access list it is the larger part of what the flag is meant to remove. This prunes the envelope archive with the same slot cutoff as the block archive and adds a unit test covering both archives.
author: nflaig

title: fix: prune archived states before the finalized epoch with `chain.pruneHistory`
body: `--chain.pruneHistory` is documented to delete all archived states before the finalized epoch, but the cutoff passed to the state archive is the finalized epoch number while the archive is keyed by slot, so it only ever removed states whose slot is below the finalized epoch number, the first 1/32 of the chain. Since #7427 the states kept by the frequency archive strategy, one per 1024 epochs, have accumulated regardless of the flag. This uses the finalized epoch's start slot as the cutoff, capped at the latest archived state so the anchor state reloaded on restart is never deleted, since state archiving can trail finalization by up to 32 epochs. Adds tests for both cases.

buildoor still compares the url verbatim, so the builder-dev kurtosis setup fails auth until it follows the spec change.

title: feat(api): carry forkchoice hashes on post-gloas payload_attributes events
body:
## Motivation

Post-Gloas the builder issues its own `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` to start a payload build, so it needs the safe and finalized execution block hashes the beacon node would use, not only the head. The standard `payload_attributes` event only carries the parent block hash, and the builder has no good way to derive the other two itself since it isn't running fork choice. Part of the builder sidecar work; the spec-side discussion is ethereum/beacon-APIs#638.

## Description

- `payload_attributes` events emitted post-Gloas carry two optional top-level fields, `safe_block_hash` and `finalized_block_hash`, next to the standard `version` and `data`. They come from the same fork choice lookups (`getSafeExecutionBlockHash` / `getFinalizedExecutionBlockHash`) the beacon node uses for its own `forkchoiceUpdated`, so the builder sees exactly what the node would send.
- The client parses the fields back when present and leaves them out otherwise, so events from beacon nodes that don't send them still parse.
- Pre-Gloas the event shape is unchanged.

I've kept the fields out of the SSZ `SSEPayloadAttributes` container on purpose: required container fields would break parsing of events from other clients, and the shape isn't settled upstream yet. This mirrors what @nflaig has on his builder branch. If beacon-APIs#638 lands with the fields inside `data`, I'll follow it up here.

## Steps to test or reproduce

- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/api test:unit` – new `eventSerdes.test.ts` covers the round trip with and without the hashes, and parsing a post-Gloas event that doesn't carry them.
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/beacon-node test:unit -- prepareNextSlot` – new Gloas case asserts the emitted event carries the same safe and finalized hashes the node passes to `notifyForkchoiceUpdate`.
- On a Gloas devnet node with `--emitPayloadAttributes`, subscribe to `/eth/v1/events?topics=payload_attributes`; post-fork events include `safe_block_hash` and `finalized_block_hash`.

title: fix: delete block archive index entries when pruning history
body:
`--chain.pruneHistory` removes archived blocks by slot, but the block archive's root and parent root indexes are only cleaned up by the value based `remove` paths, so every pruned block leaves its two index keys behind, about 80 bytes per block, and root lookups for pruned blocks resolve to a slot that no longer has a value. This adds a range delete to the block archive that removes the value, slot, root and parent root entries together. The parent root of each block is the root of the previous archived block, read from the slot index before it is deleted, so only the first block of the range and any block following an unindexed one have their bytes read. The parent root entry keyed by the last pruned block points at the first kept block and is left in place. The pruned slot ranges are now included in the debug log.

The state archive is left alone, its root index has not been written since states are archived with `putBinary` (#6504), so there is nothing to clean up there. Index entries left behind by pruning runs before this change are not swept, the fix only guarantees that pruning leaves nothing behind from now on.
author: nflaig

title: test: raise regression threshold for high-variance noise sendData benchmarks
body:
## Motivation

The `network / noise / sendData` benchmarks (`send data - 1000 {N}B messages`) keep firing false **Performance Alert** regressions on unrelated commits. A recent example flagged the three largest payloads with no send-path change:

| Benchmark | Current | Previous | Ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| send data - 1000 4096B messages | 132.58 ms/op | 22.325 ms/op | 5.94 |
| send data - 1000 16384B messages | 453.91 ms/op | 63.498 ms/op | 7.15 |
| send data - 1000 65536B messages | 1.9031 s/op | 275.51 ms/op | 6.91 |

## Root cause

Each run encrypts and streams 1000 messages, allocating up to ~64MB of short-lived buffers for the 65536B case. On the shared benchmark runner the measured time is dominated by **GC pauses and event-loop scheduling**, not the noise send path — so the large sizes swing ~6-7x run-to-run while the small (low-allocation) sizes stay stable. The rolling per-commit baseline amplifies this: one noisy run becomes the baseline and poisons the comparison for the next commit.

This is the same failure mode fixed for the data-availability benchmarks in #10074, and the observed swing (4-8x, bounded) matches the profile that PR gated with `threshold: 10` (as opposed to the unbounded ~250x KZG outliers it left `noThreshold`).

## Change

Set `threshold: 10` on the noise sendData benchmark. Normal shared-runner variance now passes, while a genuine >10x send-path regression still fails CI. The numbers are still measured and posted to the comparison comment as before — only the alert threshold changes.

If 10x proves insufficient (a lucky-fast baseline meeting an unlucky-slow current can stack multiplicatively), the escalation is `noThreshold` (report-only), matching the blob-reconstruction benches in #10074.

title: fix: index archived states by root again
body:
The state archive keeps a root to slot index that `getStateByStateRoot` falls back to for archived states, so every state endpoint called with a root as `state_id` depends on it. The index is only written by `put`, and since #6504 states are archived with `putBinary`, which stores the value only, so no state archived since March 2024 can be found by root.

- `putBinaryWithRoot` stores the state bytes and the index entry in one batch, `put` delegates to it
- the frequency strategy passes the state root in both branches. A state archived from memory uses its own cached root. A state archived from persisted bytes has no root at hand, so it is taken from the head state's state roots history, which holds the root of the state at every slot of the last `SLOTS_PER_HISTORICAL_ROOT` slots. A finalized slot further behind the head than that, over a day without finality, is archived without an index entry and logged
- the anchor state written on startup is indexed with its own root

Draft to see how much the fix takes, the alternative is to remove the index and the `getBinaryByRoot` path with it. States archived before this change stay without an index entry.

title: feat: reduce `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` for gloas
body:
`MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` (33024 epochs, ~5 months) is the max weak subjectivity period for a large validator set (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2131). EIP-8061 changes the churn limits in gloas which roughly halves the weak subjectivity period, so `compute_min_epochs_for_block_requests()` has to follow. With `delta = 2/3 * exit + 1/3 * activation + consolidation` and the activation churn capped, the window becomes 14299 epochs (~2 months) on mainnet.

- add `config.getMinEpochsForBlockRequests(epoch)`, `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` pre-gloas and `MIN_VALIDATOR_WITHDRAWABILITY_DELAY + 3 * Qe * Qc // (2 * (2 * Qc + 3 * Qe))` from gloas on (`Qe = CHURN_LIMIT_QUOTIENT_GLOAS`, `Qc = CONSOLIDATION_CHURN_LIMIT_QUOTIENT`)
- use it for the `--chain.pruneHistory` cutoff of blocks and envelopes and the `BeaconBlocksByHead` lower bound
- limit the blocks pruned per run on a running node to 4096 slots. The shorter window would otherwise prune ~18.7k epochs at once in the first finalization after the fork, and the same happens today when finality resumes after a long period of non-finality. The prune on startup is not limited

Unfinalized blocks are still never pruned.

Draft until https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5680 is merged.

title: refactor: align gloas progressive list limits with the spec
body:
Adopts ethereum/consensus-specs#5642, which moves every progressive list bound from runtime checks onto the type declarations, `LIMIT = <constant>` where a consensus rule exists and `LIMIT = None` where none does, and drops the type-specific size presets since the p2p bounds derive from the types. Lodestar already enforces limits at decode since #10042 and derives its bounds from the types since #10053, so this aligns our declarations, presets and spec test harness with what the spec will ship. Meant to merge together with the spec test bump to a release that includes it.

- drop the limits on `Validators`, `Balances`, `EpochParticipation`, `InactivityScores`, `PendingDeposits`, `PendingPartialWithdrawals` and `PendingConsolidations`, the spec declares them unbounded and they only appear in `BeaconState`, which is never decoded from a peer, so a bound there protects nothing
- remove `MAX_SIGNED_AGGREGATE_AND_PROOF_SIZE`, `MAX_ATTESTER_SLASHING_SIZE`, `MAX_SIGNED_EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_BID_SIZE` and `MAX_SIGNED_EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_BID_SIZE_HEZE` from the presets, they only backed test expectations and the gossipsub IDONTWANT threshold, which now reads `SignedAggregateAndProof.maxSize` directly (same value), the tests assert the literal byte counts instead
- rename `BlobKzgCommitments` and `BlsToExecutionChanges` to the spec casing so the ssz_static handlers resolve without a name mapping
- support the proposed ssz_static `ssz_limit` suite: every bounded progressive list type becomes a handler with an `at_limit` case in the standard format and an `over_limit` case that must fail to deserialize, and every container holding such a list gets the same pair per field, each case declares its validity in `meta.yaml` and the runner branches on that, both the at-limit and the over-limit bytes are decoded with the type as declared since the uint replacement clone drops the limits, `CellsBitList` is skipped with the other partial data column types, verified locally against vectors generated from ethereum/consensus-specs#5642 with the generator change, 203 cases per preset, and setting the `Attestations` limit one too low or the `Withdrawals` limit one too high fails exactly the standalone and container field cases of those lists
- drop the `shouldErrorOnInput` handling from the sanity and operations runners and the option from `spec-test-util`, the spec no longer ships vectors that fail to decode, remove the two deleted `verify_*` functions from the specrefs and clear the remote preset exclusions from the params sync test

`Transactions` and `Transaction` keep their existing bounds, the spec side for those is being discussed separately. No wire behavior changes, every gossip and req/resp bound stays the same.

Red by design until the spec test pin moves: the 26 pinned gloas and heze `invalid_too_many_*` and `invalid_old_style_deposit_rejected` sanity and operations vectors that only decoded through the dropped handling, the params sync test and the constants exposure e2e test since v1.7.0-beta.0 still ships the removed presets, and the specrefs check for the two removed functions. Everything else passes on this head.

title: chore: update ethspecify mappings
body:
`ethspecify check` only verifies that a search string exists, so stale exceptions and mappings that point at the wrong code go unnoticed. This audits all specrefs against the pinned pyspec and the source, exceptions go from 330 to 101.

- map fast confirmation (#8837), it was still excepted as not implemented

- map implemented gloas state transition, fork choice, validator and builder items, and the gloas light client items
- map pre-gloas helpers that exist inline or under a different name (`compute_fork_version`, withdrawals helpers, phase0 reward deltas, sync committee helpers, `*_gindex_at_slot`) and the matching types and constants
- remove 9 entries whose spec text is identical to the previous fork and the stale `PartialDataColumnHeader#gloas` exception
- fix wrong targets: `is_data_available#gloas`, `get_signed_proposer_preferences#gloas`, `upgrade_lc_bootstrap_to_{capella,deneb,electra}`
- move `CustodyColumnBits#gloas` to exceptions, the previous target is a column index lookup and custody columns are not sent to the EL
- add second sources where the logic is split, e.g. `get_head`, `compute_ptc`, `get_attestation_participation_flag_indices#deneb`

Remaining exceptions have no counterpart: heze inclusion lists, partial data columns, removed merge transition and eth1 voting helpers, spec tree walks that proto-array replaces, `Seen`, `LatestMessage` and a few trivial accessors.

title: fix: replace latest messages by slot from gloas
body:
From gloas `LatestMessage` tracks the attestation slot and [`update_latest_messages`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#modified-update_latest_messages) replaces a vote when `slot > store.latest_messages[i].slot`, while we kept comparing epochs as the pre-gloas spec does. The two only differ for a validator with two attestations in the same epoch, which is a slashable double vote that can only reach fork choice through a block since gossip already drops the second one. The spec keeps the vote from the later slot regardless of arrival order, we kept whichever was processed first, so until the attester slashing is processed our weights could differ from other clients.

This compares slots for attestations from gloas onwards and keeps the epoch comparison before it, see the discussion in https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/8739#discussion_r2861304520.
author: nflaig

title: fix: count block payload attestations for all PTC positions of the attester
body:
`compute_ptc` samples by balance, so a validator can hold several PTC positions, and [`notify_ptc_messages`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#new-notify_ptc_messages) resolves the aggregation bits of a block's payload attestation to validator indices and then applies the vote to every position each of them holds. We passed the set bit positions straight to fork choice instead.

This only differs for an aggregate that has some but not all bits of a multi-seat validator set, which is still a valid block since the indexed attestation is `[validator]` with a single signature. Honest proposers do not produce that, our pool, Prysm and Lighthouse all set every position of a validator, and votes received over gossip already count for all positions. So it takes a crafted block and only affects votes the node has not seen on gossip, in which case we counted fewer PTC votes than the spec.

This takes the PTC of the attested slot from the post state and votes on all positions held by the attesters, so the block path matches the gossip path and the spec.
author: nflaig

title: fix: use the builder balance from state in the builders sweep
body:
[`get_builders_sweep_withdrawals`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md#new-get_builders_sweep_withdrawals) withdraws `builder.balance` as it is in the state, the balance after prior withdrawals is only tracked for validators. We applied the validator pattern to builders too and swept the balance net of the builder's pending withdrawals emitted earlier in the same call, so a withdrawable builder with a pending withdrawal `X` would get `[X, B - X]` instead of the spec's `[X, B]`.

This is not reachable on a valid chain, a builder can only exit with no pending balance to withdraw and cannot bid afterwards, so it has no pending withdrawals left by the time it is swept. The change just removes the difference to the spec and the builder balance map that is no longer needed.
author: nflaig

title: fix: match payload status variants of the same root in `isDescendant()`
body:
In gloas [`is_ancestor`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/gloas/fork-choice.md#modified-is_ancestor) a `PENDING` ancestor matches every payload status variant of the same block, and the doc comment of `ProtoArray.isDescendant()` says the same. The ancestor walk starts at the parent block though, so for the same root it only returned `true` when both statuses were equal and a `PENDING` ancestor never matched its own `EMPTY` / `FULL` variants.

No caller hits this today, `processBlocks` passes an `EMPTY` ancestor, fast confirmation passes the default variant for both roots and `getViableHeads()` worked around it with a same-root short-circuit.

- compare variants of the same root directly, a `PENDING` ancestor matches all variants that exist
- drop the same-root short-circuit in `getViableHeads()` that is no longer needed

`getViableHeads()` is only exercised by the fork choice compliance tests, the gloas ones pass with the short-circuit removed.
author: nflaig

title: fix: import attestations of all blocks into fork choice
body:
The current or previous epoch check in [`validate_on_attestation`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.0/specs/phase0/fork-choice.md#validate_on_attestation) only applies to attestations from gossip, attestations from blocks are exempt (`is_from_block`, since https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/2727) and latest messages never expire. We applied the window to block attestations too and only passed them to fork choice if the block and the target were within one epoch of the clock. A node that syncs or restarts, or that receives blocks more than an epoch late, ended up without the votes included in those blocks, which matters for the last vote of offline validators and for branches revealed late during non-finality, where our weights could differ from clients that follow the spec (e.g. Lighthouse).

- pass the attestations of every imported block to fork choice as from block, finalized range sync still skips them via `AttestationImportOpt.Skip`
- keep the recency window for `seenAggregatedAttestations`, `seenBlockAttesters` and the validator monitor, which only track recent epochs
- log fork choice attestation errors of old blocks at debug, they can attest to blocks that are no longer in fork choice

The sync cost should be small but I have not measured it. Indexed attestations are already computed for every block to verify signatures, the window only affected head sync, unknown block sync and late gossip blocks, and what is added per block is the latest message update per attester.

`importsBlockAttestations()` is renamed to `isRecentBlock()` since it no longer decides that. The orphaned payload skip in `processBlocks` that is keyed on it is left unchanged, its reason (no attestation weight for old blocks) only holds for finalized sync now and can be revisited separately.
author: nflaig

title: fix: keep idle event streams alive
body:
The events API only writes to the response when an event is emitted, and the response headers are sent with the first write. A topic that emits rarely runs into the idle timeout of whatever sits on the other end, commonly 60 seconds.

- behind nginx the request for such a topic fails with `504 upstream timed out while reading response header from upstream`, on the glamsterdam-devnet-8 nodes a `chain_reorg` subscriber loops on this ~1200 times a day per node
- buildoor reconnects an event stream after 60 seconds without any bytes, events are not replayed, so everything emitted until it has reconnected is lost. `proposer_preferences` emits nothing between the burst at the start of an epoch and the preferences our validator client submits 8 slots ahead of a proposal, and as 60 seconds is exactly 5 slots the stream is cut in the same moment such a slot aligned submission arrives. buildoor then answers the bid request with `400 no proposer preferences cached for slot`, this happened on ~7% of my proposals and only with the buildoor instances backed by Lodestar, all 6 cases within its log retention have the idle reconnect in the same second as the submission

This sends the response headers right away and writes a comment line every 15 seconds, the interval suggested by the [specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#authoring-notes), comment lines are ignored by clients. Lighthouse and Grandine send a comment every 15 seconds, Prysm every 12 and Teku every 30.

title: refactor: make slot timing fork-aware to prepare for slot duration changes
body:
Prepares slot timing for EIP-8198 quick slots, extracted from #9933. Slot durations and deadlines go through fork config, and clocks use computed slot boundaries.

Timers use the fork of the slot they run in, including preparation, proposer-duty lookahead, payload polling, reconstruction, validator-monitor thresholds, and notifier logging. Regression tests cover shorter and longer slot durations across fork boundaries.

All forks still return `SLOT_DURATION_MS`; actual duration changes remain in #9933. On non-12-second networks, block-production timeouts and cutoffs, the reprocessing guard, and light-client rate-limit windows now scale with slot duration.

title: test: fail gossip spec tests on unexpected errors
body:
**Motivation**

The gossip spec runner maps raw `TypeError` and `RangeError` to `REJECT`, while production returns `IGNORE`. This can make tests expecting rejection pass for the wrong reason.

**Description**

Remove the special case so unexpected errors fail the test. Only `GossipActionError` determines the gossip result.

**Validation**

Lint and beacon-node type checks pass. Direct runner checks with injected `TypeError` and `RangeError` fail before the fix and pass after it.

The networking suite is currently skipped. Calling the runner directly, nine out-of-range cases pass before and after; one voluntary-exit case hits the same existing anchor-state fixture error.
author: nflaig

title: fix: reject pre-Gloas payload attestations on gossip
body:
**Motivation**

At the Gloas boundary, a pre-fork payload attestation within the gossip clock disparity throws a plain error and gets mapped to IGNORE.

**Description**

Reject pre-Gloas slots before the clock check and all lookups. This takes priority over the slot-window IGNORE since pre-fork slots are invalid regardless of clock skew.

Pending the spec change in `ethereum/consensus-specs#5652`.
author: nflaig

title: fix: harden validator block signing
body:
Proposal work from adjacent duty slots can overlap when an earlier block production request remains pending, per-slot duty deduplication does not serialize this work. A beacon node could answer the request for slot `S+1` with a block for slot `S`, and two checks for the same key running at the same time could both pass the double proposal check before either block is recorded, since `checkAndInsertBlockProposal` reads and writes the database in separate steps.

- require produced blocks to match the requested duty slot with a typed `SLOT_MISMATCH` error, `signBlock` now takes the `dutySlot` (this replaces the untyped check added in #10169)
- serialize block slashing protection checks and writes per validator, including interchange block imports so an import cannot race a check for the same slot
- add regression coverage, align the doppelganger block fixtures with duty slots and correct a public-key test fixture

Without the serialization the overlap tests fail: two conflicting proposals for the same slot are both accepted, a lower slot is accepted after a higher one, and an interchange import racing a check for the same slot loses the imported block.
author: nflaig

title: test: assert progressive balance drift metric
body:
## Motivation
Follow-up to #10046: the progressive-balance self-heal increments `lodestar_stfn_progressive_balances_mismatches_total`, but the direct spec-test runners were not passing state-transition metrics, so drift could be silently healed during spec tests.

Twoeths also pointed out that the mismatch metric should say whether the current or previous target balance cache drifted, and that fork-choice spec tests are important because `on_block` computes unrealized checkpoints from fork-choice state.

## Changes
- Label `lodestar_stfn_progressive_balances_mismatches_total` by `target="current" | "previous"` and increment the matching label when that side drifts.
- Add isolated spec-test metrics for direct STF runners.
- Pass metrics through epoch processing, rewards, sanity, finality, and transition spec runners.
- Assert the progressive-balances mismatch counter stays at zero, including expected-error vectors where the shared `shouldError` path would swallow assertion failures.
- Add fork-choice spec-runner coverage that validates each successfully imported block post-state with the same progressive-balance invariant, without wiring state-transition metrics into production fork-choice APIs.

## Verification
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/beacon-node --filter @lodestar/state-transition --filter @lodestar/fork-choice check-types`
- `git diff --check`
- `pnpm vitest run --project spec-minimal packages/beacon-node/test/spec/presets/{epoch_processing,rewards,sanity,finality,transition}.test.ts` (5 files, 2811 passed / 9 skipped)
- `pnpm vitest run --project spec-minimal packages/beacon-node/test/spec/presets/fork_choice.test.ts` (494 passed / 11 skipped)

## Spec Compliance
- N/A: this adds test coverage and improves metric attribution; consensus transition behavior remains the #10046 self-heal behavior.

title: chore: remove legacy backfill sync
body:
## Motivation

Legacy backfill sync was introduced in #3384 and has been disabled by default since #3763. It remained available through the hidden `sync.backfillBatchSize` option, but was never updated for subsequent forks and is no longer a supported or spec-compliant sync path.

Keeping it still adds production wiring, database writes on every finalization, metrics, dashboard panels, and maintenance overhead. Any future backfill implementation should be introduced as a new fork-aware path. The backfill v2 work in #9238 remains separate from this cleanup.

## Description

- Remove the hidden `sync.backfillBatchSize` option and the legacy `BackfillSync` lifecycle wiring.
- Remove the legacy implementation, verification helpers, tests, metrics, and dashboard panels.
- Remove the `BackfilledRanges` repository and the range updates performed during finalization.
- Keep database bucket 42 reserved so existing data cannot be interpreted under a future schema.

This does not change normal sync behavior because the legacy path has been disabled by default since #3763.

## Testing

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/beacon-node check-types`
- `pnpm --filter @chainsafe/lodestar check-types`
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/beacon-node lint`
- `pnpm --filter @chainsafe/lodestar lint`
- `pnpm vitest run --project unit packages/cli/test/unit/options/beaconNodeOptions.test.ts`
- `pnpm lint-dashboards`

## AI assistance disclosure

> I used OpenAI Codex to trace the legacy path and prepare the cleanup. I reviewed the resulting diff and test output before submission.

title: refactor: remove legacy backfill sync
body:
Remove the legacy backfill implementation and its hidden `--sync.backfillBatchSize` flag, along with range bookkeeping, metrics, dashboard panels, and tests. Future backfill support will be built from scratch.

The implementation was introduced in #3384 and made opt-in in #3763 (February 2022). Database bucket 42 remains reserved.

Regression coverage for future backfill ([background](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10147#discussion_r4070973194), [phase0 note](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/phase0/p2p-interface.md#why-must-the-proposer-signature-be-checked-when-backfilling-blocks-in-the-database)):

- Reject a validly signed block whose message root differs from the requested root.
- Reject a non-genesis block with the expected root but an invalid proposer signature.
- Verify that range responses connect to the trusted anchor across batches and restarts.
- Ensure rejected data cannot modify archived blocks, indexes, or recorded progress.

body:
The [September 22 nightly](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/35693811106) downloaded August 30 vectors because GitHub returned stale workflow runs. The same API issue is reported in [GitHub discussion #206725](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/206725).

title: feat: persist pubkey cache across restarts
body:
## Motivation

On every restart the beacon node rebuilds the pubkey cache by decompressing every validator pubkey from the anchor state. On mainnet (2.37M validators) that is the single largest chunk of boot after loading the anchor state.

## Description

- On boot, best effort load of the pubkey cache from `${dataDir}/pubkeys` before syncing from the anchor state. Success and failure are logged at debug.
- On graceful shutdown, save the pubkey cache to the same file as the very last step, after `node.close()` (and after the db close in the error path).
- Hidden `--pubkeysFile` flag overrides the location.
- Native `load()` only checks framing, ABI and checksum. The loaded entries are spot-checked against the anchor state (index 0 and the last overlapping index) so a file from another chain gets discarded and we fall back to a full sync.
- Skip `getAllReadonlyValues()` for the handler's `syncPubkeys` when the loaded cache already covers the anchor state.

## Measurements

Local mainnet restarts from an existing db (32 cores, `--execution.engineMock`, warm page cache). Times are seconds since process launch.

| | "Initialized state from db" to "Flat file store initialized" | Launch to metrics server started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unstable (3 runs) | 9.36 / 9.26 / 9.40 | 42.65 / 42.71 / 43.65 |
| this PR, file loaded (3 runs) | 1.57 / 1.55 / 1.63 | 34.73 / 34.27 / 35.30 |

About 7.8s saved per restart (~19% of time to metrics server). A run with no file present matched unstable (9.12s / 43.26s).

- Load: 53-56ms for 2,370,466 entries
- Save on shutdown: 182-297ms
- File size: 341 MB (48 byte compressed + 96 byte affine point per validator)

Also ran the node for 150s from a loaded file: synced to head, finality advanced, no signature or pubkey errors, and the file was re-saved on shutdown.

## Notes

- The file format is ABI-locked (zig version, arch). A lodestar-z upgrade that changes it makes the load fail and the node falls back to a full sync, then saves a fresh file on shutdown.
- Entries beyond the anchor state's validator count (from unfinalized states in the previous run) are kept, same as they would have been in memory had the node not restarted.
- Discarding a mismatched file uses `pubkeyCache.reset()`, which lodestar-z documents as testing-only. It is safe here since no workers use the cache yet.

title: fix(validator): make slashing protection interchange import atomic
body:
Fixes #10001

**Issue Description:**
When importing an EIP-3076 slashing protection interchange file, `SlashingProtectionAttestationService.importAttestations` writes raw attestation records to `attestationByTarget` before calculating/validating min and max surround spans. If an imported attestation is rejected due to surround violations (or conflicting/invalid records), previous spans and attestation records from the failed batch remain persisted in LevelDB. This partially applied state corrupts slashing protection records and causes subsequent valid signing requests to be falsely rejected.

**Root Cause:**
1. `attestationByTarget.set(pubkey, attestations)` was called prior to inserting and verifying attestations against `minMaxSurround`.
2. `minMaxSurround.insertAttestation` mutated underlying LevelDB distance stores directly without rollback capabilities if subsequent attestations in the batch triggered surround rejections.

**Solution:**
1. Introduced `MemoryOverlayDistanceStore` wrapping `IDistanceStore`, staging min/max span updates in memory Maps with an explicit `commit(pubkey)` method.
2. Added `MinMaxSurround.createOverlay()` allowing batch insertions to validate and stage min/max spans in isolation.
3. Updated `SlashingProtectionAttestationService.importAttestations` to evaluate all attestations on the memory overlay first, and only commit `attestationByTarget.set()` and `overlay.commit(pubkey)` once all assertions pass.
4. Added unit test verifying that rejected batches leave no partial records and do not affect future valid signing operations.

title: fix: derive ephemery config from published iteration, not process start time
body:
## Motivation

Reported in #10160: with `--network ephemery`, a validator client refuses to start against its own beacon node when started any meaningful time after it:

```
Error: Local and remote configs are different
MIN_GENESIS_TIME different value: 1790188665039 != 1790188516030
```

`MIN_GENESIS_TIME` ends up being the **process start time in milliseconds** (so it differs for every process), and `/eth/v1/config/spec` reports a **fractional** `DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID`.

## Root cause

The ephemery config derived its dynamic values from:

```ts
const RESET_INTERVAL_MS = 604800000;
const iteration = Math.floor(Date.now() - baseChainConfig.MIN_GENESIS_TIME) / RESET_INTERVAL_MS;
```

Two compounding bugs:

1. **Misplaced `Math.floor`** — it wraps only the subtraction (already an integer), then divides, so `iteration` is fractional. That flows straight into `DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID` / `DEPOSIT_NETWORK_ID` → fractional deposit chain id.
2. **ms vs seconds** — `Date.now()` is milliseconds, `MIN_GENESIS_TIME` is seconds. With the fractional `iteration`, `RESET_INTERVAL_MS * iteration` reduces to `Date.now() - MIN_GENESIS_TIME`, so `MIN_GENESIS_TIME = RESET_INTERVAL_MS * iteration + baseChainConfig.MIN_GENESIS_TIME` collapses to exactly `Date.now()` (ms) — the process start time.

On top of that the bundled config was stale (see references below): ephemery's reset interval changed from 7 → **28 days** and `GENESIS_DELAY` from 300 → **600**, but the config still used `604800000 ms` / `GENESIS_DELAY: 300`.

## Why these values changed (upstream references)

All values are anchored to ephemery-genesis [`values.env`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/blob/a4b5a2ee5c1c40e378edc92f2ccd9938cf9207d0/values.env) (pinned, iteration 164):

| value | old | new | upstream change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| reset interval | 7d (`604800`) | 28d (`2419200`) | [`131d330`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/commit/131d330aab546ed2564b81be14981776cf8b1e2c) — "increase reset interval to 28days" (2024-06-28) |
| `GENESIS_DELAY` | `300` | `600` | [`f761969`](https://github.com/ephemery-testnet/ephemery-genesis/commit/f761969dd0c827af58f6b19c4fce0f5298fe8f65) — "update genesis generator, new release layout" (2024-06-28) |
| `MIN_GENESIS_TIME` / `CHAIN_ID` | iteration-0 base | iteration 164 (`1790276400` / `39438164`) | current `values.env` (advances by one each reset) |

Ephemery periodically resets (EIP-6916); `values.env` publishes each new iteration. Lodestar bundles a base and rolls it forward, so the base only needs to stay within the current reset cadence rather than be bumped every iteration.

## Description

- Rebase the bundled base to the current published iteration (`values.env` iteration 164) and fix `GENESIS_DELAY` `300 → 600`.
- Recompute the iteration in **whole seconds** with a correctly-placed `Math.floor` and the 28-day interval.
- `values.env` stages the *next* iteration ahead of its activation, so resolve the iteration **active at `nowMs`** (the most recent reset at/before now) rather than clamping forward-only — a node started before the staged iteration activates still derives the live iteration.
- Extract `getEphemeryChainConfig(nowMs)` so the time-dependent derivation is deterministic and unit-tested (`packages/config/test/unit/networks.test.ts`).

Every process within an iteration now computes identical whole-second values, which is what the VC↔BN params check requires.

## Verification

Reproduced through the actual failing path (`assertEqualParams`, `validator.ts:372 → params.ts:95` in the stack trace) with the reporter's exact process start times:

```
OLD -> Local and remote configs are different | MIN_GENESIS_TIME different value: 1790188665039 != 1790188516030
FIX -> BN.MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200 VC.MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200 DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID=39438163 (assertEqualParams OK)
```

The fix derives the **live** iteration 163 values (`MIN_GENESIS_TIME=1787857200`, `genesis_time=1787857800`, `DEPOSIT_CHAIN_ID=39438163`) — matching the reporter's synced beacon node — so a BN and a VC started ~149s apart agree and the VC connects. Local: config unit tests green, `tsc` + biome clean.

Closes #10160

title: fix: use exact integer division for Electra slashing penalty
body:
The Electra correlation penalty per increment was computed with float division followed by `Math.floor`. Once the numerator exceeds `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, which takes roughly 3M ETH slashed within the slashings window, an exact quotient just below an integer can be rounded up by the division itself, leaving nothing for `Math.floor` to truncate. The penalty is then 1 Gwei per effective balance increment higher than the spec and the post-state root diverges from other clients.

- compute the penalty per increment with bigint, same as `getBuilderPaymentQuorumThreshold`
- add a unit test with a vector that previously rounded up (268437223 instead of 268437222 Gwei per increment)

Not practically exploitable since it needs ~9% of total stake slashed within 36 days and the division to land in the rounding window (~1 in 37M), but spec tests cannot cover it. Verified with the reporter's reproduction, on the same SSZ pre-state the post-state root now matches Prysm. The pre-Electra branch and other float divisions in the state transition keep their numerators below 2^53 or divide by a power of two.
author: nflaig

title: fix: validate slot and epoch values on slashing protection import
body:
Slot and epoch values of an EIP-3076 interchange file were parsed with `parseInt` without any range check. Values of `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` or more are either stored truncated (`18446744073709551615` becomes slot or epoch 0) or are invisible to the range scans of the slashing protection DB, so the imported lower bound is lost and the export writes different values back out. Values close to 2^64 also make the min-span update on import loop forever since `epoch - 1 === epoch`. Malformed strings like `12abc` or `1.5` were silently accepted as well.

- parse slot and epoch values strictly as decimal uints below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, otherwise reject the import with `ERR_INTERCHANGE_INVALID_VALUE` before anything is written to the DB
- add unit tests for accepted and rejected values

Not exploitable in practice, an import requires the keymanager API token or an operator importing an untrusted file, and a file with valid low values already lowers the lower bound the same way (a later import may lower it for a complete database, see `should_succeed_complete` in the v5.3.0 interchange tests). Real slots and epochs are bounded by the clock, the largest value in the EIP-3076 test vectors is 1201.

Validation

- the new unit tests fail without this change (9 of 11) and pass with it
- ran the affected scenarios through `SlashingProtection.importInterchange`, which the keymanager API and `slashing-protection import` both use, before and after this change

| scenario | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| block floor at slot 5000, then import slot `2^64 - 1` | import succeeds, slot 4000 is signed, export shows slot `"0"` | import rejected, slot 4000 still refused, export unchanged |
| empty DB, import slot `2^53 - 1` | import succeeds, the record is invisible to range scans | import rejected, nothing written |
| attestation floor at epoch 500, then import epoch `2^64 - 1` | import succeeds, attestation (10, 20) is signed | import rejected, (10, 20) still refused |
| empty DB, import attestation `(2^64 - 1, 2^64 - 1)` | import never completes | import rejected immediately |

- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass

Target epochs below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` that are far in the future can still make the import run practically forever, this is addressed separately in #10170.
author: nflaig

title: test: apply EIP-3076 interchange test steps in order and update to v5.3.0
body:
The EIP-3076 interchange test runner did not follow the [test format](https://github.com/eth-clients/slashing-protection-interchange-tests#how-to-run), which starts each test with an empty database and then, step by step, imports the interchange and attempts the block and attestation signings, remembering the ones that succeed, before moving to the next step.

Instead, every step with checks registered a `beforeEach` hook in the same `describe`, so before every single signing check all hooks ran, each clearing the database and importing its own step. This means

- every check ran against a database holding only the interchange of the last step that has checks, steps without checks were never imported
- messages signed by one check were cleared before the next one
- steps with `contains_slashable_data` never ran their checks, and the expected import failure for them was never exercised
- a `should_succeed: false` import was expected to resolve, which also never ran since that test has no checks

Changes

- run each test case as a single test that applies all steps in order on the same database
- a step with slashable data that Lodestar refuses to import as slashable (`InvalidAttestationError` from the import check, or `SurroundAttestationError` if the surround is only found while inserting spans) skips its checks, the format allows clients to refuse such data and the checks assume it was imported, any other import failure fails the test. Steps with an expected import failure still run their checks
- update the vectors from v5.1.0 to v5.3.0, which adds 5 multi-interchange tests and `should_succeed_complete` next to `should_succeed`. Releases after v5.2.0 no longer attach a tarball, so the source archive of the tag is downloaded instead (38 test files, identical to `tests/generated` at the tag)
- check signings against `should_succeed` where it is equal to `should_succeed_complete`, otherwise accept either outcome. `should_succeed` is the expected outcome for a minimal database and `should_succeed_complete` for a complete one, Lodestar stores all signed messages but also enforces the lower bounds of imported data so it sits in between (e.g. after importing block 40 and then block 50, a complete database may sign block 45, a minimal one may not)

All 38 vectors pass on current code, so this does not depend on any other change. Five steps skip their checks because the import is refused with `ERR_INVALID_ATTESTATION_NEW_SURROUNDS_PREV` (`duplicate_pubkey_slashable_attestation`, `single_validator_slashable_attestations_surrounds_existing`, `single_validator_slashable_attestations_surrounded_by_existing`, and step 1 of `multiple_interchanges_single_validator_first_surrounds_second` and `multiple_interchanges_single_validator_second_surrounds_first`).

To confirm the runner now tests what it is supposed to, I added a mutation that clears the database on every import (simulating an import that drops previously imported data). The new runner fails 5 multi-interchange tests, the previous runner with v5.1.0 still passes all 94 tests. None of the vectors re-sign a conflicting message after a successful signing within a step, so remembering signed messages is required by the format but not covered by the current vectors.

The CI cache key for these vectors is the hash of `params.ts`, so the version bump invalidates it.
author: nflaig

title: fix: do not replace recorded slashing protection data on interchange import
body:
Importing slashing protection interchange data wrote each block and attestation with `batchPut`, which replaces whatever was stored for the same slot or target epoch. A record of a message that was actually signed could therefore be replaced by an imported record with a different signing root.

For example, after signing a block with root `A` at slot 100, importing `{"slot": "100", "signing_root": "<B>"}` stores root `B` for slot 100. A later request to sign block `B` at slot 100 is then treated as a repeat of the same block (`SAME_DATA`) and gets signed, which is a double proposal together with `A`. The same applies to attestations with the same target epoch (double vote), including an imported attestation with a different source epoch for a target that is not the latest one (the existing import check only covers the latest target). This requires importing interchange data, via the keymanager API or the `slashing-protection import` command, and a second signing request for the same slot or target epoch, which the validator client does not make on its own.

Imported records are now merged with what is already stored, both in the database and earlier in the same file

- same source epoch and signing root: stored as before, so importing an export of the same history is a no-op and re-signing the same message still works
- anything else: stored with a zero signing root, which refuses any block at that slot or attestation with that target epoch. This is the same handling as for an imported record without `signing_root`, EIP-3076 requires treating any new message at that slot as slashable in that case
- for attestations the higher source epoch is kept, the import already requires the latest attestation to have the highest source epoch as `checkAttestation` relies on it

This adds one database read per imported block and attestation, next to the reads the min-max surround update already does for each imported attestation.

Validation

- new unit tests in `test/unit/slashingProtection/import.test.ts`, 4 of the 7 fail on `unstable` with the conflicting message being signed, the other 3 cover cases that already worked (import without signing root, re-signing the same message) and guard the merge logic
- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass with the current runner (v5.1.0, 94 tests) and with the runner from #10167 (v5.3.0, 38 tests)
author: nflaig

title: fix: check attestation target epoch and block slot before signing
body:
The validator client only checked that attestation data and blocks received from the beacon node are not for a future epoch or slot. It did not check that they belong to the duty being performed, so a malicious or faulty beacon node could get it to sign

- attestation data for the duty slot with an older target epoch (only `duty.slot === data.slot` and `target.epoch <= currentEpoch` were checked)
- a block for an older slot during a proposal (only `block.slot <= currentSlot` was checked)

Neither is valid for the duty, and slashing protection is the only thing left that prevents such a message from being slashable. That is fine as long as the slashing protection database has the full history, but not for history it does not know about, e.g. after an interchange import that did not include all signed messages, which the EIP-3076 lower bounds only partially cover.

- reject attestation data where `target.epoch` is not the epoch of `data.slot`, this also covers aggregates since they go through the same `validateAttestationDuty`
- only sign a block if its slot equals the proposal slot

Honest data always passes both checks. `process_attestation` requires `data.target.epoch == compute_epoch_at_slot(data.slot)` (also asserted in `processAttestationPhase0`), and our beacon node derives the target epoch from the requested slot. The block service passes the slot it requested the block for as `currentSlot`, and the block returned for that request must have that slot.

Validation

- added unit tests to `validatorStore.test.ts` that fail on `unstable` (both messages get signed) and pass with this change, the existing validator store and services unit tests pass
- the web3signer e2e test signed attestation data with target epoch 0 at slot 2375711 (epoch 74240) and aggregates with target epoch 0 at the start slot of each fork, which is now refused. The fixtures use the target epoch of the slot, verified locally against web3signer, 7 tests fail with the old fixtures and all pass with the new ones
- the doppelganger e2e test signs a slot 0 block at the current slot, updated to sign a block at the current slot. The suite is skipped and fails on `unstable` for unrelated reasons (timeouts, pre-electra block production), un-skipped locally the new check no longer shows up in its failures with the updated fixtures
author: nflaig

title: fix: reject slashing protection import of attestations from the future
body:
Importing an attestation updates the min-max surround spans, and the max-span update does one database read for each epoch between the source and target epoch until it finds an existing span that is large enough. On the first import for a validator nothing stops it early, so an interchange file with an attestation like `{"source_epoch": "0", "target_epoch": "9007199254740990"}` makes the import run practically forever, collecting span entries in memory until the process runs out of it. #10166 rejects values close to 2^64 where `epoch - 1 === epoch` made the loop endless, but values below `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` are still valid.

The keymanager API imports slashing protection data inside the running validator client, which never responds to the request and keeps growing memory. There the current epoch is known, and no attestation can have been signed for a target epoch that has not happened yet.

- `importInterchange` takes an optional `currentEpoch` and rejects the whole import with `ERR_INTERCHANGE_FUTURE_TARGET_EPOCH` before writing anything if an attestation has a target epoch more than one epoch after it, one epoch is allowed for clock disparity with the client the data was exported from, and before genesis (where the clock's current epoch is negative) the bound is taken from the genesis epoch so a genesis attestation can still be imported
- the validator client passes its current epoch for keymanager API imports

With the current epoch the max-span update is bounded by the number of epochs since genesis. The `slashing-protection import` command is not changed, it is run by the operator who can interrupt it, and it does not always know the genesis time (e.g. custom networks without access to a beacon node).

Validation

- new unit tests in `test/unit/slashingProtection/interchange/futureTargetEpoch.test.ts`, without this change importing target `2^53 - 2` times out after 20s and target `currentEpoch + 2` is accepted, with it both are rejected and nothing is written, target `currentEpoch + 1` is still accepted, before genesis targets 0 and 1 are accepted and 2 is rejected
- confirmed with a validator client process through the keymanager API (the `startValidatorWithKeyManager` e2e setup), before this change the import of `(0, 9007199254740990)` did not respond within 20s, with it the request fails in 14ms with `ERR_INTERCHANGE_FUTURE_TARGET_EPOCH`, a regular import of `(0, 1)` returns 200 in both cases
- EIP-3076 interchange tests pass (94 tests, the runner does not pass a current epoch)

title: ci: attest Docker image provenance and SBOMs

Adds GitHub artifact attestations for Lodestar Docker image provenance and SBOMs, so published images can be verified by digest instead of trusting mutable tags alone.

title: feat: schedule 200M gas limit at Glamsterdam on Sepolia
body:
**Motivation**

Keep Lodestar's Sepolia config in sync with the canonical network config for the Glamsterdam upgrade. [eth-clients/sepolia#130](https://github.com/eth-clients/sepolia/pull/130) schedules a gas limit bump to 200M at the fork, so Lodestar should ship the matching schedule.

**Description**

Adds a `GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE` entry to the Sepolia config raising the gas limit to `200000000` at epoch `353024` — the Glamsterdam (Gloas) fork, already scheduled on Sepolia via #10119.

```yaml
GAS_LIMIT_SCHEDULE:
  - EPOCH: 353024
    GAS_LIMIT: 200000000
```

title: fix: include active slashed validators in fork choice committee weight
body:
Proposer boost and the proposer reorg thresholds are a fraction of the committee weight, which the spec derives from `get_total_active_balance(justified_state)` in `compute_proposer_score` and `calculate_committee_fraction`. That total counts every active validator, including slashed ones that have not exited yet. We summed the justified balances instead, which zero slashed validators since their votes carry no weight, so the proposer boost and both reorg thresholds came out too small by the stake that is slashed but still active.

The difference is proportional to that stake and only exists until those validators exit, so it is small in practice, but it can make us choose a different head than clients that follow the spec in close cases, which today are only Teku and Nimbus. Prysm, Lighthouse and Grandine exclude slashed validators like we do (see [gist](https://gist.github.com/nflaig/25868d98c1134c187c41ce39ffc7cc9b)). Same issue as sigp/lighthouse#10057, open PR sigp/lighthouse#10062.

- the justified balances getter returns `{balances, totalBalance}` where `totalBalance` sums the effective balance increments over the active indices of the justified state, and the fork choice store keeps it next to `balances` instead of summing them
- `CheckpointBalancesCache` caches both

Vote weights still use the zeroed balances. Fast confirmation computes its total active balance from zeroed balances too (`getTotalActiveBalance`), that is not changed here.

Validation

- new unit test for `getJustifiedBalances` with an active slashed validator
- fork choice (494) and fast confirmation (1428) minimal spec tests pass

title: fix: update `earliestAvailableSlot` when pruning history
body:
`earliestAvailableSlot` is set once at startup to the anchor state slot and never updated, so a node with `--chain.pruneHistory` keeps advertising blocks in `Status` that it has already pruned once it has been running longer than `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS`. Peers then request those ranges and get an empty response instead of `ResourceUnavailable`, since the by range handlers only reject requests below `earliestAvailableSlot`.

`pruneHistory` now returns the block cutoff slot and the archive store raises `earliestAvailableSlot` to it after each run. The setter already triggers a status update.

title: fix: settle builder payment before processing parent execution requests
body:
a builder exit request in the parent's payload was applied before the parent's payment was settled. when the parent is older than the previous epoch the payment was already evicted, so the exit guard saw nothing pending and the exit went through right before the payment was re-added. the sweep then paid out the full balance while the payment was still queued

title: fix: floor attestation reward and penalty values
body:
**Motivation**

`computeAttestationsRewards` rounds ideal rewards and penalties to the nearest Gwei, while the state transition (`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`) and the consensus spec use integer division. Any value with a fractional part of 0.5 or more is reported 1 Gwei higher than what is actually applied to balances, so the per-validator breakdown does not sum to the real balance change.

**Description**

Floor ideal rewards and penalties with the same expression as `getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`.

- `computeIdealAttestationsRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`: replace both `Math.round` calls with `Math.floor` and divide by `activeBalanceByIncrement * WEIGHT_DENOMINATOR` in one step
- `attestationsRewards.test.ts`: check ideal rewards against a `bigint` reference and check each validator's `head + target + source + inactivity` against `rewards[i] - penalties[i]` from the state transition

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation and tests were primarily AI-authored and reviewed by me.

title: fix: use fork inactivity quotient in rewards
body:
**Motivation**

`computeAttestationsRewards` always uses `INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ALTAIR`. Bellatrix lowered the quotient from `3 * 2**24` to `2**24`, and the state transition (`getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`) already selects it by fork. Since Bellatrix the API reports about one third of the inactivity penalty actually applied to balances.

**Description**

Select the inactivity penalty quotient by fork, matching `getRewardsAndPenaltiesAltair`.

- `computeTotalAttestationsRewardsAltair`: use `INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_ALTAIR` for Altair and `INACTIVITY_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_BELLATRIX` afterwards
- `attestationsRewardsInactivity.test.ts`: check `inactivity` against a `bigint` reference for Altair and Bellatrix states

title: perf: use set for attestation rewards filter
body:
**Motivation**

`computeTotalAttestationsRewardsAltair` checks each validator against the requested ids with `Array.includes`, which costs O(requested ids × validators). 

**Description**

Look up requested validator indices in a `Set`. Behavior is unchanged.

title: fix: initialize earliestAvailableSlot from retained history on startup
body:
## Motivation

On an **in-place restart** (existing DB, not a fresh checkpoint sync), `earliestAvailableSlot` was re-initialized to the anchor state slot and only ever raised afterwards (`Math.max` on prune). A node that still retains finalized history below the anchor then rejects `beacon_blocks_by_range`, `execution_payload_envelopes_by_range`, and `data_column_sidecars_by_range` requests for data it actually holds — the incoming by_range error rate jumps to ~100%.

Observed live on v1.49.0 RC soak nodes: after a restart, `earliestAvailableSlot` jumped `246560 → 313312` (the finalized anchor) while the node still retained history back to ~246560, and every by_range request for that range was rejected with `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE`. `beacon_blocks_by_range` (never deduped) behaved identically to the envelope path, confirming it is not dedup-related.

Closes #10181. Part of #7997 (the startup/init "correct location" for `earliestAvailableSlot`).

## Description

In `ArchiveStore.init()`, after pruning, initialize `earliestAvailableSlot` from the earliest block still present in the archive (`db.blockArchive.firstKey()`) instead of leaving it at the anchor slot set in the constructor. Falls back to the anchor when the archive is empty (fresh checkpoint sync with nothing below the anchor). It now runs regardless of `pruneHistory`, so archival nodes also advertise from their earliest retained block rather than the anchor.

The block-archive floor is the correct single value for all three by_range handlers:
- `beacon_blocks_by_range` and `execution_payload_envelopes_by_range` share the block retention floor (envelopes are pruned together with blocks in `pruneHistory`).
- `data_column_sidecars_by_range` handles slots above the floor with missing columns gracefully (spec-legal short response, no error — see `handleColumnSidecarUnavailability`), so the block floor is a safe lower bound.

Tightening `earliestAvailableSlot` to also track the (usually higher) data-column retention floor, and lowering it during backfill, is the DA-window/expiry side of #7997 and is left as follow-up.

## Testing

Added unit tests in `archiveStore.test.ts`:
- `init` lowers `earliestAvailableSlot` from the anchor to the earliest retained block.
- `init` keeps the anchor when the archive is empty.

title: fix: persist earliestAvailableSlot across checkpoint sync restarts
body:
## Problem

Follow-up to #10185 and the review discussion at https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10186#discussion_r4110612893.

A checkpoint sync can leave older archived blocks separated from the new anchor by a gap. Using `blockArchive.firstKey()` as `earliestAvailableSlot` then advertises a range the node cannot serve. Keeping the checkpoint anchor only for that startup still exposes the gap on the next plain database restart.

## Fix

- Thread `isCheckpointState` from `initBeaconState` through node/chain initialization to `ArchiveStore`.
- Append DB bucket 61 and a single-value Slot store, preserving all existing bucket IDs.
- On checkpoint sync, persist the anchor floor and replace any stale record. On plain startup, restore the persisted floor.
- When no record exists, retain the #10185 `firstKey()` fallback (or the anchor for an empty archive) and persist the result for later restarts.
- Persist runtime prune advances and clamp the startup floor to the startup prune cutoff.

The hidden `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` path remains conservatively classified as a checkpoint when its checkpoint state is selected as the anchor. Backfill and DA-window-aware floor selection remain outside this change (#7997).

## Validation

- `pnpm build`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm check-types`
- ArchiveStore and DB unit suites: 221 tests across 19 files, including real LevelDB close/reopen regressions for checkpoint and prune floors, upgrade fallback, slot zero, and singleton isolation.

Checks used the supplied dependency installation with command-local `pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=false`.

Refs #10185, #7997.

> AI assistance: The original change was generated with Claude Code. The persisted-floor implementation and regression tests were written with OpenAI Codex and reviewed by Codex agents.

title: feat: allow enabling the discv5 inbound rate limiter
body:
**Motivation**

`@chainsafe/discv5` has an inbound packet rate limiter (global + per IP GCRA), but the beacon node never passes `rateLimiterOpts` to `Discv5.create`, so it is always off and the discv5 UDP port accepts unbounded inbound packets.

**Description**

- Plumb `rateLimiterOpts` from network options through `Discv5WorkerData` into `Discv5.create` in the worker.
- Add hidden flags `--network.discv5RateLimitGlobal` and `--network.discv5RateLimitPerIp` (packets per second). Both must be set together. Unset keeps current behavior.

I kept it opt-in on purpose. The discv5 limiter bans an IP until restart once it exceeds the per IP quota (`bannedIPs` is never pruned), so picking default values could cut off legit peers behind a shared IP. If you want it on by default I can add defaults here, or first add ban expiry in discv5. Which do you prefer?

Testing:
- Unit tests for the option parsing (mapping and the both-or-neither check).
- Manual: started a `Discv5Worker` on localhost and sent it 500 UDP packets. Limiter off: `discv5_rate_limit_hit_ip 0`. Limiter on (100/s global, 10/s per IP): `discv5_rate_limit_hit_ip 1`, the IP gets banned and the rest are dropped.
- `pnpm lint`, `check-types` for beacon-node and cli.

**Motivation**

`initBeaconState()` mixes source selection, loading, validation, and persistence, making it difficult to maintain.

Refactor startup to select a BeaconState serialized bytes and deserialize  exactly once. This also prepares the initialization flow to return `IBeaconStateView` in a separate PR.

**Description**

- Read genesis identity, slot, and active-validator statistics from serialized bytes
- Make checkpoint downloads return bytes without constructing a state.
- Preserve the main `unstable` behavior

```text

                            |
                    Validate options
                            |
              Read archived DB bytes once
              and assess weak subjectivity
                            |

                             |
```

- `ReconstructMismatchPolicy` -> `ReconstructMissPolicy`, covering both misses: `"throw"` for REST and single lookups, `"omit"` for by-root
- REST answers `500` with the reason instead of `404` (EL down stays `503`); `404` remains for envelopes that are not archived. No API change needed: the chain getters used to return `null` here, which fell through to the `404` in `getSignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope`; they now throw, and the existing `EnvelopeReconstructionError` catch in `api/impl/beacon/blocks/index.ts` maps anything but `ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE` to `500`
