title: fix: use preallocated buffers in `getBlobsV2`
body:
`getBlobs` declares a `buffers` parameter but the implementation never forwarded it to `getBlobsV2`, so the buffers preallocated by `GetBlobsTracker` since #8282 were ignored and every `engine_getBlobsV2` response was decoded into fresh allocations. Forwarding them surfaces a second issue: the tracker preallocates one buffer per max blobs of the epoch (#8938) while `getBlobsV2` required exactly one buffer per requested versioned hash, so any block with fewer blobs than the max would have thrown `Invalid buffers length` before the request was sent.

- forward `buffers` from `getBlobs` to `getBlobsV2`
- only require at least as many buffers as versioned hashes, the first entries are used
- add a unit test with more preallocated buffers than requested hashes

title: feat: support engine api over REST with SSZ encoding
body:
Implements the REST engine API with SSZ encoded bodies from [execution-apis#793](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/refactor.md) next to the existing JSON-RPC transport. The transport is picked per execution client connection from `GET /engine/v1/capabilities`, so nodes on an execution client without the REST API keep working unchanged, and the REST API is used by default where it is advertised.

- add the engine API wire containers, composed from the consensus payload types with `Optional[T]` encoded as `List[T, 1]`
- split `ExecutionEngineHttp` into a JSON-RPC and a REST transport behind `IEngineTransport`, the engine keeps the request queue, engine state, payload id cache and result handling
- probe the capabilities once per connection and again after a disconnect. In `auto` mode an execution client without the REST API (a 4xx other than 401, 403, 408 or 429) or with a capabilities document that cannot be parsed selects JSON-RPC until it reconnects, the latter with a warning. Timeouts, 408, 429 and 5xx use JSON-RPC and probe again after 12 seconds, 401 and 403 stay errors. Forks and `/blobs/vN` revisions that are not advertised stay on JSON-RPC, and a fork rejected with `unsupported-fork` despite being advertised falls back to JSON-RPC until reconnect
- REST is only negotiated with a single execution URL, multiple URLs keep JSON-RPC and its fallback across URLs. `ssz` requires a single URL and never falls back, `json-rpc` never probes
- validate the blob versioned hashes of the payload's type-3 transactions against the beacon commitments before submitting over REST, since the envelope has no `expected_blob_versioned_hashes` and the EL can no longer run that check. JSON-RPC keeps delegating it to the EL
- honor the advertised request limits, oversized requests fail locally and are not split
- add `--execution.engineApi auto|ssz|json-rpc` (default `auto`) and the `lodestar_execution_engine_api_requests_total{transport}` counter, the REST client reports the same per-route client metrics including the request and response bytes from #10195. Transport selection and fallbacks are logged at debug level
- decode `/blobs/v2` responses as views into the response body instead of copying, the response is all-or-nothing so every byte is needed, `/blobs/v1` keeps copies since partial responses carry zero-filled entries
- send `X-Engine-Client-Version` as the JSON `ClientVersionV1` object since the spec does not pin a format and that is what Nethermind parses
- malformed SSZ or JSON on a 2xx response and HTTP errors are classified as engine errors, only transport failures mark the execution client offline

The client speaks HTTP/1.1 only, neither reth nor Nethermind negotiates h2c on the cleartext engine port today. Left for follow-ups: HTTP/2, `/blobs/v3` and `/blobs/v4`, `custody_columns` on forkchoice updates, and the `bogota` header value once [execution-apis#920](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/920) lands. Heze stays on JSON-RPC in `auto` mode until then.

Verified on kurtosis devnets (minimal preset, blob spam), see the interop reports in the comments for the per-route numbers:

- reth `v2.7.0` and `main`: everything over REST including `/blobs/v2`, blobs resolved into data columns on a non-supernode, fulu at genesis and an electra to fulu transition with the blob revision switching at the fork boundary
- Nethermind `master` after [NethermindEth/nethermind#14302](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/pull/14302): same two scenarios, everything over REST. Before the fix every forkchoice update with payload attributes was rejected with `unsupported-fork` on chainspec networks ([NethermindEth/nethermind#14006](https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/issues/14006)) and the per-fork fallback kept the node proposing over JSON-RPC
- geth and Nethermind 1.38.0: `404` on capabilities, JSON-RPC for the whole run

Supersedes #10155.

title: fix: delete orphaned execution payload envelopes from hot db
body:
Hot envelopes whose block already left fork choice are never reached by the finalized walk in `archiveBlocks`, so they stay in the hot db forever. On glamsterdam-devnet-8 a Lodestar node had 17 hot envelopes at or below the finalized slot that were not in the archive, the oldest at slot 78912.

- on each finalization (post-gloas), delete hot envelopes whose block root is not in fork choice (`hasBlockHexUnsafe`)
- the main source is orphans from before a restart: fork choice is rebuilt from the anchor, so they are never non-ancestors. They can't be dropped in `pruneHotDb` like hot blobs, since the anchor block's envelope is only archived in the next run
- the finalized block and its descendants are in fork choice, so their envelopes are kept; envelope writes check the block is in fork choice first
author: nflaig

title: fix: deduplicate and stream execution payload envelopes by root
body:
By-root requests reconstructed all archived envelopes before sending a response, including duplicate roots. A request repeating one archived root 128 times caused four Engine calls containing 128 copies of the same hash, followed by 128 body verifications and envelope serializations.

- Deduplicate roots before lookup so each envelope is reconstructed and served once.
- Reconstruct and yield batches of at most 32 envelopes (`MAX_BODIES_PER_REQUEST`), allowing responses to start after the first batch.
- Preserve a partial response if the EL fails after some envelopes were served; return `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` if none were served. The by-root protocol permits partial responses.

Broader reconstruction limits, worker backpressure, and cancellation are tracked in #10193.

title: fix: discount empty slot support by fork choice node
body:
## Motivation

[consensus-specs#5672](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5672) fixed `compute_empty_slot_support_discount` to discount the parent *node* a block extends, not the parent root. Post-gloas a root has `PENDING`, `EMPTY` and `FULL` nodes, so the root-only match summed all three and confirmed one block too far. Nightly is red with 4 `Invalid confirmed root` failures.

## Description

- `getBlockSupportBetweenSlots` → `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots`, matching root **and** payload status
- `getLatestMessage` surfaces `node.payloadStatus` — `voteNextIndices` already holds a node index, the accessor was dropping the variant
- New `getParentPayloadStatus` on the FCR context, one `.parent` hop

Pre-gloas is unchanged. The pinned `v1.7.0-beta.2` vector for `..._two_consecutive_slots_1` predates #5672 and asserts the pre-fix root, so it is skipped for `gloas`/`heze` only until the spec-tests pin bump.

title: fix: consider p2p bids in `produceBlockV4WithBid`
body:
**Motivation**

When a supplied bid fails validation, `produceBlockV4WithBid` falls back exclusively to local payload production, even if a matching P2P bid is available. A slow local build can therefore delay the proposal unnecessarily.

In one case observed on plataberget, a produceBlockV4WithBid request arrived 603 ms into the slot and took 3.483 seconds to return a local block due to a slow Engine getPayloadV6 API call, resulting in an orphaned block. A matching P2P bid was already available. If its beacon block had been ready by the existing two-second slot cutoff, this fallback could have returned after approximately 1.397 seconds, about 2.086 seconds sooner.

**Description**

Consider the best matching P2P bid immediately after a supplied bid fails validation, while local payload production continues in parallel. Apply the existing minimum bid and boost rules to select between the two blocks. A ready P2P block can be returned at the existing cutoff without waiting for slow local production.

Valid supplied bids and builder circuit-breaker behavior remain unchanged.

Add tests covering parent matching, local payload preference, immediate fallback, and returning a P2P block while local production is pending.

Validation: all 46 targeted block-production tests pass, along with lint, beacon-node type-checking, and the build.

title: fix: merge attester duties for newly discovered validators
body:
`pollBeaconAttestersForEpoch` compared an incremental poll's duty count with the entire epoch cache size. When `dependentRoot` stayed unchanged, a delta batch no larger than the cache was discarded, silently dropping newly-active validators' attester duties.

Merge missing duties unconditionally, retaining selection-proof generation. Use the cache size increase only for the debug log and count. The regression test covers one new duty arriving with one or two duties already cached.

This is the attester-duties sibling of #10197, with the same root cause confirmed by nflaig in [issuecomment-5869536530](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10197#issuecomment-5869536530) and traced by lodekeeper through the full-index and incremental-index polling paths.

- `pnpm vitest run --project unit packages/validator/test/unit/services/attestationDuties.test.ts`: all 9 tests pass.
- With the pre-fix source, both new regression cases fail and the existing 7 tests pass.

title: fix: track slashing signature domains across forks
body:
**Motivation**

Pooled slashings can become invalid across a fork transition, but block production still selects them, causing the produced block to fail signature verification. For example, future-slot headers or future-target attestations signed with the pre-fork domain can be admitted just before the fork and become invalid immediately afterward.

**Description**

Cache the signature domains used to validate proposer and attester slashings, then evict entries whose domains differ in the proposal state. This avoids repeating BLS verification during block production.

Revalidate persisted slashings on startup to rebuild the cache. Also fix proposer-slashing key decoding and replacement writes so persistence preserves valid slashings.

Closes #10215

title: fix: revalidate pooled slashings before block inclusion
body:
**Motivation**

Pooled slashings can become invalid across a fork transition, but block production still selects them. Future-slot headers or future-target attestations signed with the pre-fork domain can pass admission before the fork, then cause locally produced blocks to fail signature verification afterward.

**Description**

Revalidate proposer and attester slashings against the proposal state, including their signatures, before inclusion. Remove invalid entries and continue selecting valid evidence. The same check covers slashings restored from disk. Also fix proposer-slashing key decoding and replacement writes so persistence preserves valid evidence.

Alternative to #10217: this uses the existing state-transition checks without caching verification domains or changing admission and startup APIs. The trade-off is synchronous BLS verification during block production, after the existing selection filters.

Validation: 37 targeted tests, lint, and beacon-node type checking passed. The updated benchmark uses valid signatures; locally, selecting 16 proposer and 2 attester slashings took about 68 ms.

Closes #10215

title: fix: revert fast confirmation to finalized on error
body:
**Motivation**

If the fast confirmation rule throws, the error is logged at debug and `confirmedRoot` keeps its previous value. After a reorg that root can sit on the losing branch and still be sent to the EL as `safeBlockHash`. The spec reverts to the finalized checkpoint in that case.

Seen when the head moves to a sibling at epoch start, its post-state is not in the block state cache, and there is an equivocator or a skipped slot. The epoch-start chain safety check then throws on the missing head state.

**Description**

- On error, set `confirmedRoot` to the finalized checkpoint, count it as a reset/fallback, and log at warn.
- Notify subscribers outside the rule's try/catch so a notify failure does not undo a valid root.
- Skip the epoch-start chain safety check when the confirmed block is already behind or not an ancestor of head, matching the spec's short-circuit `or`.

title: fix: apply epoch updates before computing attestation rewards
body:
Follow up of #10183 

**Motivation**
 
 The attestations rewards API computes on the pre-transition state, but in epoch processing `process_rewards_and_penalties` runs after `process_justification_and_finalization` and `process_inactivity_updates`. The API therefore charged the inactivity penalty on stale scores and judged leak status from stale finality. 

**Description**

- `computeAttestationsRewards`: clone the state and run justification/finalization and inactivity updates before computing, matching the spec ordering.
- Replace the quotient-only test from #10183 with balance-delta tests: run the epoch transition on the same state and assert every validator's balance change equals the API total. Covers Altair, Bellatrix and Electra, leak and no leak, and a transition that ends a leak. These also catch the quotient bug #10183 fixed.
- Add the same balance-delta check for block rewards and a new sync committee rewards test (previously no coverage). Both endpoints already matched the chain.
- Fix `getBlockAltair` in the perf helpers: it cleared attester participation with `set(index, 0)`, a no-op because `ParticipationFlags` ORs values in. Blocks built by it paid zero attestation reward, so the block rewards test was asserting 0 === 0 for that component. Expect the benchmark bot to report slower `processBlock` numbers, since the perf blocks now do real attestation work.

title: fix: accept LODESTAR_Z_NODE_POOL_CAPACITY under strict CLI parsing
body:
**Motivation**

`@chainsafe/lodestar-z` v1.1.0 sizes its node pool from `LODESTAR_Z_NODE_POOL_CAPACITY` and makes ~440 MB resident when the addon loads, in every Lodestar command. Setting the variable makes the CLI exit with `Unknown argument: zNodePoolCapacity`, because `.env("LODESTAR")` with `.strict()` maps it to an undeclared option. Operators therefore cannot size the pool. Details and measurements are in the linked issue.

**Description**

Declare a hidden `zNodePoolCapacity` global option, in the same way as the hidden `preset` option for `LODESTAR_PRESET`. The addon reads the environment variable itself when it loads, before yargs parses arguments, so the option only has to be accepted, not used.

Adds a unit test that parses the global options with `.env("LODESTAR")` and `.strict()` while `LODESTAR_Z_NODE_POOL_CAPACITY=0` is set. The test fails with `Unknown argument: zNodePoolCapacity` without this change.

Verified on v1.49.0 with this change: `lodestar bootnode` on hoodi with `LODESTAR_Z_NODE_POOL_CAPACITY=0` starts, uses 454 MiB instead of 837 MiB, and logs no pool errors.

This does not change the default. The default case is fixed in lodestar-z by ChainSafe/lodestar-z#648 (pool created on first use), which is not in a stable lodestar-z release yet.

Closes #10225

title: fix: reject checkpoint sync state with mismatching fork
body:
Follow-up to #10200. Checkpoint sync states are now decoded using the local config's fork at the state slot, so the `Eth-Consensus-Version` response header was no longer read. Servers omitting the header were accepted, and a server on a different fork schedule failed with an unclear `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary` error.

- require the `Eth-Consensus-Version` header again and reject the state if it does not match the fork local config expects at that slot
- add the expected fork and slot to `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary` errors, to hint at a fork or network mismatch for sources without a header

Tested by running `initBeaconState` from before #10200 (3579e999b5), current unstable and this branch against a local LevelDB, state files and a mock checkpoint sync server.

Fork schedule skew, local node and server disagree on `FULU_FORK_EPOCH`, empty db, state at epoch 500:

| | server behind (serves electra, local expects fulu) | server ahead (serves fulu, local expects electra) |
|---|---|---|
| before #10200 | accepted and persisted, every restart then fails with `First offset must equal to fixedEnd` | `State current fork version 0x06000000 not equal to current config 0x05000000` |
| unstable | `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary from checkpointSyncUrl` | same |
| this PR | `Checkpoint sync server returned electra state at slot 16000 but local config expects fulu` | `Checkpoint sync server returned fulu state at slot 16000 but local config expects electra` |

`assertAnchorStateForkMatchesConfig` does not catch this case. On unstable the weak subjectivity byte scan fails before it runs, and before #10200 a server that had not activated the fork yet passed it since the state's own fork field is consistent. For sources without a header, e.g. `--checkpointState`, this PR reports `Cannot extract weak subjectivity summary from checkpoint file, expected fulu state at slot 16000, possible fork or network mismatch`.

Server omitting `Eth-Consensus-Version`: rejected before #10200, accepted on unstable, rejected again with this PR.

Full matrix of 15 db states (empty, within or outside weak subjectivity period, ahead of checkpoint, genesis only, corrupt, other network, persisted checkpoint states) x 57 flag combinations (`checkpointState`, `checkpointSyncUrl`, `unsafeCheckpointState`, `lastPersistedCheckpointState`, `wssCheckpoint`, `forceCheckpointSync`, `ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck`, genesis) = 855 scenarios, comparing anchor state, `isFinalized`, db writes and errors:

- vs unstable, only the 9 missing header scenarios differ
- vs before #10200, the remaining differences are the intended ones from #10200: `ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` no longer bypasses a `wssCheckpoint` mismatch (24), a corrupt archived state no longer blocks checkpoint sync (30), and the genesis block is no longer re-persisted from a db at slot 0 (8, db writes only)
author: nflaig

title: perf: hoist weak-subjectivity staleness check before anchor state load
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #10227 ([review comment](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10227#issuecomment-5926570942)).

The checkpoint weak-subjectivity staleness check lives in `validate(state)`,
which runs **after** the anchor state has been deserialized into a
`BeaconStateView`. When a checkpoint is stale (outside the weak subjectivity
period and `--ignoreWeakSubjectivityCheck` is not set) we build the full state
— and reserve pubkey-cache capacity for it — only to immediately throw
`STALE_CHECKPOINT` and discard it.

The staleness check is derived purely from the state **bytes** (the weak
subjectivity summary), so it does not need the deserialized state.

## Description

Add a `validateBeforeLoad()` step to `StateInitialization` and call it at the
top of `executeStateInitialization`, before `createBeaconStateView`:

- **checkpoint** source: the weak-subjectivity / `STALE_CHECKPOINT` check moves
  into `validateBeforeLoad()`. `validate(state)` keeps the checks that require
  the deserialized state (supplied-checkpoint match, anchor fork match, logging).
- **genesis** source: no-op — genesis is never rejected for staleness.
- **archived (db)** source: no-op — db staleness only warns, it does not gate
  loading.

A stale checkpoint now fails fast without building the state or reserving
pubkey-cache capacity.

Note: the supplied-checkpoint match (`--wssCheckpoint`) still needs the built
state, so it stays in `validate`. For a stale checkpoint that is also outside
the WS period, `STALE_CHECKPOINT` is now surfaced before the checkpoint-mismatch
error (previously the order was reversed); both indicate a bad checkpoint source.

## Tests

Adds `packages/cli/test/unit/cmds/checkpointState.test.ts` asserting that a
stale checkpoint throws `STALE_CHECKPOINT` from `validateBeforeLoad()` and that
`createBeaconStateView`, `getValidatorCountFromStateBytes`, and
`pubkeyCache.ensureCapacity` are **not** called — plus the ignore-WS and
within-period paths.

title: fix: fall back to db and check fork for unfinalized checkpoint states
body:
When `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` is set but no checkpoint state was persisted, startup falls back to genesis even if the db holds an archived state. That means syncing from genesis and writing the genesis state into a db that already has later states. States loaded via `--unsafeCheckpointState` or `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` also skip the anchor state fork version check that finalized sources get, so a state from another network is accepted.

- fall back to the archived db state instead of genesis if no unfinalized checkpoint state is found, same as if no checkpoint source was set
- check the anchor state fork version for unfinalized sources too

Behavior changes:

- stale db + `--lastPersistedCheckpointState` with nothing persisted resumes from the db with the usual stale state warning instead of starting from genesis, and no longer needs a genesis file
- if that db state is corrupt, startup now fails on it like it does without checkpoint flags, instead of silently starting from genesis
- an unfinalized checkpoint state whose fork version does not match the config is rejected with `State current fork version ... not equal to current config ...`

Verified with the startup matrix from #10228 (855 scenarios), only these cases change.

title: test: follow current head slot in sync waits
body:
## Motivation

The multifork simulation can time out while waiting for a syncing node even though that node has moved past the requested slot. `waitForHead` captures the first head event's slot and keeps checking it on every later event. If that first event is too early and the requested root was already imported, neither success condition can fire.

This showed up in #9979's [failed simulation](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/35157369708/job/109995673162). The node emitted later heads but the wait kept comparing slot 17 against slot 23.

## Changes

Check the current event's slot instead. Keep the existing exact-root success path and listener cleanup. No production code or timeout values change.

## Testing

- Five local regression probes passed, covering later slots, the exact-root path, node isolation and listener cleanup. The probes are kept outside the PR, following the repository's guidance for simulation utilities.
- Full local Docker multifork simulation rerun on 3 October passed using the repository's pinned Geth v1.16.7 and Lighthouse unstable-d235f2c images.
- Ordinary CLI type-check, changed-file Biome and diff checks passed.

This fix is separate from #9979, whose updated branch passed the simulation without it and has now merged. The earlier failed run motivated the investigation, but this PR is not needed to unblock bid publication.

Local simulation success is not a claim that hosted CI or the complete Gloas Builder lifecycle has passed.

title: fix(api): serve PTC duties across the Gloas fork boundary
body:
## Problem

`getPtcDuties` validates the **requested** epoch's fork (`isForkPostGloas`) but then fetches the head state at the **current** epoch (`getHeadStateAtCurrentEpoch`) and rejects it with a `400` when that state is not yet post-Gloas:

```ts
const state = await chain.getHeadStateAtCurrentEpoch(RegenCaller.getDuties);
if (!isStatePostGloas(state)) {
  throw new ApiError(400, `PTC duties are not available before Gloas fork=${state.forkName}`);
}
```

A validator client requests next-epoch PTC duties one epoch ahead (normal lookahead, allowed by the `epoch <= currentEpoch + 1` guard). One epoch before the Gloas fork the current head state is still pre-Gloas, so the first PTC duties request across the fork boundary always returns `400` and the **first PTC duty after activation is missed**.

This was surfaced on `glamsterdam-sepsf-1`: Lighthouse and Grandine independently hit the same fork-boundary bug. Grandine shipped a fix by upgrading/preprocessing the state ([grandinetech/grandine#951](https://github.com/grandinetech/grandine/pull/951)); Lighthouse observed a real miss on the first PTC duty after the fork. The sibling attester/proposer duty handlers avoid this because they compute from the shuffling cache (keyed on the decision root) rather than requiring a post-Gloas state object, whereas PTC duties read `state.getEpochPTCs(epoch)` which needs a Gloas state.

## Fix

When the current head state is still pre-Gloas, regen the state at the **requested** (post-Gloas) epoch before computing the committees. `getEpochPTCs` already serves both the current and next epoch from a post-Gloas state, so the fast path (post-fork) is unchanged — the regen only happens during the single epoch before activation, and the requested epoch is bounded to `currentEpoch + 1`, so it advances at most one epoch.

## Testing

New `ptc.test.ts`:
- Fork boundary: head state pre-Gloas (epoch N-1), request epoch N → duties served and the state is regenerated at the requested epoch (previously `400`).
- Fast path: post-Gloas head state → duties served without the regen fallback.
- Still rejects PTC duties requested for a pre-Gloas epoch.

Verified the fork-boundary test fails against `unstable` without the fix (`ApiError { statusCode: 400 }`). `tsc`, `biome`, and the test suite pass.

title: fix: serve PTC duties for the first Gloas epoch before the fork
body:
Validator clients poll PTC duties one epoch ahead, so in the epoch before Gloas they request duties for the first Gloas epoch. The head state at the current epoch is still fulu at that point and `getPtcDuties` returns a 400. The Lodestar VC then only gets the duties at the start of the Gloas epoch, after the duties for the fork slot were already looked up, so all PTC duties of that slot are missed.

This dials a clone of the head state across the fork to serve them. Going through regen like #10238 caches the checkpoint state, and `getHeadState()` then returns it one epoch ahead of the clock until the head changes, which makes `prepareForNextSlot` fail with `EPOCH_CONTEXT_ERROR_PROPOSER_EPOCH_MISMATCH`. The clone costs an epoch transition per request, but only in the epoch before the fork.

Tested on kurtosis, minimal preset with Gloas at epoch 3, 2x lodestar/geth. For #10238 and this PR both beacon nodes were also polled with `getPtcDuties(3)` 2s into every slot of epoch 2.

| | `getPtcDuties(3)` in epoch 2 | PTC votes for slot 24 in block 25 | `prepareForNextSlot` failures in epoch 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| unstable | 400 | 0/16 | 0 |
| #10238 | 200 | 16/16 | 14 |
| this PR | 200 | 16/16 | 0 |

Supersedes #10238

title: fix: do not miss PTC duties in the first Gloas epoch
body:
PTC duties of the first Gloas epoch only exist once the state is upgraded at the fork, so unlike later epochs they can't be polled one epoch ahead. The VC requested them anyway in the last Fulu epoch, which the beacon node rejects with a 400, and only got them from the poll at the start of the Gloas epoch. The PTC task of the fork slot runs at the same time and checks for duties before that poll returns, so all PTC duties of the first Gloas slot were missed.

- don't poll PTC duties before the first Gloas epoch
- at the first Gloas slot, read the duties again after waiting for the payload or the deadline, by then the poll at the start of the epoch has returned. All other slots are unchanged

Tested on kurtosis, minimal preset with Gloas at epoch 3, 2x lodestar/geth with 128 validators. Payload attestation bits for each slot of the first Gloas epoch included in the next block:

| | 24 | 25 | 26 | 27 | 28 | 29 | 30 | 31 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| unstable | 0/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| this PR | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |

On unstable the VCs published 75 of 86 PTC duties in that epoch and logged `Failed to download PTC duties epoch=3` in epoch 2. With this PR, in two runs, they published 80 of 80 and 77 of 77 with no errors. The duties were downloaded 29 to 86ms into the fork slot and the payload became available after 565 to 589ms.

Supersedes #10238 and #10240, which serve the duties from the beacon node by advancing the head state across the fork. That runs an epoch transition and the Gloas upgrade per request, and the result is still speculative since blocks later in the last Fulu epoch can change the committees.

title: fix: evict invalid payload envelopes from the seen cache
body:
A payload envelope is added to its `PayloadEnvelopeInput` once it passes gossip validation, the full verification only runs during import. If the import then fails because the envelope is invalid, the envelope stays in the seen cache until the entry is finalized or evicted by the size cap. By-root sync and range sync both reuse the cached envelope instead of the one they get from peers, so every attempt fails the same way and the node can't import the payload, or any block building on it, even though peers serve a valid envelope.

This can be triggered over gossip since a builder can sign more than one envelope for the same block, e.g. one with a wrong `parent_beacon_block_root` (not part of the gossip checks) followed by the valid one, and over req/resp by a peer serving a modified envelope as in #9660.

This evicts the cache entry when the import fails with a verdict caused by the envelope itself (`INVALID_SIGNATURE`, `ENVELOPE_VERIFICATION_ERROR`, `EXECUTION_ENGINE_INVALID`). Sync then recreates the entry from the block and fetches the envelope from peers again. Execution engine errors and a missing block or state are left alone, those are not caused by the envelope.

- add `SeenPayloadEnvelopeInput.removeInvalid()` with prune reason `invalid`, it is a no-op if the cached entry is not the failed object as that may already be the recreated one
- evict in the `execution_payload` gossip handler, by-root sync and range sync, the latter also logs peer and client of the envelope source
- remove the TODO about invalid payload inputs never leaving memory

The envelope is not replaced in place. A valid envelope arriving on gossip after the eviction is still ignored (`PAYLOAD_ENVELOPE_INPUT_MISSING`) and is fetched by root instead, same for the columns collected for the evicted entry. The API publish path is unchanged.

Tested on a kurtosis devnet (minimal preset, 6s slots, Lodestar without validators, Teku, Lighthouse) where the builder reveals an envelope with a wrong `parent_beacon_block_root` 300ms into the slot and the valid one at 3.5s. Lodestar on top of `glamsterdam-devnet-8` with and without this change:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| cached envelope after failed import | kept | evicted |
| by-root sync | 68 failed attempts reusing the cached envelope | 0 failed attempts |
| payload imported | 6 min 12s later, once the entry hit the cache size cap | 3.3s to 3.7s later, within the slot (3 of 3 slots) |
| head | stuck for 61 slots | never behind |

Closes #9660

title: fix: surface archived envelopes the EL cannot serve
body:
Supersedes #10201 (same change, rebased over #10207 with the review follow-ups folded in). Co-authored with @nflaig.

**Motivation**

An archived header envelope whose body the EL can no longer serve (`nimbus-eth1` returning no block access list for blocks with 0 withdrawals, `reth` after an EL restart on `glamsterdam-devnet-8`) was indistinguishable from an envelope we never had: the chain getters returned `null`, so `GET /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_envelopes/{block_id}` answered `404` and the by-range non-finalized path failed with `SERVER_ERROR`.

**Description**

`BODY_UNAVAILABLE` is added to `EnvelopeReconstructionErrorCode` and carried by the unavailable rebuild miss, like `BODY_ROOT_MISMATCH` already was. `RebuildMiss` collapses to one shape since both variants now carry an error.
`ReconstructMismatchPolicy` → `ReconstructMissPolicy`: "throw" for REST / single lookups, "omit" for by-root. The omit path now logs an unavailable miss at debug the same way the by-range generator does, so a partial by-root response leaves a trace.
REST: `BODY_UNAVAILABLE` maps to 503 alongside `ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE` (the data exists, our EL can't serve it right now — clients retry or ask another node); a body root mismatch stays 500; 404 only for an envelope that was never archived.
By-range: the non-finalized path now ends short / `RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE` on an unservable envelope, matching the finalized path, instead of `SERVER_ERROR`.

Metrics are unchanged (`beacon_payload_envelope_reconstruction_envelopes_total{result="unavailable"}` still counts these).
author: markolazic01

title: fix: prevent range sync stall when rate limit backoff expires
body:
When a peer rate limits us, `SyncChain` arms a timer for the end of the backoff. The timer callback triggered the batch downloader and then rescheduled the timer, each reading the clock on its own. If the backoff expires between the two reads, the downloader still skips the peer and the reschedule then drops it as expired without arming a new timer. Nothing triggers the downloader again, so with a single usable peer the chain stalls until another peer or batch event comes in.

This is also why `Should retry a rate-limited peer after metadata backoff expires` times out in CI from time to time.

- reschedule before triggering the downloader in the timer callback
- add a test where the backoff expires while the timer callback runs
author: nflaig

title: fix: prevent unknown block sync stall when rate limit backoff expires
body:
Same kind of lost wakeup as #10249, this time in `BlockInputSync`. A by-root download whose eligible peers are all in rate limit backoff is deferred and relies on the backoff timer to retry it. Expired backoffs are dropped whenever they are read, and peer selection, the rate limit check and the rescheduling each read the clock on their own. If the backoff expires between two of those reads, either peer selection skips the peer while the rate limit check already sees no backoff, so the download fails as no peer available, or the download is deferred while rescheduling finds nothing left to wait for and arms no timer, or only one for a later backoff of another peer. The block or payload then stays pending until some other event or that later timer triggers the search.

- use the same time for peer selection and the rate limit check
- if the backoff a deferred download was waiting for has expired, trigger the search right away instead of dropping or delaying the retry, for both block and payload downloads
- add tests that move the backoff expiry across every clock read around the retry timer
author: nflaig

title: fix: reject range sync envelopes whose block hash does not match the bid
body:
Range sync caches an envelope served by a peer as soon as its `beacon_block_root` matches the block at that slot, nothing else is checked before `addPayloadEnvelope`. The envelope is only verified when the payload is imported, and #10246 evicts it from the seen cache if that fails. But `assertLinearChainSegment` runs first and tracks the execution chain by the envelope's `payload.block_hash`. An envelope with a wrong hash makes the next block look like it builds on an unknown payload, the segment fails with `NON_LINEAR_PAYLOAD_ROOTS` before the import is reached, and the cached envelope is never evicted. Every retry of the batch reuses it and fails the same way, so one peer serving a single bad envelope stalls range sync until the cache entry is evicted by the size cap or finalization, same as #9660. No builder signature is needed for this.

This rejects the envelope while validating the response if `payload.block_hash` does not match the block's bid, so it never reaches the cache, and the peer is reported like for a wrong `beacon_block_root`. The same check applies to the dangling parent envelope. There a wrong hash does not break linearity, it fails at import, but the eviction then removes the parent's cache entry which range sync cannot recreate, and every retry fails on the missing entry. Gossip and by-root sync already check the block hash before caching.

- add `INVALID_ENVELOPE_BLOCK_HASH` to `validateEnvelopesByRangeResponse`, checked against the bid of the downloaded or cached block
- carry the parent bid's `block_hash` in `ParentPayloadCommitments` for the dangling parent envelope
author: nflaig

title: fix: retry rate-limited peers after a sync chain restart
body:
`stopSyncing()` clears the rate limit backoff timer but `startSyncing()` only triggers the batch downloader and never arms it again. If a chain is stopped and restarted while a peer is still in backoff, the peer is skipped on restart and nothing retries it once the backoff ends. If all usable peers of the chain are in backoff at that point, the chain stays idle until another peer or batch event comes in.

This re-arms the timer when the chain is started and adds a test for it. Related to #10249 but independent of it.

title: chore: update stale pruning note in payload envelope seen cache doc

title: fix: report builder circuit breaker as block selection reason
body:
While the builder circuit breaker is active, `produceBlockV4` neither requests builder API bids nor reads the bid pool, but the local block selection is logged and counted as `builder_no_bid` with the error `No builder bid available`. If the execution engine also flags the builder override, it is reported as suspected censorship even though no bid was considered.

Selecting the local block because of the circuit breaker now has its own reason `builder_circuit_breaker`, used in the log and in `beacon_block_production_selection_results_total`.

Before

```
Selected local block: no builder bid block produced reason=builder_no_bid, slot=368273, ..., circuitBreakerActive=true, ..., error=No builder bid available
```

After

```
Selected local block: builder circuit breaker is active reason=builder_circuit_breaker, slot=368273, ..., circuitBreakerActive=true, ...
```

title: feat: add endpoint to get proposer preferences
body:
Proposer preferences are broadcast once per epoch and the beacon node keeps the ones it has seen to validate bids, but there is no way to read them. A builder that subscribes to the `proposer_preferences` event after they were broadcast, for example after a restart, can't bid for the affected slots until the next broadcast, which can take up to two epochs.

This adds `GET /eth/v1/beacon/proposer_preferences` which returns the signed proposer preferences known by the node, optionally filtered by `slot`. It lives next to the other endpoints for off-chain Gloas messages (`execution_payload_bids`, `execution_payload_envelopes`) and not under `/pool`, which holds operations that are included in blocks.

The endpoint is specified in ethereum/beacon-APIs#659, it is ignored in the spec conformance test until the pinned spec version includes it.

title: fix: honor group validator statuses when filtering by ids
body:
## Motivation
`POST/GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/validators` accepts Beacon API group statuses (`active`, `pending`, `exited`, `withdrawal`) in addition to fine-grained statuses. When both `ids` and `statuses` were provided, Lodestar compared against fine-grained status strings only, so `statuses: ["active"]` never matched `active_ongoing` / `active_exiting` / `active_slashed`.

- Use it on the `ids` + `statuses` path in `getStateValidators` (covers GET and POST)
- Widen request types with `ValidatorStatusFilter = ValidatorStatus | GeneralValidatorStatus`
- Add unit tests for group and fine-grained filters with `ids`

title: fix: stop scoped sync committee polls from clobbering cached duties
body:
**Motivation**

`SyncCommitteeDutiesService.pollSyncCommitteesForEpoch` stored the result of a poll by replacing the whole duty map for the period, even though the poll only queried the indices it was given. `runDutiesTasks` runs a full poll and an incremental poll for newly discovered indices at the same time. If the incremental poll lands last, the period map is replaced by duties for just the new indices, or by an empty map when a new validator is not in the sync committee, and every other validator's duties are dropped until the next full poll. This is the sync committee sibling of the attester and PTC duty bugs fixed in #10213 and #10197, with a different mechanism, tracked in #10210.

**Description**

Merge the poll result into the cached period map, scoped to the indices the poll requested: overwrite the entries it returned, delete the entries for requested indices it did not return, and keep all other entries. A full poll requests every local index, so it stays authoritative for the whole period and the redundant duties behavior from #3572 is unchanged.

Closes #10210

**Steps to test a change**

Added a regression test in `syncCommitteDuties.test.ts` that drives a full poll, an empty incremental poll, a merging incremental poll, and a final authoritative full poll through `pollSyncCommitteesForEpoch`. It fails on the previous code (the empty incremental poll wipes the cached duty) and passes with this change.

Targeted checks run locally on Node 24: the full sync committee duties unit file passes (6/6, including the existing #3572 test), `check-types` for `@lodestar/validator` passes, and Biome reports no issues on the changed files. Dependencies were installed with lifecycle scripts disabled in my sandbox, so no native module builds ran locally; CI covers the standard environment.

> This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Muse). The bug analysis is from #10210, and the fix and regression test were written and verified locally with the targeted unit tests above.

Submitted by Kshot3000 (GitHub), @kshot9000 on X. No bounty is attached to #10210; the fix is offered freely.

title: fix: request the whole range sync batch again after a processing error
body:
After a processing error a range sync batch drops its downloaded blocks but keeps `requests`, which after a partial download only cover the missing data (e.g. `cols=[101]`, no blocks request). Every retry then fails with `MISSING_BLOCKS_RESPONSE` ("No blocks in data request slot range to validate data response against"), the peers end up in `failedDownloadPeers` / `hasPeerSucceededCurrentRequest`, `bestPeerToRetryBatch` returns nothing and the batch stays `AwaitingDownload` without ever reaching `MAX_BATCH_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS`, so the chain is never torn down and sync silently stops (seen on focil-devnet-0 for 3 days, zero `beacon_blocks_by_range` sent).

- reset `requests` to a fresh request of the whole batch whenever the downloaded blocks are dropped (`onProcessingError`, `onExecutionEngineError`)
- add a regression test for both paths after a partial column download

title: fix: inherit gloas block execution status from the parent variant it builds on
body:
Gloas blocks inherited the execution status of the parent's default (PENDING) variant instead of the variant their bid builds on. If the EL answered SYNCING/ACCEPTED for the parent payload, the child was still imported as VALID and `onBlock` propagated VALID to the parent's FULL variant, without the EL ever validating that payload. This also bypasses the optimistic head check in block production.

- inherit from the parent variant matching the bid's `parentBlockHash` (`getBlockHexAndBlockHash`), same lookup already used further down in `importBlock`
- once a payload turns VALID, validate all PENDING/EMPTY variants building on it (same `executionPayloadBlockHash`), not only the chain the validation walked up, so siblings and blocks on a sibling's EMPTY variant don't stay optimistic
- add `importBlock` and protoArray unit tests


Behavior change: a gloas block whose bid builds on a payload the EL answered SYNCING or ACCEPTED for is now imported as SYNCING instead of VALID. Such blocks are reported as execution optimistic, block production refuses to build on them (same as pre-gloas), and the parent payload is no longer marked VALID until the EL validates it or a descendant payload. In the other direction, once a payload turns VALID every block building on it is validated, not only the chain the validation walked up.

title: fix: do not attest to an optimistic head
body:
`produceAttestationData` only checked the execution status of the target, so a node with an optimistic head still attested as long as the target was validated, although an [optimistic validator must not attest](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/bellatrix/optimistic-sync.md#attesting). Post-gloas this also voted `index=1` for a FULL head whose payload the EL had not validated.

- check the head block voted for, post-gloas the variant voted for: PENDING for same-slot votes, otherwise the canonical variant signaled by `index`
- keep the target check
- add tests for an optimistic head with a validated target, pre- and post-gloas

title: fix: serve finalized state by root from checkpoint cache
body:
**Motivation**

checkpointz with only Lodestar upstreams fails on every finality update. It fetches the finalized block, then `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{block.state_root}`, and Lodestar returns `500 REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE`. The same state works by slot or as `finalized`.

Repro on mainnet (v1.49.0):

```
GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/finalized/root  -> 0x45a0…aa44, finalized: true
GET /eth/v1/beacon/states/0x45a0…aa44/fork -> {"code":500,"message":"REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE"}
```

**Description**

After pruning, the finalized block is the fork choice anchor and has no ancestors. `regen.getState` only checks the checkpoint state cache for ancestors, so once the block's post-state has been evicted from the block state cache there is no seed state and it throws.

`getStateByStateRoot` now checks whether the requested root is the finalized block's state root and, if so, serves the finalized checkpoint state from memory if the finalized block is at the epoch start slot (the checkpoint state is then the block post-state). With a skipped boundary slot, the checkpoint state is the advanced state with a different root, so it falls through to the existing path unchanged.

**Testing**

Local `dev` node (minimal preset, 8 interop validators, `--chain.maxBlockStates 4` so the finalized block's post-state gets evicted the way it does on mainnet), requesting the finalized block's state root after each finality update:
- v1.49.0: `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{root}/fork` and `/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{root}` both return `500 REGEN_ERROR_NO_SEED_STATE`
- this branch: both return 200 with `finalized: true`, across 4 consecutive finality updates (finalized epochs 2, 3, 4, 6)

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- genesis state by root still fails (`STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE`)
- `StateArchiveRepository` only writes the root index in `put`, but archival and startup use `putBinary`, so archived states can't be looked up by root

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Analysis and implementation by GPT-6.1 Sol, reviewed by me (lodekeeper, an AI agent).

title: feat: emit PTC quorum changes from fork choice
body:
**Motivation**

Refresh of #9284. That PR was closed in favor of #9387, which landed the blob data availability vote tracking and `shouldBuildOnFull()`. The part that never landed is making the PTC outcome observable: knowing when the committee reaches a majority that a payload was present or absent, or that blob data was available or not.

**Description**

- `ProtoArray.getPtcQuorum(root)` derives the per-field majority (`true`, `false`, or `null` while neither side has one) from the existing vote bitarrays. It reads the raw tallies and does not gate on the payload being locally available, unlike `isPayloadTimely()`, so it reflects what the committee said rather than what this node holds.
- `ForkChoice.notifyPtcMessages()` compares the quorum state before and after applying the votes. On a change it increments `beacon_fork_choice_ptc_quorum_total{vote, result}`, logs at verbose, and calls the new optional `IForkChoiceStore.notifyPtcQuorum()`.
- The beacon node wires that callback to a new `ChainEvent.forkChoicePtcQuorum`, following the existing `onJustified` / `onFinalized` / `onFastConfirmation` pattern.

**Design notes vs. #9284**

- One event instead of two (re @nflaig's question on the original). The event carries the full `{payloadPresent, blobDataAvailable}` snapshot, so a block-level PTC attestation that crosses both thresholds at once yields a single notification, and a consumer interested in one field just reads it.
- No yea/nay vocabulary (re @ensi321). Fields are named after `PayloadAttestationData`.
- No cached quorum flag. Votes overwrite per spec, so a majority can be lost when a member re-votes. A before/after comparison reports every real transition and adds no per-block state to initialize or prune.
- The `shouldExtendPayload` fix and the `blobDataAvailable` threading from the original are already on `unstable` via #9387 and #9416.

title: fix: serve archived genesis state by root
body:
**Motivation**

checkpointz v0.32.0 fetches every state by state root, including genesis (its genesis loop retries `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}` every 15s). Lodestar returns `500 REGEN_ERROR_STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE` for it, while the same state by `genesis` / slot 0 works. See ethpandaops/checkpointz#266.

**Description**

Genesis is pruned from fork choice, so regen can't find it, and the state archive can't look it up by root because archived states are written without the root index. Nodes initialized from genesis still have it in the state archive at slot 0.

`getStateByStateRoot` now looks up the genesis block's state root once (block archive slot 0, cached) and, if the requested root matches, serves the archived slot 0 state directly. It's a plain DB read, so it doesn't need `--serveHistoricalState`. Otherwise it falls through unchanged. Checkpoint-synced nodes don't have the genesis state, so nothing changes for them.

**Testing**

Local `dev` node (minimal preset, initialized from genesis), after the first finalizations:
- unstable: `/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}` and `/eth/v1/beacon/states/{genesis_state_root}/fork` return `500 REGEN_ERROR_STATE_NOT_IN_FORKCHOICE`
- this branch: both return 200, and the SSZ bytes are identical to `/eth/v2/debug/beacon/states/genesis`

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Analysis and first implementation by GPT-6.1 Sol, simplified and reviewed by me (lodekeeper, an AI agent).

title: fix: use runtime genesis metadata for ephemery
body:
**Motivation**

Ephemery’s genesis validators root changes between iterations, but its static network metadata advertises a zero root. Slashing-protection import/export therefore uses the wrong chain identity. Light-client update serialization also reconstructs fork digests instead of preserving a supplied runtime beacon config.

**Description**

- Mark Ephemery’s static genesis validators root as unknown and fetch the live root from the beacon API.
- Honor `--force` for HTTP errors and thrown request failures.
- Preserve supplied runtime beacon configs for SSZ light-client update ranges.
- Update the Web3Signer test helper for nullable static roots.
- Add regression tests for live-root lookup, failure handling, and runtime fork digests.

Related to #6050 and re-authors the remaining genesis metadata fixes from closed PR #9204. This PR does not close the full issue: automatic reset, genesis generation, and process coordination remain outside its scope.

Validation on WSL with Node 24.21.0:

title: fix: verify inclusion list signatures without batching
body:
Gossip inclusion list signatures are verified with `batchable: true`. The BLS pool holds batchable sets until more than 32 are buffered or 100ms passes. A slot only has 16 inclusion lists, so the batch never fills and every IL waits the full 100ms before it is accepted, forwarded to peers, stored, and emitted on the `inclusion_list` event stream. On a FOCIL devnet this makes Lodestar consistently about 100ms later than every other client, and each Lodestar hop adds that delay to gossip propagation ahead of the 8s IL deadline. The `batchable` docs say it is only for non-time-critical objects. This verifies IL signatures unbatched. `proposerPreferences.ts` uses the same setting and may deserve the same treatment.

### Proof

Kurtosis network with 11 nodes (Lighthouse, Lodestar, Teku × Besu, Ethrex, Nethermind, Reth), Gloas at genesis, Heze at epoch 1. Lag is the delay between a client emitting the `inclusion_list` event and the first client to see the same list, as recorded by Dora. Validation time is `beacon_inclusion_lists_validation_time_seconds{source="gossip"}` on one Lodestar node.

| | before (`batchable: true`) | after (`batchable: false`) |
|---|---|---|
| Lodestar median lag | **111ms** | **14ms** |
| Lodestar p90 lag | 285ms | 138ms |
| Gossip IL validation time, average | **106ms** (84.3s / 794) | **9ms** (5.3s / 587) |
| Lighthouse / Teku median lag (control) | 9ms / 10ms | 12ms / 16ms |

title: fix: preserve IPv6 dial candidates from dual-stack discovered ENRs
body:
### Summary

Fixes #10256.

When a discovered ENR advertises both IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints, `PeerDiscovery` only passed the IPv4 multiaddr per transport to the peer store. `ENR.getLocationMultiaddr("tcp")` returns the IPv4 location when both families exist, and `"quic"` does the same, so a dual-stack peer got no IPv6 dial candidate from discovery and was undialable when its IPv4 endpoint was unreachable.

### Changes

- `onDiscoveredENR` now queries each family explicitly (`tcp4`/`tcp6`, `quic4`/`quic6`) and keeps every advertised multiaddr.
- `CachedENR` and `handleDiscoveredPeer` carry `multiaddrsTCP` / `multiaddrsQUIC` arrays instead of a single optional multiaddr per transport, and `dialPeer` merges all of them into the peer store.
- The libp2p `peer:discovery` path now keeps all matching multiaddrs per transport instead of only the first one, for the same reason.

### Testing

New regression test in `discover.test.ts`: a dual-stack boot ENR (IPv4 and IPv6, TCP and QUIC) is processed at construction, then dialed via `discoverPeers`, and the test asserts all four multiaddrs reach `peerStore.merge`.

- Before the fix: the test fails, only the two IPv4 multiaddrs are merged (`expected [ ...(2) ] to include '/ip6/::1/tcp/9000'`).
- After the fix: `vitest run --project unit test/unit/network/peers/discover.test.ts` passes 3/3, and Biome check is clean on both changed files.
- Full package `check-types` was not run to green locally because the workspace dependencies are not built in my sandbox (pre-existing module resolution errors in unrelated files, none in `discover.ts`). The changed expressions were type-checked in isolation under strict mode. CI is authoritative.

title: fix: deduplicate incomplete payload sync at the payload deadline
body:
**Motivation**

Gloas columns currently trigger payload sync at the block deadline and arm one timer per column. An envelope with no arriving columns never triggers that fallback. Duplicate notifications and overlapping async work can restart an in-flight payload fetch or import.

**Description**

Schedule one incomplete-payload notification per input at the configured payload deadline for the input slot's fork, from either envelope or column gossip. Skip inputs that complete or leave the cache while waiting. Track scheduled inputs in a WeakSet so notification bookkeeping does not retain them.

title: test: fix waitForHead race in sim sync assertions
body:
**Motivation**

`Multifork sim test` on unstable hit the 672s simulation deadline in [run 37526851304 (attempt 1)](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/37526851304/job/112486568374). It was stuck in `assertCheckpointSync` on `Waiting for head=0xd388… slot=23 on node=checkpoint-sync-node` for over 5 minutes. The node itself was healthy: it synced in about 1s and followed the chain to slot 111.

The cause is a race in `waitForHead`. It latched `firstHeadEventSlot` from the first head event, then waited for either that slot to be >= the target slot or for the exact target root. The checkpoint-sync node log in the run artifact shows the bad ordering:

- `Eph 4/2 1.302`: target block slot 16 (`0xd388…`) imported
- `Eph 4/2 1.373`: tracker SSE `eventstream` request arrives
- `Eph 4/2 1.396`–`1.408`: slots 17–23 imported

The first observed head event was slot 17, which is below 23. The target root had been imported before the subscription and was never emitted again, so the promise never resolved. The attempt 2 rerun passed because the subscription timing happened to fall outside that window.

**Description**

Resolve `waitForHead` on any head event at or past the target slot, or on the exact target root. This keeps the semantics the existing fast-sync branch already relied on, but no longer depends on when the event stream connects. Range and checkpoint sync still wait for `isSyncing=false` in parallel, and unknown-block sync already checks the exact block via `getBlockHeader` after `waitForHead`.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Investigated and authored by lodekeeper (AI contributor), using the run artifact logs. Reviewed by a second model, which also replayed the old and new logic deterministically: the old logic hangs on events 17–23 with target 23, and the new logic resolves at 23.

title: fix(validator): do not leave state behind a rejected interchange import
body:
**Motivation**

The example in the issue no longer reaches the span loop, #9999 rejects `[(12,13), (9,14)]` on the invariant check before anything is written. A file still leaks when the conflict is between its own attestations and the highest target happens to carry the highest source epoch. Over a history of `(10,11)` and `(11,12)`, importing `[(12,30), (13,14), (20,40)]` is rejected on `(13,14)` but leaves all three rows and the spans of `(12,30)` behind, and `(11,31)` is then rejected although it surrounds neither recorded attestation.

**Description**

Span inserts now go through an in-memory buffer that reads through to the store, so intra-file conflicts are still caught by the same code path and nothing is written until the whole file is accepted. I did not put the rows and spans in one `db.batch` as the issue suggests, that would need the service to reach past its repositories into the raw db. Spans are committed before the rows they cover, because spans without rows only ever reject more while rows without spans is the direction that loses protection. #10158 buffered the same way and went stale, its test uses the sequence from the issue body, which passes on `unstable` without the fix.

Closes #10001

title: fix: serialize attestation slashing protection checks per validator
body:
This is not a security issue. The overlap below needs `--distributed`, which is only used by DVT clusters (e.g. Charon). There the validator client holds a key share, not the full key, and the DVT middleware aggregates signatures, so the validator client cannot produce a slashable message on its own. Running full keystores with `--distributed` makes no sense and nobody does it. The pre-electra case needs a beacon node serving two duties for one key, and every live network is past electra. The race is still worth fixing.

The attestation slashing protection check and the write recording the attestation are separate steps, two checks for the same key running at the same time both pass before either one is recorded. The validator clock only waits for a slot's attestation task when skipping slots is allowed, with `--distributed` (`clock.skipSlots=false`) slot `S+1` starts while slot `S` is still waiting for attestation data. A beacon node that serves two duties for one key in an epoch under different validator indices and releases both responses together gets two signatures with the same target epoch. Before electra the default config is exposed as well, two duties with different committee indices sign different roots in the same slot. Attestation counterpart of #10142.

- serialize attestation checks and writes per validator, including interchange imports
- checks for keys covered by a running interchange import wait until the import is done, imports run one after another, this applies to block proposals as well
- add regression coverage for overlapping checks and imports

Without the serialization the overlap tests fail, a double vote and a surround vote are accepted next to the attestation they conflict with.
author: nflaig

title: fix: cancel req/resp bridge iterators when the consumer returns early
body:
With the network worker (default), req/resp iterators are bridged between threads as events. If the consumer stops early (`break`, `return()`), only its local pending entry is dropped. The other thread is never told and keeps iterating its source to the end, posting every item across the thread boundary just to be dropped on arrival.

For outgoing requests the main thread stops after `maxResponses` chunks or on the first invalid chunk, but the worker keeps decompressing and copying whatever the peer sends until the stream is closed or `RESP_TIMEOUT` (10s) fires. The early exit path in `sendRequest` (close, `closeRead`, scheduled abort) only runs without the worker. For incoming requests the main thread handler keeps reading from the db after the remote reset the stream.

- the caller's `return()` emits a cancel event for the request id
- the handler keeps the iterator per request id and calls `return()` on it, this runs the source's `finally` and for outgoing requests the graceful close in `sendRequest`
- at most one more item is produced after the cancel since `return()` queues behind the in-flight `next()`

This also releases the self rate limiter slot and roundtrip timer of an outgoing request once the consumer is done instead of when the stream ends.
author: nflaig

title: fix: record block timeliness after data availability
body:
Fork choice derives the block delay from the gossip arrival time of the block body. A block whose blobs or data columns complete after the attestation deadline is still marked timely, it gets proposer boost and the next proposer does not reorg it, while attesters that had to wait for the data voted for the parent. The spec checks data availability before `record_block_timeliness`, the store time it records is the time the block became available. Lighthouse and Prysm take the delay at fork choice insertion, Teku moved to the data availability time in Consensys/teku#11080.

- derive the receive delay from the completion time of the block input, the latest seen time of the block and its sidecars regardless of the order they were cached in, this stays the body arrival time for blocks without blob data and for gloas where DA happens on the payload envelope
- never let the receive delay drop below the caller's processing time, unknown block sync holds blocks past the proposer boost window and relies on it
- keep the completion time of a columns block input once set, columns arriving past the reconstruction threshold used to push it later
- fix the units of `lodestar_gossip_block_verified_to_blobs_availability_time` which always observed 0

Closes #10262

title: feat: honor executiononly builder selection post-gloas
body:
**Motivation**

There is no way to opt out of p2p bids post-Gloas. `--builder.selection executiononly` is currently normalized to `executionalways` (boost factor 0), which prefers the local payload but still falls back to a p2p or builder API bid if local production fails or is delayed.

**Description**

Revive `executiononly` post-Gloas as strictly local-only, matching its pre-Gloas semantics:

- The validator client no longer maps `executiononly` to `executionalways` post-Gloas.
- When producing a Gloas block with `executiononly`, the validator client sends no builder entries and sets the top-level `minBid` (which only applies to p2p bids) to `2**64 - 1`. The beacon node therefore never selects a bid. If the local payload fails or is not produced in time, the block is proposed without an execution payload instead of using a bid (requires the dummy bid fallback that is implemented separately, without it the proposal is missed).
- As a safety net, the validator client refuses to sign a block that commits to a non-self-build bid when `executiononly` is configured, same as the pre-Gloas check on `executionPayloadSource`.
- The validator client refuses to start if `executiononly` is configured together with `builders` in the same config (CLI args / default config or a per-key config).
- `executiononly` validators also skip builder preferences submission (existing check that was previously unreachable post-Gloas).

A per-key builder boost factor set through the standard builder config (keymanager API / proposer settings) still takes precedence over the selection alias, as before.

Operators who want to keep builder API bids but drop p2p bids can still do that with a high global `minBid` and per-builder `min_bid` overrides.
author: lodekeeper

title: feat: produce gloas block without execution payload if none is available in time
body:
**Motivation**

Post-Gloas, block production currently fails if neither the local payload nor a builder bid block is available, e.g. the execution client fails or is too slow while the builder circuit breaker is active, no bids are available, or `executiononly` is used (#10309). This results in a missed proposal even though the beacon block itself could still be proposed on time.

**Description**

If neither the local block nor a builder bid block is produced by the block production cutoff (2s into the slot), or both fail before it, the beacon node now produces the block with an empty self-build bid instead of failing block production.

- The empty bid is a self-build bid with `value = 0`, the infinity signature, no blob commitments and a zero `block_hash` (the spec only requires it to differ from `parent_block_hash`). `parent_block_hash`, `prev_randao` etc. are derived the same way as for a regular self-build bid. The block body is assembled through the existing builder bid path, so no execution client call is required.
- The execution payload is never revealed, so the slot ends up without an execution payload, but the beacon block (attestations, etc.) still gets included.
- The empty bid block is only produced once it's required, i.e. after the cutoff or once both the local and the bid block failed. If the local or a bid block is produced first, it's selected as before.
- `produceBlockV4` returns the block without contents (`executionPayloadIncluded=false`) even if `include_payload` is requested.
- The validator client detects a self-build bid with a zero `block_hash` and skips revealing the execution payload envelope.
- New selection reason `no_payload` in metrics / logs.

Note: our own block without payload counts as an empty slot for the builder circuit breaker, same as any other slot without payload.
author: lodekeeper

title: fix: recreate the dangling parent payload entry in range sync
body:
The first batch of a sync chain downloads the payload of the block before the batch by root if its first block builds on that block's FULL variant, that is the head when the chain was created, in practice the checkpoint anchor when the epoch-start slot was skipped. The envelope is attached to the parent's existing `PayloadEnvelopeInput`. If it is invalid in a way only the import catches (bad signature, wrong `prev_randao`, ...), #10246 evicts that entry and nothing recreates it: the anchor entry is seeded once from the anchor state, its block body is not in the db, and `cacheByRangeResponses` only creates entries for blocks of the batch. Every retry then fails with a generic `Missing PayloadEnvelopeInput` error, which is not attributed to the peer, until `MAX_DOWNLOAD_ATTEMPTS` tears the sync chain down, and the next chain starts with the same first batch. The node stays stuck until a restart. The cache cap evicts the same entry without any invalid envelope once the look-ahead batches fill it up.

The sync chain now captures the head block (root, slot, proposer and bid) instead of only its bid, which is enough to recreate the entry via `addFromBid` when it is missing. Carrying the head root also lets `shouldDownloadParentEnvelope` require the first block's `parent_root` to match it, so the parent payload is only ever validated against the bid of the block it belongs to.

- recreate the dangling parent `PayloadEnvelopeInput` from the head's bid if it is missing from the seen cache
- only download the parent payload if the first block's `parent_root` is the head block
- reject a parent envelope whose `payload.slot_number` does not match the parent's slot, it was keyed under the wrong slot and failed the batch with `PARENT_PAYLOAD_UNKNOWN` instead
- validate the parent's columns against the parent's slot instead of the slot claimed by the first column

Follow-up to #10251.

title: feat: implement FOCIL EIP-7805 in heze
body:
Implements FOCIL (EIP-7805) for Heze per consensus-specs v1.7.0-beta.4 ([`specs/heze`](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/tree/v1.7.0-beta.4/specs/heze)) and the engine API [`bogota.md`](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/bogota.md) (`engine_getInclusionListV1`, `engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV5`, `engine_newPayloadV6`).

- Inclusion list gossip topic, validation and `InclusionListsByIndices` req/resp responder, with a store that tracks timely vs untimely lists and the two-message equivocation rule
- Inclusion list transactions passed as payload attributes, the payload id cache misses when the set changes
- Inclusion list verdict from `newPayload` recorded per block in proto array, `should_extend_payload` builds on the EMPTY variant of an unsatisfied payload, verdict exposed in the fork choice dump
- Bid `inclusion_list_bits` validated against the local timely lists on gossip, the beacon API and the builder API, bids received before the inclusion list deadline of `bid.slot - 1` are ignored
- Validator API routes for inclusion list duties, production and publishing, plus the `inclusion_list` event
- Validator client inclusion list duties and service, lists are built once the slot's payload is imported and published before the deadline

Deviation from beta.4: bid bits are checked against timely lists only, also by the proposer (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5741). `INCLUSION_LIST_DUE_BPS` stays at 6667 until https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5727 is released.

title: chore: update consensus specs to v1.7.0-beta.4
body:
**Blocked by #10312 (FOCIL).** This bump skips every Heze spec test, and #10312 un-skips the Heze `on_inclusion_list` and `gossip_inclusion_list` suites, which pass at beta.3 but need the new Heze SSZ shapes at beta.4. Merge FOCIL first, then this PR is rebased and its specrefs regenerated on top.

Update spec tests and specrefs to [v1.7.0-beta.4](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/releases/tag/v1.7.0-beta.4), following the beta.3 bump in #10280.

### Consensus change

ethereum/consensus-specs#5719 moves the Gloas builder pending payment clearing from `process_proposer_slashing` into `slash_validator`. A proposer could previously get itself slashed through an attester slashing first, which made the later proposer slashing invalid and left the builder paying for the equivocated block. Now every slashing of a proposer clears all of its `builder_pending_payments` entries, and the Gloas `process_proposer_slashing` override is gone. This changes Gloas state roots whenever a slashed proposer has a pending payment, so it should ship in a coordinated release with the other clients.

### Heze tests skipped (temporary)

v1.7.0-beta.4 adds EIP-8015 (ethereum/consensus-specs#5655), which removes `eth1_data`, `eth1_data_votes`, `eth1_deposit_index` and `deposit_requests_start_index` from the Heze `BeaconState` and `eth1_data` and `deposits` from the Heze `BeaconBlockBody`, and EIP-8365 (ethereum/consensus-specs#5713). Lodestar does not implement either yet, so no Heze vector carrying a state or a block deserializes. All Heze suites are skipped in `specTestIterator.ts` except `ssz_static` for containers EIP-8015 does not touch. The skip carries a TODO and will be lifted in the EIP-8015 and EIP-8365 PRs. The matching specrefs entries are recorded as exceptions.

### Other changes

- ethereum/consensus-specs#5679 (slashed validators excluded from `calculate_committee_fraction` and `compute_proposer_score`) needs no code: fork choice justified balances and the fast confirmation total active balance already zero slashed validators.
- ethereum/consensus-specs#5710 replaces `SLOT_DURATION_SCHEDULE` with `SLOT_DURATION_MS_EIP8198`; EIP-8198 is not implemented, so the new key joins `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` in the config sync ignore list.
- ethereum/consensus-specs#5721 (inclusion list domain from the list's own slot) is already handled in #10312.
- Removed the stale `process_proposer_slashing#gloas` specref, refreshed the builder README badge.

### Validation

- Gloas `operations/proposer_slashing` and `attester_slashing`, and the new `sanity/blocks` slashing cases (`builder_payment_removed_when_proposer_slashes_itself`, `invalid_proposer_and_attester_slashings_same_validator`, `proposer_and_attester_slashings_partial_overlap`) on both presets.
- Full `sanity`, `fast_confirmation`, `fork_choice` (includes the new `get_head` cases) on minimal: 2,483 passed.
- Heze `ssz_static`: 8,840 passed, state and block containers skipped as intended.
- Config sync e2e test, `check-types` for state-transition, beacon-node and config, biome, prettier, and `ethspecify check` (1,231 refs valid).
- Full fork choice compliance run against the beta.4 comptest vectors: 10,304 passed, 0 failed (about 1h45m locally).

title: feat: disallow new validators with BLS withdrawal credentials in heze
body:
Implements EIP-8365 for heze, see https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5713. Pending deposits that would create a new validator with BLS withdrawal credentials are skipped before signature verification and without a refund, including deposits queued before the fork. title: fix: retry proposer preferences submission on error response
body: The response of `submitProposerPreferences` is not asserted, so an error response is treated as a successful submission and the slots are marked as submitted. A beacon node that rejects the preferences, e.g. because it has not seen the dependent root of the duties yet, leaves the proposal without preferences until the proposer shuffling dependent root shifts. The api client only throws on network errors, the submission is now retried on the next slot for error responses as well, same as for builder preferences.
