title: refactor: combine proposer and builder preferences services
body:
`ProposerPreferencesService` and `BuilderPreferencesService` share the same structure, both submit ahead of upcoming proposals using the same submission window, track submissions per epoch keyed by the proposer shuffling dependent root and resubmit when it shifts. They only differ in what they sign and where they submit.

Combine them into `ProposalPreferencesService` with one duty window and dependent root tracking. The proposer and builder submissions are still tracked separately since they succeed or fail independently, a failed submission of one is retried on the next slot without resubmitting the other. No behavioral change otherwise.

Closes #9919
author: nflaig

title: fix: send a zero commit in engine_getClientVersionV1 when git data is missing
body:
`getLodestarClientVersion` falls back to an empty commit when the build has no git data (`.git-data.json` with `"commit": ""`, which a Docker build from a worktree or an install without a `.git` directory produces). The engine client then sends `commit: "0x"` in `engine_getClientVersionV1`, which is not a valid value: the [spec](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/identification.md#clientversionv1) defines `commit` as `DATA, 4 bytes`. Nimbus-eth1 rejects it with `-32602 Parameter [version] of type 'ClientVersionV1' could not be decoded`, the other ELs happen to accept it.

- fall back to `00000000` when the commit is missing, so every consumer gets 8 hex characters
- the default graffiti becomes `LS0000` instead of a bare `LS` for such builds, and `/eth/v2/node/version` reports `0x00000000` instead of `0x`
- release images carry git data and are not affected

Found while testing #10204 against Nimbus-eth1, see #10322 for the state flap the rejected call causes, which is a separate change.
author: nflaig

title: fix: handle partial failures when submitting proposal preferences
body:
When some of the submitted proposer or builder preferences are rejected, the beacon node responds with an `IndexedErrorMessage` listing the failed entries by index. The validator client treated this as a failure of the whole batch, nothing was marked as submitted and all entries were sent again on the next slot, including the ones the beacon node had accepted.

- expose the per-index `failures` of an error response on the client `ApiError`
- mark the accepted proposer and builder preferences as submitted and only retry the rejected ones, a proposal is retried with all its builders if one of them rejected the entry
- log each rejected entry with its slot instead of the joined failure messages
- fix `mockApiErrorResponse` which never set the response body

Follow-up to #10319, addresses the partial failure handling mentioned in #9920.
author: nflaig

title: fix: resubmit proposal preferences after the beacon node resynced
body:
Proposer and builder preferences are submitted once per proposal and tracked per dependent root on the validator client, while the beacon node keeps them in memory only. A beacon node restart between the submission and the proposal loses them and peers do not re-gossip preferences they already know, so bids for the proposal are ignored and the proposer falls back to a local payload.

The syncing status tracker already detects this case, a restarted beacon node fails the status poll or reports syncing until it is back at head. The preferences service now resets its submission tracking when the tracker reports the node as resynced and submits everything within the window again. The beacon node ignores preferences it still has.

Addresses the beacon node restart part of #9920. Failover to a second beacon node that never received the preferences is not covered, the status poll goes through the same fallback client.
author: nflaig

title: feat: persist proposer preferences across beacon node restarts
body:
The beacon node keeps the proposer preferences it validated in memory only. After a restart the pool is empty and peers do not re-gossip preferences they already know, so bids for the affected slots are ignored at gossip validation, for the local proposer and for every other proposer, until the next epoch's preferences arrive.

Persist the pool the same way as the op pool, written on shutdown and restored on startup, dropping entries whose proposal slot has passed. Entries were validated before they were persisted and lookups are keyed by the dependent root of their branch, so nothing needs to be re-validated on load.

- add a `ProposerPreferencesRepository` keyed by proposal slot and dependent root
- persist the pool in `persistToDisk` and restore it in `loadFromDisk`
- move `persistDiff` to the op pool utils to share it

A resubmission after a restart now hits the already-known check, the restored entry is neither republished on gossip nor emitted as `proposer_preferences` event. Peers already have the message and ignore duplicates, and the event is defined as received and validated, which a restored entry was not. A builder whose event stream dropped with the restart resyncs via `GET /eth/v1/beacon/proposer_preferences`, which the restored pool now serves for all proposers instead of only the node's own validators.

Addresses the beacon node side of #9920, the validator client side is #10326. A crash skips `persistToDisk`, same as for the op pool.
author: nflaig

title: fix: respect advertised engine REST endpoints
body:
In `auto` mode, REST transport selection only considered supported forks and blob revisions. It ignored the endpoint lists returned by capability discovery. For an EL that advertises REST but omits an endpoint, Lodestar would call the unsupported REST endpoint instead of falling back to JSON-RPC.

Parse `fork_scoped_endpoints` and `unscoped_endpoints`, and use REST only when the requested endpoint is explicitly advertised. Missing endpoint lists default to the standard endpoint sets for compatibility with earlier implementations.

They are documented in the upstream Engine API REST + SSZ refactor proposal:

- [GET /engine/v1/capabilities response](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/refactor.md#get-enginev1capabilities)
- [Rationale for the structured capability fields](https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/blob/main/src/engine/refactor.md#capabilities-format)

## Summary

- parse fork-scoped and unscoped endpoints from REST capabilities
- default omitted endpoint lists to the standard sets
- use JSON-RPC in auto mode when the requested REST endpoint is not advertised
- preserve strict SSZ mode behavior

## Testing

- 88 targeted execution engine tests passed
- Biome checks passed
- docs lint passed

author: nazarhussain

title: fix: bound engine getBlobs retries and request blobs before newPayload
body:
`GetBlobsTracker` only deduplicated in-flight requests, so every gossip column that arrived after the EL had answered `null` triggered another `engine_getBlobsV2` for the same block, about 14 per blob block on a non-supernode, all with the same answer. It also deferred the request to the next event loop tick, which let block processing issue `newPayload` first. Nimbus-eth1 and Nethermind drop a transaction's blobs as soon as the payload is validated, so on those ELs the request could never succeed. Sequence from a debug run, Lodestar on the left, Nimbus on the right:

```
cl 15.191  Call engine api newPayload slot=8
cl 15.194  Trigger getBlobsV2 for block slot=8
el 15.204  POST /engine/v1/payloads
el 15.205  New payload received and validated number=8
el 15.205  POST /engine/v1/blobs/v2 -> 204
el 15.283 .. 15.390  seven more POST /engine/v1/blobs/v2 -> 204
```

- the request is sent synchronously from `triggerGetBlobs`, so it leaves before `processBlock` reaches the engine
- after a `null` answer or a failed call the block root is retried at most `MAX_GET_BLOBS_ATTEMPTS` times and only once `GET_BLOBS_RETRY_INTERVAL_MS` has passed, since the answer only changes if the EL receives the transactions later. The map of failed attempts is capped at 64 block roots
- the v1 path gets a `catch` as well, a rejected `getBlobSidecarsFromExecution` was unhandled before

Closes #10321
author: nflaig

title: feat(builder): persist proposer preferences across builder restarts
body:
**Description**

The builder keeps the proposer preferences it received from the beacon node in memory only. After a restart it depends on a single fetch on connection (#10290) to learn the preferences of upcoming slots, and that fetch returns nothing if it fails or if the beacon node has lost its own pool.

Persist the tracker the same way the beacon node persists its pool in #10327, written on shutdown and restored on startup, dropping entries whose proposal slot has passed. Entries were validated by the beacon node before they were tracked, so nothing is re-validated on load.

- add a `ProposerPreferencesRepository` keyed by proposal slot and dependent root, same key as the beacon node
- restore the tracker in `Builder.init` and persist it in `Builder.close`
- open a LevelDB database at `$dataDir/builder-db` in the builder command, closed after the builder

Pruning is unchanged: the tracker drops past slots on every slot tick, only the retained entries are written on shutdown, and entries with a past proposal slot are skipped on load.

**Notes**

- A crash skips the write on shutdown, same as for the beacon node.
- This only restores what the builder knows. The beacon node validates bids against its own pool, so if it lost its preferences it still ignores bids for those slots until it has them again, which is what #10327 covers.
- This doesn't create a Bucket enum and other machinery, proposerPreferences are at bucket 0. We can introduce this once the need to persist other things arises.
author: markolazic01

title: fix: queue column reconstructions in event multiple come in before completion
body:
### Motivation

`ColumnReconstructionTracker` gates reconstruction behind one process-wide `running` flag. If block A holds the flag when a different block B reaches the 64 column threshold, B's trigger is dropped and nothing retries it.

A supernode imports B on `hasAllData` with 64 columns, times out waiting for `hasComputedAllData` in persistence, and archives only the columns it physically holds. Later gossip columns for B are ignored once it is in fork choice and `getBlobsV2` is skipped once `hasAllData` flips, so the gap is never filled and the node cannot serve part of its advertised custody for that block.

For this bug to come up it needs two roots to reach 64 columns inside the same ~1-2s window (random delay plus KZG time). With 12s slots that means one of:

- block A ~10s late, B on time
- equivocation in a single slot, splitting column indices across two roots
- non-finality with multiple forks, where different proposers build blocks for the same slot and both roots propagate in full
- an event loop stall near a full slot

### Description

- Track reconstruction in an insertion-ordered map keyed by block root. A trigger for a root already queued or in flight is a no-op, a new root waits its turn, and the next root drains when the current attempt finishes. Concurrency stays at one.
- Remove a root once its attempt finishes so a later column can retry a failed attempt.
- Move the under-half-columns guard into the tracker and credit time spent in the queue toward the pre-reconstruction delay.
- Add tracker unit tests covering the dropped second root, dedupe, single concurrency, draining after a failure, and retry.

title: feat: stop depending on prepare_beacon_proposer for custody and gloas payloads
body:
Beacon APIs [#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608) asks beacon nodes to derive the set of validators using the node from `beacon_committee_subscriptions`, to size the custody group count, and makes signed proposer preferences the source of the proposer's fee recipient and gas limit from Gloas on. Lodestar derived both from `prepare_beacon_proposer`, which is deprecated from Gloas and may be dropped by validator clients, only the gas limit already came from the pool.

- track the validators of `beacon_committee_subscriptions` in the proposer cache without fee recipient, the union of both sources feeds the custody group count and the local proposer detection in `prepareNextSlot`
- resolve the fee recipient of a local Gloas payload from the requested one, then the pooled proposer preferences, then the proposer cache, for block production and for the payload attributes prepared a slot ahead
- share the pooled preferences lookup between the fee recipient and the target gas limit
- use the attached validator set for the two other local proposer checks as well, pooling gossip payload attestations for the next proposal and the proposer boost fcU override, both looked for a registered fee recipient
- track the subscribing validators regardless of the sync state, the subscription itself does not fail if the tracking does

`prepare_beacon_proposer` stays supported, it remains the per-validator fee recipient source pre-Gloas and the fallback after. The validator client keeps calling it for now, dropping the call post-Gloas is a follow-up once beacon nodes with this change are released.

title: feat: stop calling `prepareBeaconProposer` from gloas
body:
From Gloas the beacon node takes the proposer's fee recipient from the signed proposer preferences and derives the validators using it from the committee subscriptions, see #10336. `prepare_beacon_proposer` is deprecated from Gloas in beacon APIs [#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608) and beacon nodes may remove it, so the validator client stops calling it once the epoch is in Gloas, same as `register_validator`. The last pre-Gloas submission keeps the proposer cache warm through the fork.

Requires a beacon node with #10336, without it an older beacon node loses custody derivation and local proposer detection for the validators of this client.

title: fix: keep proposer boost root for the payload tiebreak when boost is withheld
body:
In gloas, `should_extend_payload` reads `store.proposer_boost_root` whether or not `should_apply_proposer_boost` applies the boost weight. When the boost is withheld, `updateHead()` only runs the `applyScoreChanges()` pass with `proposerBoost: null` and the payload tiebreak derived its root from that argument. For a previous slot block with a known but not timely payload this prefers the FULL variant over the EMPTY variant the boosted block extends, so the head stops at the parent's FULL variant instead of following the boosted block. The re-application in `validateLatestHash()` replays the previously applied boost and has the same gap.

The tiebreak root is now tracked in `ProtoArray` apart from the applied boost and passed explicitly from the withheld pass. The `should_apply_proposer_boost_withheld` spec vector never imports a payload for the parent so it does not reach the tiebreak, hence the unit test.
author: nflaig

title: feat: track validators that submit proposer preferences as attached
body:
Since #10336 the validators using a beacon node are known from their committee subscriptions. Signed proposer preferences submitted through `POST /eth/v1/validator/proposer_preferences` are a second, more targeted signal: the message is signed by the validator, validated against the proposer lookahead and arrives ahead of the exact slot `prepareNextSlot` prepares for. The validator client also resubmits them once the beacon node is back after a restart (#10326), which tracks the upcoming proposer again at the same time.

Track the validators of preferences that pass validation or are already known, the latter because a pool restored on startup (#10327) makes a resubmission known. Rejected messages and preferences received over gossip are not tracked, they say nothing about which node a validator uses.
author: nflaig

title: feat: reject proposer data and validator registrations from gloas
body:
`prepare_beacon_proposer` and `register_validator` are deprecated from Gloas in beacon APIs [#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608), signed proposer preferences and builder preferences replace them and beacon nodes may remove the endpoints. Beacon APIs [#435](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/435) is the reason to actually do that: proposer data is unsigned, so anyone who can reach the beacon node api can set the fee recipient of any validator, while a signed preference can only come from the validator itself.

Both endpoints respond with 410 once the clock is in Gloas, with a message naming the replacement endpoint, so validator clients that still call them notice. Pre-Gloas is unchanged.

Follow-up to #10336 and #10337.

title: feat: submit proposal preferences of the next epoch from mid-epoch
body:
The validator client submits proposer and builder preferences 8 slots before the proposal slot. Every other client submits them for the whole next epoch as soon as the duties are known, which is what beacon APIs [#608](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/608) describes, and builders only learn about a Lodestar proposal 96 seconds ahead.

Submitting at the epoch boundary has its own problem though: the dependent root of the next epoch's proposals is the last block of the previous epoch, which a proposer boost reorg at the boundary can still orphan in the first slots. Preferences signed right at the boundary would carry a dead branch's root and have to be re-signed.

- submit the preferences of the current epoch's proposals as soon as the duties are known, their dependent root is one epoch deep
- submit the preferences of the next epoch's proposals from the middle of the current epoch
- refetch the first Gloas epoch's duties when a head event in the epoch before the fork changes their dependent root, the pre-Gloas head handling only refreshed the current epoch so preferences signed for the first Gloas epoch could stay on an orphaned root until the fork

Every proposal now gets at least half an epoch of lead instead of 8 slots, and the first Gloas epoch's preferences go out from the middle of the epoch before the fork. The resubmission on a dependent root shift stays as the safety net for deeper reorgs.

title: fix: do not change engine state when the client version request fails
body:
**Motivation**

`engine_getClientVersionV1` is optional and a failure is only logged at debug level, but its errors still went through the engine state tracking. As described in #10322, an EL that rejects the call (Nimbus-eth1 with an empty commit) flips the state from `SYNCED` to `SYNCING` at startup and logs `Execution client request failed` as a warning. #10324 fixed the commit value; this PR handles the remaining part, so the client version call no longer drives the engine state whatever the EL answers.

**Description**

- JSON-RPC: the `JsonRpcHttpClientEvent.ERROR` listener skips errors whose payload is an `engine_getClientVersionV1` request.
- REST: `withTransport` takes an `updateStateOnError` argument (default `true`), and `getClientVersion` passes `false`, so a failing `/identity` request does not update the state either.

Errors from the REST capabilities probe in `getTransport` still update the state as before, and every other call is unchanged. The existing `.catch` in the callers keeps logging the failure at debug level.

Tests: a new case in `restCompatibility.test.ts` makes the client version request fail over JSON-RPC (`json-rpc` mode) and over REST (`auto` mode) and checks that the state stays `SYNCED` with no warning. Both cases fail on `unstable` (`SYNCING`) and pass with this change. `vitest run --project unit test/unit/executionEngine/` passes (103 tests), and `biome check` and `tsc --noEmit` for `beacon-node` are clean.

title: fix: deduplicate pending payload downloads
body:
For an unrevealed Gloas payload, each data column can emit `incompletePayloadEnvelope` at the cutoff. Each event replaced the pending entry and reset its status, so later events bypassed the in-flight guard and started overlapping downloads for the same root. Complete inputs could also be queued for processing repeatedly.

Preserve fetching and processing entries while collecting new peers. Ignore delayed reconciliation, download and processing results if their queue entry was removed or replaced. Failed attempts remain retryable through the existing scheduler.

Tests cover repeated events during downloads and processing, retries after failure, and delayed results racing with entry replacement. All 56 sync tests pass, along with full type checks and lint. The three duplicate-event regressions fail on unmodified `unstable`.

Part of #10114

title: fix: do not treat hex block ids as slots in getBlockRoot fast path
body:
**Motivation**

The Beacon API block_id for getBlockRoot is one of "head", "genesis", "finalized", a decimal slot, or a hex-encoded block root with a 0x prefix (beacon-APIs v5.0.0-beta.0). A 0x string is a block root, but getBlockRoot parsed it as a slot number instead. When that number was a recent slot, the handler returned the historical root for that slot and never loaded the requested block.

**Description**

0x block ids now skip the slot shortcut and are loaded as roots. Decimal slot strings, numeric slots, and 'head' still use the shortcut.

The new unit test requests a root of 0x followed by 31 zero bytes and 05 while the head is at slot 10. The old code treated that id as slot 5. It now returns the root of the loaded block. title: feat: implement quick slots EIP-8198 in heze
body:
Implements EIP-8198 (quick slots) as part of Heze per [consensus-specs#5718](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5718), which folds the eip8198 feature into the fork and derives slot durations from the fork schedule ([consensus-specs#5710](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5710)). Builds on the fork-aware slot timing from #10138.

- `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE` (mainnet 10000, minimal 5000) and `MIN_BLOB_DATA_RETENTION_MS` config values, `getSlotDurationMs(fork)` returns the heze duration post-heze so all deadline and clock call sites pick it up
- piecewise timeline helpers per spec (`getSlotDurations`, `getSlotDurationMsAtEpoch`, `computeTimeAtSlotMs`/`computeTimeAtSlot`, `computeSlotAtTimeMs`), execution payload timestamps follow it
- rewards priced per spec: base reward and sync participant reward scale by `duration(epoch) / duration(GENESIS_EPOCH)`, flag deltas and inactivity penalty priced at the previous epoch, attestation proposer reward at the attestation's target epoch (new `baseRewardPerIncrementPrevEpoch` on the epoch cache), inactivity denominator scales by the squared ratio
- gloas churn limits scale by the duration ratio, bounds applied before scaling and increment rounding once after
- data column retention preserved in wall-clock terms via `getBlobDataRetentionStartEpoch` (ByRange/ByRoot validation, pruning, `isDaOutOfRange`), gossip `seenTTL` uses the largest configured duration

Spec vectors generated from the spec PR head pass (10350/10399 minimal; the 16 fork_choice failures are a pyspec harness artifact in the generated vectors, raised on the spec PR, and the 7 random failures are vectors predating consensus-specs#5719 on the spec PR's base, neither is a Lodestar issue). Note the pyspec harness never activates the schedule (`HEZE_FORK_EPOCH` stays `FAR_FUTURE` in config), so all vectors are generated with the duration unchanged and test configs set `SLOT_DURATION_MS_HEZE = SLOT_DURATION_MS` to match; the scaled path is covered by unit tests and a kurtosis devnet run (gloas genesis, heze at epoch 3, 6s -> 4s slots: clean fork, no missed blocks, full participation, finality advancing).

title: perf: decode hex natively in nodejs fromHexInto
body:
**Motivation**

Since #10203, `getBlobsV2` decodes responses into the preallocated buffers through `fromHexInto`. In nodejs that function was re-exported from the browser implementation, a JS loop that is much slower than native hex decoding. The allocation savings were outweighed by extra main-thread time. On our Hoodi nodes, the `getBlobsV2` call duration (`beacon_engine_getBlobsV2_request_duration_seconds`) went up by ~8-17ms per call after #10203, while the EL HTTP time stayed flat.

`packages/utils/test/perf/bytes.test.ts`, 128KB blob, node 24:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| nodejs `fromHex(blob)` | 130.8 us/op | 130.8 us/op |
| nodejs `fromHexInto(blob)` | ~1.04 ms/op (browser impl) | 120.3 us/op |

**Description**

- implement `fromHexInto` for nodejs with `Buffer#write(hex, "hex")` into the preallocated buffer instead of re-exporting the browser loop
- reject invalid characters by checking the number of bytes written, `Buffer#write` stops silently at the first invalid character
- cover invalid characters and length mismatch for `fromHexInto` in unit tests

title: fix: separate api client response timings
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10349 ([review](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10349#pullrequestreview-5486056636)). The REST API client has the same skew: `stream_time` wraps `rawBody()`, which reads and parses JSON responses but only reads SSZ responses, so JSON looks slower than SSZ. The client is used by the validator (`vc_rest_api_client_*`), the builder (`bc_rest_api_client_*`) and the beacon node builder API client (`lodestar_builder_http_client_*`).

**Description**

- `stream_time` now covers only response body consumption (`text()` / `arrayBuffer()`), including failed reads and HTTP error bodies.
- Add `response_parse_time_seconds{routeId,encoding}` for `JSON.parse` and SSZ deserialization, including failures. This excludes later JSON value conversion, same as #10349.
- Timing moves into `ApiResponse`, which gets the client metrics as an optional constructor argument. SSZ is deserialized lazily in `value()`, so its parse sample is recorded there.

Note: empty responses (`isEmpty` routes, 204) don't read a body, so they no longer produce a `stream_time` sample.

Tests: api client unit tests 45 passed, full api unit suite 741 passed before the last two tests were added. The new timing tests fail without the change. `api` and `builder` type checks and Biome pass locally. title: ci: add nightly mixed client interop workflow
body:
Runs Lodestar against the default-branch image of every other consensus client every night, crossed over so both directions of the beacon API are exercised at once: a Lodestar beacon node drives the other client's validator client and the other client's beacon node drives a Lodestar validator client, with a third Lodestar node without validators as the bootnode. Same idea as the engine API interop run from #10333, so client pair regressions show up the day they land, with the logs needed to file an issue on either side.

- one job per client, Lighthouse, Prysm, Teku, Nimbus, Grandine and Vero, on their default-branch images rebuilt nightly by ethpandaops (`-minimal` builds where the preset is compiled in). Tags are resolved to their digest before every run and the summary row records the digests and versions that were judged. Lodestar runs the published `chainsafe/lodestar:next`, geth master sits behind every node, both can be overridden through `workflow_dispatch`. The package has no separate Grandine validator client and Vero has no beacon node, those two run with Lodestar on both sides of the affected node
- fulu at genesis with blob spam against both validator nodes, judged once epoch 4 is finalized. A gloas at epoch 2 scenario is in the script but not in the workflow yet, it joins once the other clients are ready for it
- the verdict comes from Lodestar's own metrics and logs after the first finalized epoch plus the chain as the Lodestar beacon node sees it: every REST error response of the Lodestar beacon node by route and status, gossip rejects, req/resp errors and peer drops, errors in its log; request errors, duty and signing errors, missing publishes and warnings of the Lodestar validator client; missed slots named with the proposer's pair, every validator hitting the attestation target in every judged epoch and each pair hitting the head with at least 90% of its attestations, sync committee seats filled per block, both beacon nodes agreeing on finality and staying connected
- every beacon node subscribes to all subnets, with a handful of peers a message could otherwise not be published at all (the `submitPoolAttestationsV2 failed` warning in every engine interop run is exactly that), and the Lodestar beacon node serves historical states so participation can be read from finalized states
- a failure with a known cause, on either side, is listed in `known-issues.mjs` with a pattern for the failure text, optionally a log line that has to confirm it, a note and the issue link. It shows up as a known issue in the summary row without failing the job, anything else on the same pair still does, and the entry goes once the fix is in the image the nightly runs
- every run uploads all container logs, the metrics snapshots and a `result.json` plus a summary table row

State of the matrix: Lighthouse, Grandine, Nimbus and Teku pass, Prysm and Vero are green with known issues. Found and filed from the first runs: Teku ignored the whole subscription message of a peer announcing more than 200 topics, a Lodestar supernode with all subnets announces 205, so the pair never finalized (Consensys/teku#11482, fixed in Consensys/teku#11483 the same night); Prysm returns the current epoch's dependent root for next-epoch proposer duties (OffchainLabs/prysm#17681); the Nimbus validator client trips its own doppelganger detection on a block proposal in epoch 0 (status-im/nimbus-eth2#9278, the nightly runs it with detection off until that is fixed); Vero still requires `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` (serenita-org/vero#353). On our side: `produceAttestationData` hands out the next epoch's source after the epoch precompute in the last slot of an epoch, which is what Prysm's aggregators run into (#10368), liveness marks last-slot attesters live in the next epoch, which took the Nimbus VC down after a beacon node restart (#10367), and attester duties for epoch 1 are rejected before genesis (#10369). The matrix ran on this PR through a temporary `pull_request` trigger, last run https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38385107280, removed before merge as in #10333.

title: fix: retry getBlobs for triggers that arrived while a request was in flight
body:
Follow-up for #10329, addresses https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10329#discussion_r4252085059.

**Motivation**

Triggers for a block root with a request in flight hit the `activeReconstructions` early return and were dropped. If that request then failed or returned null, `recordFailedAttempt` recorded the failure but nothing armed the trailing retry. A column burst that landed during a slow EL call therefore got no retry at all.

**Description**

- remember triggers dropped while a request is in flight
- once that request failed, re-enter `triggerGetBlobs`. The failed attempt was just recorded, so this arms the trailing retry instead of sending another request right away
- same for the getBlobsV1 path, where a request that leaves blobs missing counts as failed since the helper handles EL errors and misses internally
- tests: a pending request with triggers in flight gets one retry after the interval (fails without the fix), and a null answer without further triggers still gets no retry

title: fix: avoid per-validator reads in fast confirmation scans
body:
**Motivation**

With `--chain.fastConfirmation` and `--chain.nativeStateTransition` both enabled, the JS heap grows by hundreds of MB per scanned state.

Fast confirmation runs every slot and three of its scans call `state.getValidator(i)` for every active validator, only to read `slashed` and the activation and exit epochs:

- `ensureVoteMaps`
- `getCurrentTargetScore`
- `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots`

On the JS state view this is free: `getReadonly(i).toValue()` returns the value object the tree node already holds. On `NativeBeaconStateView` each call crosses the binding, builds a new validator object with two new byte arrays, and the view keeps it in `cachedValidator` for as long as the view lives. Views do not share these objects, so every scanned checkpoint or head state keeps its own full copy.

A Node simulation of the retained shape (objects built in JS, not through the real binding) for 1M cached validators:

```
retained: Map<index, Validator> x 1M  heapUsed  570.0 MB  external  76.5 MB
retained: Uint16Array x 1M            heapUsed    0.0 MB  external   1.9 MB
```

**Description**

Read scan weights from `getEffectiveBalanceIncrementsZeroInactive()` instead of reading validators one by one.

That array already zeroes validators that are inactive at the state's epoch or slashed, which are exactly the conditions the three scans checked, so the existing zero-weight skip covers them. `getTotalActiveBalance` already requests the same array for the same states in the same run, so this adds no new allocation on native views.

- `getZeroInactiveBalances`: new helper, memoized per state in `FastConfirmationCache.zeroInactiveBalancesByState`. The JS `BeaconStateView` recomputes the array on every call and `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots` runs many times per slot, so without the memo this change would add allocations on the non-native path.
- `ensureVoteMaps`, `getCurrentTargetScore`, `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots`: drop the `getValidator()` reads.
- `getTotalActiveBalance`: goes through the same helper, which removes its state/fallback branch.
- `getEquivocationScore`: unchanged. Slashed equivocators still count there, so it cannot use the zero-inactive balances. Its `getValidator()` reads sit behind `equivocating.has(i)` and are bounded by the equivocating set.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

The implementation and tests were written with Claude Code.

title: ci: wait for the REST re-probe before judging the engine interop EL restart
body:
## Motivation

The 2026-10-13 nightly failed nethermind/fulu with `cl2 after restart: 3 requests fell back to JSON-RPC` ([run](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38344802096)). Lodestar behaved as designed. The harness judged too early.

After `docker restart`, the wait loop polls `el_offline`. Node 2 only notices the EL is gone on its next engine call, so the first poll passes ("back after 12s" is 0s of waiting plus the fixed `sleep 12`). In that run:

- 04:11:34 EL2 restarted
- 04:11:39 node 2 sees the EL offline, the REST capabilities probe fails and backs off 12s
- 04:11:41 EL back online
- 04:11:47 `restart` snapshot taken
- 04:11:53 REST re-probe succeeds

The JSON-RPC requests between 04:11:47 and 04:11:53 landed in the judged window.

## Description

- Wait until node 2 has logged the EL recovery since the restart and, for Lodestar builds with the REST transport, a new capabilities probe result, before taking the `restart` snapshot. Drop the fixed `sleep 12`.
- If the EL is in sync but node 2 logged neither within 240s, log it and judge anyway instead of aborting.
- README: the unjudged restart window now includes the re-probe.

Checked the gate against `cl2.log` from the failing run: it holds until the 04:11:53 re-probe and passes after it.

title: test: pin fake clock in prepareNextSlot slot offset test
body:
**Motivation**

`prepares at the current slot offset when the next duration is 6000 ms` in `prepareNextSlot.test.ts` is flaky (about 1% of runs): https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38387876396/job/115265388997

The scheduler subscribes to a real `Clock` (genesisTime 0) whose fake timers start at wall time. If a wall time slot boundary for the last slot of an epoch lands in roughly the first 4s of the test window, the slot event runs `prepareForNextSlot(wallSlot)`. The test's fork stub turns that into an altair epoch transition. It sleeps 6000ms * 0.6667 and calls `recomputeForkChoiceHead` before the asserted 8s mark. In the failing run, wall slot 149324159 (the last slot of its epoch) started at 11:11:48 UTC, while this test was running.

**Description**

Anchor the fake clock to the start of `clockSlot`, which is the same approach the gloas builder status test in this file already uses. The real clock then cannot emit a slot event during the test.

Verified locally: seeding the test's fake timers at the CI failure time (11:11:45.6 UTC) reproduces the failure without this change and passes with it. A scan over 200 start times gave 7 failures without the change and 0 with it. The full file passes (13/13) and Biome is clean.

title: feat: integrate native beacon networking
body:
**Motivation**

A native networking backend needs a clear boundary with the beacon node. Socket and protocol work can move to Zig, while consensus validation, fork choice, regeneration, BLS execution, and serving data remain owned by Lodestar. That split only controls resource use if native admission and host work agree about capacity and completion.

For example, closing a response stream does not stop a database read already in progress. Expiring a gossip validation does not cancel its BLS job. Handing every received message to an unbounded JavaScript queue would lose the native admission bound at the first callback. This integration carries resource ownership through those boundaries and reuses Lodestar's existing validators and handlers.

Companion native implementation: [ChainSafe/lodestar-z#782](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar-z/pull/782). This draft pins `@chainsafe/lodestar-z` to `c37fc50560672cffb730613b65e60f496af9d028` so both sides use the reviewed binding contracts.

**Description**

Adds an opt-in `NativeNetworkCore` behind `INetworkCore`, together with the host capacity, serving, persistence, and observability needed to run it as a beacon-node backend.

### Overall shape

| Component | Owns | Design consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Network` / `INetworkCore` | Backend selection and the network interface used by sync, APIs, and the beacon chain | `libp2p` remains the default. Native implements the same application-facing responsibilities through a dedicated adapter. |
| Lodestar-z runtime and binding pump | Discovery, QUIC, protocol state, gossip queues, delivery, and native operation completion | Native has its own owner thread. Selecting the native backend does not add the libp2p JavaScript worker path. |
| `NativeGossipExecutor` | Dependency answers and execution of Lodestar's shared validators/handlers | Consensus decisions remain in the existing Lodestar implementation; native owns admission and scheduling. |
| `BoundedServing` / `ServingContext` | Admission of serving work and its reads, serialization, cancellation, and retirement | A request remains charged while child work is alive, even after its network stream has ended. |
| Native peer/state adapters | Chain status, custody/committee demand, peer observations, reports, and restart persistence | Desired state updates coalesce; asynchronous results preserve the identity and origin of the work that produced them. |

Select the backend with `--network.backend=native --tcp=false --quic=true`. Native supports IPv4, IPv6, and dual-stack listeners. It currently supports forks through Fulu: a future Gloas schedule does not prevent startup, but active Gloas and unsupported native requests/topics are rejected. The Git dependency currently requires the native build toolchain at installation.

### Gossip and host capacity

`NativeGossipExecutor` supplies the existing single-message and grouped-attestation validators. Native owns per-kind item/byte budgets, source shares, grouping, dependency waiting, expiry, and slot eligibility. Lodestar answers dependency checks from fork choice and starts bounded unknown-root searches. The [gossip policy comparison](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/cayman/8e71c4ab/packages/beacon-node/src/network/core/native/README.md) records which rules match `NetworkProcessor` and where queue order, grouping, expiry, and byte accounting intentionally differ.

BLS and regeneration capacity changes wake the binding pump. Capacity notifications coalesce and cause a fresh read; they do not reserve work. Blocks, blobs, and data columns retain urgent treatment under native execution limits. The remaining kinds wait when host validation is backpressured. This keeps chain capacity decisions with the components that know their actual load.

Validation completion and native verdict disposition are separate. `GossipJob.reported` acknowledges that native applied or retired the verdicts, including forwarding admission for eligible accepts. Deferred accepted-handler work follows that acknowledgement. Host execution remains accounted for until its work completes, even if the protocol validation deadline has passed. Handler-order adjustments also affect the shared libp2p path and need review with both consumers in mind.

### Request/response and storage

`IncomingRequest.ready()` gates production of the first chunk on native response readiness and bridge capacity. Each `respond()` completes when native no longer borrows that chunk and has reserved room for the next one. The host serving handler tracks its source, asynchronous reads, serialization, and iterator cleanup. Cancellation stops further production; the lease is released only after outstanding child work retires. Capacity refusals produce local resource/rate-limit outcomes rather than peer misconduct reports.

Serving limits reach the data sources: bounded archive/range reads, flat-file header and size checks, limited decompression/materialization, and serialization under a `ServingContext`. This avoids allocating the entire response before checking whether it fits. The native backend requires these handlers. The legacy column-serving fallback remains outside the new bounded-serving contract.

The draft also migrates the DB controller and libp2p peer datastore to `@chainsafe/lodestar-z/leveldb`. The controller preserves existing key/value encodings, missing-value semantics, ranges, batches, cache policy, and lifecycle. The binding checks borrowed value lengths before copying results and supports two concurrent reads per handle alongside serialized writes/cursors/maintenance. This supplies the bounded read operations used by serving.

**The storage migration applies to both network backends.** Switching back to `libp2p` does not switch back to the previous LevelDB binding. Storage adoption and rollback therefore need their own review decision.

### State, attribution, and lifecycle

- **`NativeIntent`:** retains one submitted update and one pending batch. Pending status/custody/topic values coalesce to the latest desired state; committee demand merges. Acknowledged state changes only after success. This bounds update accumulation when epochs, subscriptions, and chain status change together.
- **`NativePeers`, `NativeRequests`, and `NativePeerReports`:** translate peer snapshots and protocol outcomes into existing Lodestar consumers. Response chunks and gossip carry captured connection/endpoint evidence through later SSZ decoding and validation. A current peer connection cannot substitute for the origin of earlier work. Native-attributed faults are not penalized again by the adapter; local overload stays neutral.
- **`rememberedPeers`:** persists a bounded, genesis-scoped set of qualified outbound peers for restart. Invalid or missing state gives a cold start. This is separate from libp2p's peer datastore.
- **Shutdown:** stops new delivery, performs bounded host cleanup, takes the final remembered-peer snapshot, and closes the native runtime. Failure preserves its original cause. Protocol completion and outstanding host-task retirement remain distinct.

### Metrics and Xray

Network metric registration is separated so only the selected backend instantiates its families. Native exports use existing Lodestar/gossipsub names where their semantics match, with additional capacity and scheduling measurements where needed. This avoids duplicate families and makes backend comparisons usable.

Optional Xray capture works on both backends. Native capture is exported entirely from Zig; libp2p uses the JS SDK and stream middleware. Replay is bounded and gaps are explicit. The draft includes the SDK archive and libp2p patches needed by that backend, as described in [the Xray integration notes](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/blob/cayman/8e71c4ab/.xray/README.md). Enabling capture observes application streams; its timestamps do not establish remote packet arrival times.

### Validation

Fresh native integration run after updating the dependency pin:

```text
Test Files  1 passed | 1 skipped (2)
Tests       18 passed | 1 skipped (19)
```

This exercised the real ReleaseSafe addon, native/libp2p interoperability over IPv4 and IPv6, metrics registration, response-origin attribution, and runtime lifecycle. The skipped case is the standalone peer-process entry point. Frozen lockfile validation and lint also pass.

The preceding branch review ran 51 changed unit-test files (710 tests), DB/minimal-serving checks (36 tests), and five integration tests against a rebuilt Xray collector across native and libp2p, including worker mode. Those counts describe separate runs and overlap other branch checks. Beacon-node build and type checks also passed during that review cycle.

### Before merge

- [ ] Review the intentionally different native gossip scheduling policies and continue tracking upstream `NetworkProcessor` changes.
- [ ] Decide the PR boundaries for the all-backend LevelDB migration, shared handler/serving changes, and libp2p Xray integration.
- [ ] Coordinate with the native PR on the outstanding [quiche receive-memory issue](https://github.com/cloudflare/quiche/issues/2814), platform qualification, and native fork support.
- [ ] Settle dependency release ordering and test the artifacts installed through that path. Replace the Git pin, SDK archive, and middleware patches when suitable releases are available.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implementation, tests, and this description were primarily authored with OpenAI Codex, with architecture and policy decisions developed through iterative maintainer direction. This is a draft for human review.

author: dependabot

title: test: make data column range benchmarks report only
body:
**Motivation**

The `dataColumnSidecarsByRange` range benchmarks are the largest source of false `Performance regression` failures in the Benchmark workflow. Of the last 17 failed benchmark attempts, 9 are these benches tripping the 10x threshold (from #10074) at 12x to 101x. That includes all 4 attempts of the v1.50.0 merge back on unstable.

The legacy range benches are bimodal on the shared runner. `8 slots / 1 columns / legacy` normally measures 120-340us over 1.7k-3.3k runs. On unrelated commits it measures ~11-17ms on every op and converges at 26-44 runs. The very next bench (`8 slots / 8 columns / legacy`, 8x more data) is back to ~0.7ms. The slow mode only ever hit a legacy bench that runs right after a flat files bench. No threshold separates that from a real regression.

It also poisons the rolling baseline. A spiked unstable run is persisted before the regression check fails, and PRs based on that commit then report `head state / 8 slots / 1 columns / legacy` at x0.018.

**Description**

Set `noThreshold: true` on the range benches so they are still measured and reported but no longer gate CI. The two single slot lookup benches keep `threshold: 10`. They have not tripped in this sample.

title: feat(builder): minimal wiring, bidding and revealing
body:
**Motivation**

The builder services are merged but not connected, so a running builder only observes. This wires them into a bidding and reveal loop and connects the builder to an execution client.

**Description**

Minimal changes ported from existing variants of wiring.

Additions:
- Bidder: on `payload_attributes`, builds a payload for the next slot, retrieves it at `--bidding.deadlineBps` (default 95%), prices it with `ProportionalBidPolicy` and publishes the bid
- Revealer: publishes the envelope once a block selecting one of our bids is imported, unless it arrived after `--reveal.cutoffBps`
- BidLedger: won bids settle three epochs after their slot
- CLI: `--execution.*`, `--jwtSecret`, `--bidding.*`, `--reveal.cutoffBps`; the EL connection goes through `initializeExecutionEngine`
- Kurtosis devnet config and nightly smoke test updated to run with an EL and assert bids, wins and reveals

Relates to #10234, #10247, #10259, which contain several improvements over this, can be shipped as follow-ups.

Co-authored-by: Nico Flaig <nflaig@protonmail.com>
author: markolazic01

title: fix: check bid inclusion list bits against timely lists only
body:
Bids are now ignored until the inclusion list deadline of `bid.slot - 1`, and the proposer no longer re-checks a bid's inclusion list bits against every list it observed (`only_timely=False`, [validator.md](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/v1.7.0-beta.4/specs/heze/validator.md?plain=1#L124-L137)) before picking it. Builder API bids get the same timely check as gossip bids.

The current behavior allows two griefing attacks:

- an inclusion list committee member releases its list after the deadline, right before the proposer picks a bid; no builder can cover it in time, so every bid is dropped and the proposer falls back to a local payload
- a builder gossips a very high bid early, before most lists exist; it passes gossip, blocks all lower bids from propagating, then gets dropped at selection, crowding out every other p2p bid without ever paying

With bids only accepted after the deadline, every bid is checked against one final set of timely lists and the proposer picks the highest one. The proposer's own payload still uses every observed list.

Spec change: nflaig/consensus-specs#12. Only effective once all clients ignore early bids, until then other clients still relay early bids.
author: nflaig

title: perf: avoid array concat when deserializing ENR subnets
body:
**Motivation**

`enrSubnets - fastDeserialize 64 bits` is one of the most frequent false benchmark regressions. Across the 600 failed Benchmark runs since June, it was flagged in 21 of them at x3.0 to x5.0, most recently on unstable: https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/38464919941/job/115529054217

The 64 bit path builds the result with 8 chained `concat` calls, so each call allocates 8 intermediate arrays. On CI it measures 632-853ns normally and 2.2-3.8us when it trips. That makes the "fast" path 2-3x slower than `ssz BitVector 64 bits` in the same file. The ssz bench allocates a single array and has never been flagged.

**Description**

Preallocate the result array and copy the cached per-byte bits into it, the same way `newFilledArray` builds its arrays. Output is unchanged.

Local numbers (5M calls):
- concat: 4914ms, 1629 GC events
- preallocated: 710ms, 318 GC events

`@chainsafe/benchmark` locally, `enrSubnets - fastDeserialize 64 bits`: ~1.1us/op before, ~310ns/op after. ssz BitVector is ~410ns/op.

Unit tests in `enrSubnets.test.ts` pass (11/11).

title: fix: allow next epoch duties requests before genesis
body:
**Motivation**

Before genesis `chain.clock.currentEpoch` is -1, so the one-epoch-ahead guard in `getAttesterDuties` rejects epoch 1 with a 400. Validator clients request the current and next epoch on startup, which is the Nimbus and Prysm noise seen in the interop nightly (#10361).

**Description**

The guard now uses `Math.max(chain.clock.currentEpoch, GENESIS_EPOCH)`, so epoch 0 and 1 are accepted before genesis and epoch 2 is still rejected. After genesis nothing changes. `getPtcDuties` has the same guard, so it gets the same change. The proposer duties check already skips negative epochs. Sync committee duties have no epoch-ahead guard.

Added `duties/attester.test.ts`: with the clock one slot before genesis, epoch 1 gets past the guard (it fails on `unstable`), and epoch 2 still returns the "more than one ahead" error.

Tested: the new test, `biome check`, `tsc` for beacon-node, and the beacon-node unit suite. Two unrelated files (`executionEngine/rest`, `opPools/opPool`) timed out once under load and pass when re-run. I didn't run an interop devnet, so I haven't checked the actual duties response for epoch 1 from the genesis state end to end.

Closes #10369

title: fix: remove signer from validator store if its index is known
body:
`removeSigner` returned early when `indicesService.removeForKey()` succeeded, so a key with a known validator index was never removed from `validators`. Keymanager `DELETE /eth/v1/keystores` and `DELETE /eth/v1/remotekeys` answered `deleted` and removed the key from disk, but the key stayed loaded, the next index poll found it again and it kept performing duties. Without doppelganger protection it kept signing, which can get the validator slashed if the exported slashing protection is imported into another client. Keys removed from an external signer by `externalSignerSync` were affected the same way.

The index is now removed and the key is always deleted from `validators`, with a regression test for a key whose index has been polled.

Closes #10385
author: nflaig

title: fix: isolate selection proof failures per validator
body:
Selection proofs are signed one validator after another while polling attester duties and when getting sync committee duties for a slot, and a single failure aborted the whole loop. One validator with a failing signer made every validator on the client miss its attester duties for the epoch, or its sync committee duties for the slot.

The easiest way to hit this is a remote key the external signer does not hold, e.g. imported through the keymanager API with the wrong URL, since `importRemoteKeys` does not check the signer has the key. The selection proof then fails every epoch and the client stops attesting for all of its validators. A key removed from the external signer while still in the sync committee did the same to sync committee duties until the next duties poll (see #10386).

Errors are now caught and logged per validator, matching how attestation and sync committee message signing already handle them. A skipped attester duty is retried on the next poll.
author: nflaig

title: fix: skip buffering unknown-root gossip messages from expired slots
body:
Follow-up to #10039. The per-slot budget of buffered unknown roots is keyed by the message slot, and `onClockSlot` only keeps the last `MAX_UNKNOWN_ROOTS_SLOT_CACHE_SIZE` slots. Messages are accepted up to 32 slots in the past though, so a message from an already expired slot was still buffered, and each of those slots got its own fresh 5-root budget until the next tick. The effective bound was ~33 slots x 5 roots instead of 3 x 5.

Such messages are no longer buffered, for both the block and the payload await queue. They are still searched so the block or payload can be recovered, they would have been dropped on the next slot anyway. The reject metric reason is `expired`.

A unit test that buffers 5 roots for every slot in the accepted range holds 165 roots before this change and 15 after. The same setup with `execution_payload` envelopes (5 unknown roots per slot, 3 envelopes per root, which hits the per-root cap of 2) holds 330 envelopes before and 30 after.
author: nflaig

title: fix: expire held gossip messages for blocks that were seen but never imported
body:
`searchUnknownBlock` and `searchUnknownEnvelope` return early when the block or payload is already seen (in the block input cache or being gossip validated), so no `searchedRootsBySlot` entry is created for that root. Messages for it are still buffered by `maybeAwaitBlock` / `maybeAwaitPayload`, but `onClockSlot` only expires roots that have a search entry. If the block then never imports (failed import, `DATA_UNAVAILABLE`, failed gossip validation) there is no `block` / `executionPayload` event either, so those messages and their share of the awaiting counter stay forever. Over time the global cap fills up and every message for an unknown block is dropped with `reached_limit` until restart.

Buffered messages now mark their (slot, root) entry and `onClockSlot` also expires on that mark, for both the block and the payload queue. Roots that are only buffered now count toward `MAX_SEARCHED_ROOTS_PER_SLOT`, at most `MAX_BUFFERED_ROOTS_PER_SLOT` per slot.

This matches what our mainnet node showed on 2026-09-11 (v1.47.0). It fell ~70 slots behind while the EL was OOMing and was back at head about an hour later, but `lodestar_awaiting_block_gossip_messages_per_slot_total` stayed at 16385 for 3+ hours with zero expired or resolved messages, until the node was restarted.

The two new unit tests fail on `unstable` and pass with this change. A broader A/B against the real `NetworkProcessor` (10 aggregates per root, clock advanced 100 slots):

| case | `unstable` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| block truly unknown (control) | 10 -> 0 | 10 -> 0 |
| block seen, import fails | 10 -> 10, never expires | 10 -> 0 |
| payload seen, import fails | 10 -> 10, never expires | 10 -> 0 |
| 450 seen blocks fail import (40 aggregates each), then a new unknown block | 16385 stuck, new block's messages: 0 held | 120 held (last 3 slots), new block's messages: 10 held |

title: feat(builder): apply verified payment accounting atomically
body:
## Motivation

Winning bids stay reserved until their payment is reflected in the balance used for bidding, or there is evidence that they cannot be paid. Releasing them by age can overstate the available balance; keeping every paid win reserved indefinitely understates it.

This is the accounting application part of LOD-112, split from evidence retrieval and runtime wiring so the ledger invariants can be reviewed on their own.

## Changes

- Apply a balance snapshot and verified paid/cancelled decisions together, after checking the entire batch against the exact local bids and selected block roots.
- Reject cancelled or overlapping reads, older/inconsistent snapshots, and changed ledger records before changing accounting state.
- Retain unresolved obligations, enforce an explicit balance freshness bound, and stop returning a usable balance if the finalized anchor is invalidated.
- Distinguish confirmed cancellation from payment settlement in the ledger.

The caller must establish canonical, finalized evidence against the exact snapshot. These decisions are not proofs by themselves. This PR adds no age-based settlement, API polling, or live automatic release of reservations. Production evidence retrieval and connection to the common runtime in #10379 remain separate follow-ups.

## Validation

- 43 focused ledger/accounting tests pass.
- Builder type-check and build pass, with the dependency packages built.
- Compiled accounting-module import, changed-file Biome, and diff checks pass.

No full BN/EL lifecycle run is claimed. Kept draft for review of the accounting contract and its eventual runtime integration.

title: fix: assert doppelganger safety only for messages counted in liveness
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10312#discussion_r4278615099. Doppelganger detection trips on any liveness reported for the validator while it's unverified. `validatorSeenAtEpoch` counts attestations (gossip and in blocks), aggregators, payload attestations and block proposers, so the VC must not publish any of these during detection. Slashable messages need the check anyway.

Duty services already drop unverified validators (attestation, block and PTC duties), so the store asserts are a second line of defense. Audit of the `ValidatorStore` sign methods:

- blocks, attestations, payload attestations: assert, keep
- aggregate and proof: counted in liveness through `seenAggregators` but had no assert, added
- proposer preferences: not slashable and not counted in liveness, assert removed
- sync committee messages and contributions, selection proofs, randao, execution payload envelope, voluntary exit, validator registration, builder auth: neither slashable nor counted in liveness, no assert

**Description**

- assert doppelganger safety in `signAggregateAndProof`
- drop the assert from `signProposerPreferences`
- unit test for the aggregate case, which fails without the change

title: fix: resolve builder pubkeys in a single pass in getStateBuilders
body:
**Motivation**

Looking up builders by pubkey in `getStateBuilders` (`POST /eth/v1/beacon/states/{state_id}/builders`) scans the whole builder registry for every requested pubkey. With a large registry this is O(ids × builders) on the main thread. On glamsterdam-devnet-12 (~24k builders after a deposit spray) a client polling this endpoint blocked the main thread for ~17s per request, which made the node miss proposals and fall behind head.

**Description**

Build a builder pubkey to index map at most once per request (lazily, only if a pubkey id is requested) and resolve pubkey ids against it.

Micro benchmark, 400 pubkey ids against 24k builders on a tree-backed builder list:
- linear scan per id: ~6.3s
- single pass map: ~66ms

title: fix: use the block root for the genesis dependent root fallback
body:
The proposer duties endpoint falls back to the genesis block root when the decision root is not in the state yet, which is the case for requests served from the slot 0 state on a gloas-at-genesis network (the lookahead decision slot is slot 0 itself). That fallback hashed the `SignedBeaconBlock` container instead of the block message, so the validator client received a dependent root that does not exist in fork choice and its proposer preferences for epochs 0 and 1 were rejected with `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` until the first block was imported.

Seen on the heze-devnet-2 rehearsal (3 Lodestar nodes, gloas at genesis): duties reported `0x8638…` while the genesis block root is `0x40a2…`, and every VC logged `Error submitting signed proposer preferences ... UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` at slots 0 and 1.

- hash the block message, and only read the block from the DB once the state is past the block roots window, the anchor checkpoint root already covers the slot 0 state
- unit test for the dependent root at genesis, fails on unstable

A/B on the same kurtosis config (3 Lodestar nodes on ethrex, gloas at genesis, mainnet preset): with unstable the duties endpoint reported `0x8638…` at genesis against a genesis root of `0x40a2…`, every VC logged the error twice and the beacon nodes answered the submissions with 400. With this branch the duties endpoint reported the genesis root, all proposer preferences submissions at and after genesis returned 200 and no `UNKNOWN_DEPENDENT_ROOT` was logged.

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.
author: nflaig

title: fix: prepare the next slot payload on the variant the proposer builds on
body:
While a block is in its own slot, fork choice ranks its FULL variant above EMPTY. `get_payload_status_tiebreaker` only consults `should_extend_payload` from the next slot on. `prepareNextSlot` runs before that, so after an unsatisfied inclusion list verdict it prepared the payload on FULL while the proposer one slot later built on EMPTY, missed the payload id cache and rebuilt the payload at proposal time.

- `ForkChoice.predictHeadVariantAtSlot(head, slot)` picks between the EMPTY and FULL variants with the same tiebreaker `findHead` applies at `slot`, with unit tests
- `prepareNextSlot` prepares on that variant

A/B on a kurtosis heze devnet (3 Lodestar nodes on ethrex ddffde4, spamoor): on unstable all 4 proposals after an unsatisfied payload rebuilt (`prepType=Reorged`, new payload id, 0.7s fetch). With this change every proposal after an unsatisfied payload reused the prepared payload (`prepType=Cached`, one EL build, 0.15s fetch) and still built on EMPTY: 2 of 2 with the first form of the change, 5 of 5 with the current head.

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.

body:
**Motivation**

`getInclusionList` inherits the JSON-RPC client's retry policy while occupying the serial engine queue. Retrying a failed request delays queued `forkchoiceUpdated` and `newPayload` calls. #10405 explicitly proposes disabling retries for this call.

**Description**

- HTTP 500 and timeout failures propagate after one attempt, then an already queued forkchoice update completes.
- Successful inclusion lists are decoded into transaction bytes.
- A failed primary URL still falls back to a working secondary URL.

Both failure tests configure two client retries. Before the fix, each observes three inclusion-list requests before the queued forkchoice update; after the fix, each observes one. Disabling retry rounds does not limit a multi-URL request to one HTTP attempt or guarantee the protocol deadline.

title: fix: do not prefer an unsatisfied payload as head during its own slot
body:
Fork choice only acts on the inclusion list verdict from the next slot on, through `should_extend_payload`. During the block's own slot `getPayloadStatusTiebreaker` returns the raw payload status, so the head stays on the FULL variant of a payload the node already knows it will not extend. Everything reading the head during that slot gets the wrong variant: the next slot payload is prepared on FULL and rebuilt at proposal time, and bids for the next slot are checked against the wrong parent hash.

Rank such a payload below its EMPTY variant during the block's own slot, as proposed in https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5769. Same-slot attestations support the PENDING node, so both variants weigh zero during that slot and the tiebreaker alone picks the variant. Weight decides as before once attestations from the next slot exist.

A/B on a kurtosis heze devnet (3 Lodestar nodes on ethrex ddffde4, which still builds unsatisfied payloads, spamoor): with this change the head of a block with an unsatisfied payload stays EMPTY through its own slot (head_v2 stream) and the following proposal reused the prepared payload built on EMPTY, `prepType=Cached`, 2 of 2. On unstable every such proposal rebuilt, `prepType=Reorged`, 4 of 4.

Supersedes #10410.

title: fix: scale heze rewards and churn relative to SLOT_DURATION_MS

This only differs when heze is active at genesis with a different slot duration, where the previous formula never scaled. With the new one a network launched on heze can mirror mainnet's post-heze economics by keeping `SLOT_DURATION_MS` at 12000.

Mainnet and any network that forks into heze mid-chain are unaffected. Should be merged after the spec PR lands.

title: fix: re-check fatal peers after the envelope state lookup
body:
#10239 drops gossip messages from peers reported as Fatal, but only checks when a message is queued and when its processing starts. Envelope validation awaits regen for the block state, and on a state cache miss the sender can be reported Fatal while it waits, e.g. because another of its envelopes failed the signature check. The validation then still computes the signing root, which hashes the full payload.

The gossip handler now passes a fatal peer check into envelope validation, which ignores the envelope after the state lookup if its sender has become Fatal. By-root sync and the API path are unchanged.
author: nflaig

title: fix(reqresp): reject trailing bytes after request payload
body:
**Motivation**

Closes #9362. Differential testing found that Lodestar accepts req/resp requests that carry trailing garbage bytes after the valid SSZ snappy payload. The consensus spec (phase0 p2p-interface, "Encoding strategies") lists "any remaining bytes, after having read the n SSZ bytes" as invalid input, and requires responders to answer requests with an `InvalidRequest` error in that case. Teku already rejects; Lodestar answered `Success`.

**Description**

`requestDecode` is the single-payload read path for incoming requests, so it now asks the ssz_snappy reader to verify end of stream after the payload:

* `readSszSnappyPayload` and `readEncodedPayload` take an `expectEndOfStream` flag, set only by `requestDecode`. Response chunk decoding is unchanged, since further chunks legitimately follow a chunk payload.
* With the flag set, the reader tries to read one more byte after the payload. A compliant requester closes the write side of the stream right after the request (as `sendRequest` does), so a clean request reads as end of stream here, bounded by the existing request timeout in `handleRequest`. Any byte read instead throws a new `SszSnappyError` code `SSZ_SNAPPY_ERROR_TRAILING_BYTES`, which `handleRequest` already maps to an `InvalidRequest` response for decode failures.
* Scope: methods with no request body (`requestSizes === null`) still return early, and no behavior changes for responses or for well formed requests.

**Tests**

* New fixture case in `requestEncodersErrorCases`: a Ping request followed by 4 trailing bytes must reject with `SSZ_SNAPPY_ERROR_TRAILING_BYTES`. It failed before the fix (the request decoded successfully) and passes after.
* Full `@lodestar/reqresp` unit suite: 166/166 tests passed (16 files), including the existing valid request cases, which exercise the end of stream path on well formed requests.
* `tsc` type check for the package passes, and Biome check is clean on all touched files.

I reproduced the issue with a failing test first, verified the fix against the package test suite and type check, and I will respond to review feedback myself.

author: Kshot3000

title: feat: make the builder bid deadline configurable
body:
Builder API bid requests advertise a fixed 500ms deadline via `X-Timeout-Ms` and the p2p bid is selected at a fixed 500ms from the slot start. Bid value keeps rising towards the slot boundary, so an operator may want to trade proposal latency for a longer bidding window, or shorten it on a network where builders bid early.

- add `--builder.bidDeadline` to configure the duration builders are given once block production starts, the default stays at 500ms and the value must be a positive integer
- read the p2p bid pool after the same duration from the request rather than at a fixed slot offset, and only once the builder API requests settled, so p2p bids get the same window as builder API bids including the lag buffer
- refuse to start if an explicitly configured deadline plus the 250ms lag buffer is not below the block production race cutoff of a post-gloas fork, as the local block would be selected at the cutoff before any bid block is produced. The cutoff stays at 2s on 12s slots, which caps the deadline at 1749ms on mainnet. The default is not checked so networks with short slots keep working as before
- past the race cutoff, use a pooled p2p bid right away instead of waiting for pending builder API requests
author: nflaig

title: feat: do not wait for the bid deadline when no bid can be selected
body:
Without builder API entries, block production still waits until the bid deadline before reading the p2p bid pool, even when no bid for the slot has been received by the time the local block is ready. The local block is selected in that case, so the proposal is delayed by the remaining window for nothing.

Abort the wait once the local block is produced if no builders are configured and the pool holds no bid for the proposal parent, through the same path already used for a boost factor of 0. A p2p bid arriving between the local block and the deadline is no longer considered in that case, builders are expected to bid during the previous slot.

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.
author: nflaig

title: fix: check the parent payload before importing a repeat proposal in gloas
body:
The gossip handler imports a signature-verified REPEAT_PROPOSAL sibling into fork choice if its parent is known. That check only looks at the parent block root, while gossip validation of a gloas block also requires the parent payload (`bid.parent_block_hash`) to be known. A gloas sibling whose parent payload has not been seen passes the handler check, hits PARENT_PAYLOAD_UNKNOWN in block processing, and the default catch reports the sender with LowToleranceError.

The handler now mirrors the validation check and uses `getBlockHexAndBlockHash` for gloas blocks, so such a sibling is ignored without penalty, same as a sibling with an unknown parent block.
author: nflaig

title: feat: delay and repeat builder bid requests per proposal
body:
Stacked on #10422. Bid value keeps rising towards the slot boundary, a proposer that asks builders once at slot start leaves that on the table. This lets an operator start the bidding window later and ask more than once.

- add `--builder.bidDelay`, the first bid request is sent once the slot is that many milliseconds old, a later block production request starts right away
- add `--builder.bidRequests`, the number of consecutive bid requests per proposal. Round i is scheduled at `bidDelay + i * bidDeadline` from the slot start, never before the previous round's deadline, every round advertises the full deadline. Bids from all rounds are ranked together, a bid returned unchanged to the same request is collected once, and no further round is started past the race cutoff or once the local block has been selected, the bids collected by then are still ranked
- the p2p bid pool is read when the last round would reach its deadline, so p2p bids get the same window as builder API bids including the delay
- the startup check covers the whole window, `bidDelay + bidRequests * bidDeadline` plus the lag buffer must be below the race cutoff when any of the three is configured

Defaults are 0 and 1, which is the behavior of #10422.

title: fix: reject index-1 attestations to an engine-invalidated payload
body:
Gossip and API attestations with `data.index == 1` were only gated on the payload being seen. An attestation to a block whose execution payload the execution engine rejected got `IGNORE` (the failed envelope import never creates the FULL variant, so the payload counts as not seen) instead of the `REJECT` required by `verify_attestation_payload_status`.

`importExecutionPayload` now records the block root when `newPayload` returns `INVALID`, and `validateAttestation` / `validateAggregateAndProof` reject index-1 attestations to it with `EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_INVALID`. The record lives in `SeenPayloadEnvelopeInput` and is pruned on finalization, it is bounded by the number of unfinalized blocks since envelope import requires the block in fork choice. Marking by block root is sound because the bid and the state commit every engine input (payload block hash, versioned hashes, execution requests, parent beacon block root), so no other envelope for the block can turn out valid. The FULL variant's execution status is checked as well so a payload invalidated after an optimistic import is rejected too.

Verified on a kurtosis gloas devnet (minimal preset, Lodestar + geth behind an engine proxy that answers one `newPayload` with `INVALID`), submitting an index-1 attestation to that block through `POST /eth/v2/beacon/pool/attestations` from the next slot:

| | unstable (`af6f75c124`) | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| index-0 vote to the block | 200 | 200 |
| same-slot index-1 vote | 400 `PREMATURELY_INDICATED_PAYLOAD_PRESENT` | 400 `PREMATURELY_INDICATED_PAYLOAD_PRESENT` |
| index-1 vote from the next slot | 400 `EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_NOT_SEEN` (IGNORE) | 400 `EXECUTION_PAYLOAD_INVALID` (REJECT) |

title: fix: route pending deposits by withdrawal credentials at the gloas fork
body:
at the gloas fork `onboardBuildersFromPendingDeposits` routes pending deposits by pubkey, once a builder is registered for a key every later deposit for that key tops up the builder regardless of its withdrawal credentials. a validator deposit funded by someone else that is queued behind a builder deposit for the same key ends up in the builder's balance and no validator is created, see https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/5735

routes by withdrawal credentials instead, matching https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5736: validator deposits always stay queued, a valid builder deposit registers or tops up a builder even if a validator uses the key, an invalid builder deposit is only kept where the validator path would still apply it

fork vectors generated from the spec pr pass, the pinned v1.7.0-beta.4 vectors fail on the five mixed-key cases until the pin moves to a release that includes the spec change

title: feat: add flag to disable validation of published execution payload bids
body:
The beacon node currently runs full gossip validation on every bid submitted via `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids` before broadcasting it. This adds latency to the publish path and is redundant if the API is only used by a trusted local builder which constructs the bid from the same chain state.

This adds a hidden `--api.disableBidValidation` flag which broadcasts bids submitted via the API without validating them. Validation stays enabled by default, skipping it must be an operator decision and not sender controlled as a public node would otherwise blindly forward invalid bids and get penalized by peers.

See ethereum/beacon-APIs#668 which makes validation optional in the spec.
