title: fix: register block attesters under the attestation epoch
body:
**Motivation**

Fixes #10367, found by the consensus client interop nightly. `importBlock` registered the attesters of every attestation in a block under the block's epoch:

```ts
this.seenBlockAttesters.addIndices(blockEpoch, indexedAttestation.attestingIndices);
```

An attestation for the last slot of epoch N is normally included in the first block of epoch N+1, so `validatorSeenAtEpoch(index, N+1)` and with it `POST /eth/v1/validator/liveness/{epoch}` reported those validators as live in N+1 even if they never attested in that epoch. Doppelganger protection in Lighthouse, Nimbus and Vero is built on this endpoint, so a validator client restarted at an epoch boundary could be told its validators are already live in the new epoch when they are not.

**Description**

Key the cache by the attestation's epoch, as @nflaig outlined in the issue:

```ts
this.seenBlockAttesters.addIndices(
  computeEpochAtSlot(attestation.data.slot),
  indexedAttestation.attestingIndices
);
```

This matches how the gossip caches key seen attesters, and `lowestPermissibleEpoch` in the seen caches already covers the previous epoch, so no pruning change is needed.

New regression test in `test/unit/chain/blocks/importBlock.test.ts` (added as a second suite in the existing file): imports the first block of an epoch carrying an attestation from the last slot of the previous epoch (attester index 103, the validator from the interop report) and asserts the attester is registered under the attestation epoch and not under the block epoch. The test fails on the previous code (`isKnown(attEpoch, 103)` is false) and passes with this change.

Checks run:

- The new test: red before the fix, green after
- `vitest run --project unit test/unit/chain/blocks/importBlock.test.ts` after rebasing onto current `unstable`: 5 tests passing (the 4 existing gloas tests plus the new one)
- `vitest run --project unit test/unit/chain/blocks/` on the pre-rebase base: 10 files, 65 tests, all passing
- `biome check` on both changed files: clean
- Type check of the package: no errors in the changed files (the run reports pre-existing errors in unrelated files in my local checkout, from stale build outputs of other packages)

**AI assistance disclosure**

Per CONTRIBUTING.md: this PR was prepared with AI assistance. I used an AI coding assistant to navigate the codebase, draft the regression test and implement the fix approach specified in the issue. I reproduced the bug with the failing test first and verified the fix and the surrounding test suites myself before submitting. Happy to adjust anything on review.

**Breaking change**

None. The liveness endpoint now reports the epoch the attestation belongs to, which is the documented intent of the cache.

Closes #10367

title: fix: hand out a state in the requested epoch from getHeadStateAtEpoch
body:
**What type of PR this is**

Bug fix

**What does this PR do? Why is it needed?**

Fixes #10368, found by the consensus client interop nightly. `produceAttestationData` asks `chain.getHeadStateAtEpoch(attEpoch)` for a state in the attestation's epoch so the returned `source` is that epoch's justified checkpoint. But `getHeadStateAtEpoch` returned the closest head state whenever `epoch <= computeEpochAtSlot(headState.slot)`:

```ts
if (epoch <= computeEpochAtSlot(headState.slot)) {
  return headState;
}
```

In the last slot of an epoch, `PrepareNextSlotScheduler` precomputes the epoch transition and the result lands in the checkpoint state cache, so `getClosestHeadState` hands out a state that is already in epoch N+1. A request for epoch N then got the N+1 state, whose `currentJustifiedCheckpoint` has already moved on, so aggregators re-requesting attestation data in that window computed a different data root and `getAggregatedAttestationV2` answered 404, and a late attestation-data request could produce an attestation with an invalid source.

**Description**

`getHeadStateAtEpoch` now returns the closest head state only when it is in the requested epoch:

- Requested epoch ahead of the head state: unchanged, regen to the start slot of the requested epoch.
- Head state already past the requested epoch and the head block is in the requested epoch (the interop case): return the head block's post-block state from the block state cache, falling back to regen of that block's state if it is not cached.
- Head block also past the requested epoch (a late request after the next epoch's first block): regen the state at the requested epoch's last slot from the closest canonical block at or before it.

This follows the fix direction outlined in the issue.

**Which issue(s) does this PR fix?**

Fixes https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/issues/10368

**Other notes for review**

Added `test/unit/chain/getHeadStateAtEpoch.test.ts` with five cases covering the same-epoch fast path, the regen-forward path, and the three past-epoch paths above. The three past-epoch cases fail on the previous code (they return the future state) and pass with this change.

Checks run:

- `vitest run --project unit test/unit/chain/getHeadStateAtEpoch.test.ts`: 5 passing with the fix, 3 failing without it
- `vitest run --project unit test/unit/chain/getStateByStateRoot.test.ts`: passing
- `biome check` on both changed files: clean
- Package type check: no errors in the changed files. The run reports pre-existing errors in this local checkout from stale build outputs of other packages (for example `@lodestar/validator` is not built here), and those are identical on the unmodified base. For the same reason `produceAttestationData.test.ts` cannot run in this checkout, and `prepareNextSlot.test.ts` shows timing failures that are also identical on the unmodified base.

**AI assistance disclosure**

Per CONTRIBUTING.md: this PR was prepared with AI assistance. I used an AI coding assistant to navigate the codebase, draft the regression tests and implement the fix approach specified in the issue. I reproduced the bug with failing tests first and verified the fix and the surrounding test suites myself before submitting. Happy to adjust anything on review.

**Breaking change**

None. Callers that asked for a state in an epoch now get a state in that epoch in the precompute window instead of the next epoch's state.

title: fix: drop finalized block hash from payload id cache key
body:
**Motivation**

On Sepolia, our proposals in the first slot of an epoch are published about 80ms later than in other slots (3 days of logs: slot 0 p50 603ms vs 525ms for slots 1-31). Every slot 0 proposal logged `prepType=Reorged`, every other one `Cached`.

When finalization advances at the epoch boundary, the payload id prepared by `prepareNextSlot` no longer matches because the cache key includes `finalizedBlockHash`. `produceBlockBody` then re-sends forkchoiceUpdated, the EL returns the same payload id, and we wait `PAYLOAD_GENERATION_TIME_MS` again before `getPayload`.

**Description**

- Drop `finalizedBlockHash` from the payload id cache key. The payload id only depends on the head block hash and the payload attributes. Lighthouse keys its cache the same way (`PayloadIdCacheKey {head_block_hash, payload_attributes}`).
- Add a unit test that a prepared payload id is reused when the finalized block hash changed.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Investigation, code and tests by lodekeeper (AI).

title: fix: apply forkchoiceUpdated verdicts to fork choice
body:
An INVALID response to `engine_forkchoiceUpdated` was turned into a bare `Error` and only logged by the post-import call sites, so a node that imported a payload optimistically kept the execution-invalid block as its head and extended it until a restart. A VALID response was dropped too, leaving a head imported as SYNCING optimistic until a descendant validated it.

`notifyForkchoiceUpdate` now returns the engine result instead of throwing on INVALID, and the chain feeds it back into fork choice through `validateLatestHash`: INVALID invalidates the head node and its ancestors up to the latest valid hash, VALID flips an optimistic head. The cached head is recomputed afterwards with the usual head and reorg events. The pre-gloas block segment path goes through the same chain method so it refreshes the cached head as well.

forkchoiceUpdated verdicts are applied leniently in proto-array (`strict: false`): a node the engine already validated is never invalidated, the walk never crosses the justified block or anything below it, and a null, unknown or conflicting latest valid hash only invalidates the queried payload and the gloas variants that inherit it. One wrong reply from an EL behind a load balancer or after a restart must not shut the beacon node down, which is what the existing Valid-to-Invalid consensus failure would do. The strict semantics stay for newPayload verdicts about the payload just processed. A poisoned tree now sets `irrecoverableError` from `updateHead`, so the node shuts down instead of failing every head computation silently. Blocks and gloas envelopes building on an invalidated payload are rejected before the engine is asked, otherwise a conflicting VALID would poison the tree.

Supersedes #9332.

A/B on a kurtosis devnet (minimal preset, Fulu from genesis, teku+geth producer, lodestar+geth target behind an engine proxy that rewrites one `newPayload` VALID to SYNCING and then the `forkchoiceUpdated` for that head to INVALID with `latestValidHash` = parent):

| | `chainsafe/lodestar:next` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| fcU INVALID | `Error pushing notifyForkchoiceUpdate()`, dropped | `Invalidated execution payloads in fork choice source=forkchoice_updated` |
| head after the verdict | keeps advancing on the invalid branch | moved back to the parent and stays there |
| descendants of the invalid block | imported | ignored |
| fork choice state | optimistic-invalid head | head on the latest valid payload, no poisoned tree |

Fork choice spec vectors (minimal) pass, the runner keeps the post-import fcU on so predefined INVALID statuses now exercise the new path. Unit tests cover the proto-array policies: null LVH on pre-gloas and on gloas EMPTY and FULL heads, lenient skip of a Valid from node, LVH below a Valid node treated as unknown, the justified guard, VALID resolved by block root, and strict mode unchanged.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:

- gloas envelope `newPayload` INVALID with a latest valid hash never invalidates the ancestor payload chain
- gloas gossip rules on the FULL variant status (`[REJECT]` attested payload invalid, block building on an invalidated payload)
- attestation production on an optimistic head, needed before the spec's `[IGNORE] attested payload is optimistic` can ship
author: nflaig

title: fix: invalidate the parent payload chain on a gloas envelope INVALID verdict
body:
Stacked on #10436.

A `newPayload` INVALID for a gloas envelope threw before touching fork choice, so the ancestor payloads between the engine's latest valid hash and the envelope's parent stayed viable. The pre-gloas block segment path already invalidates that chain through `validateLatestHash`.

The envelope import now routes the verdict through `invalidateExecutionPayloads` from the parent pair the block builds on, `(block.parentRoot, payload.parentHash)`, the same pair the segment path uses. It resolves to FULL(N-1) when the block extends the full parent and to EMPTY(N-1) otherwise, and pass 1 of the invalidation walks up the variant parent pointers to the LVH node. Because the from node is the parent and not the payload the engine judged, an unknown or conflicting latest valid hash drops the verdict instead of falling back to invalidating the from node (`fromNodeJudged: false`), which is what the forkchoiceUpdated path does for its own head. A verdict whose LVH equals the parent hash changes nothing, as before.

Covered by proto-array unit tests: LVH from a child payload invalidates the parent payload and its dependents but leaves the EMPTY variant and the grandparent payload alone, and an LVH off the ancestor chain is dropped. No kurtosis A/B for this one, it needs a gloas devnet with a proxy that returns an LVH below the parent, the pre-gloas fcU A/B is on #10436.
author: nflaig

title: feat: reject gloas attestations and blocks on an invalidated payload
body:
Stacked on #10437.

Index-1 attestations and aggregates to a block whose FULL variant was invalidated by the execution engine are now rejected, the `[REJECT] The attested execution payload is processed and invalid` branch of `verify_attestation_payload_status`. The status comes from the fork choice node that was actually imported, so a builder cannot plant it with a tampered envelope (the problem with #10426). The attestation check sits after the `seenAttestationDatas` lookup, a cached attestation data must recheck it because the payload status can change after the data was cached.

A block building on an invalidated payload is ignored at gossip on the variant resolved from the bid's parent block hash. Before, the rule only looked at the default variant, so a block on an invalidated FULL(N) was forwarded and died at import.

Peers relaying such attestations are downscored with `HighToleranceError` instead of the topic default. The invalid status is this node's execution engine opinion, and a divergent engine must not partition the node from honest mesh peers relaying index-1 votes for the live head. Open for discussion, the spec says REJECT without qualifying the penalty.

Not included: the `[IGNORE] attested payload is optimistic` branch. `produceAttestationData` sets index 1 for a FULL head and only checks the target for optimism, so with a Syncing FULL head the node's own `submitPoolAttestations` would get 400 and drop its validators' votes. That needs attestation production to refuse optimistic heads first.

No unit tests for the guards themselves, the branches are one lookup each; the invalidation they key off is covered by the proto-array tests in #10436 and #10437.

title: test: use fake timers instead of Date.now spies
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10434. Most time-dependent tests use `vi.useFakeTimers`, but a few spied on `Date.now` directly. A `Date.now` spy also ties a test to the clock the code reads today: if `wrapPromise` moved to `performance.now()`, its duration tests would fail (`expected 0.03 to be 100`) and need rewriting.

**Description**

- `utils/test/unit/promise.test.ts`: `vi.useFakeTimers({now: 1000})`, a real `setTimeout` promise and `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(100)` instead of `Date.now` spies, keeping the exact `durationMs === 100` assertion.
- `beacon-node/test/unit/chain/validatorMonitor.test.ts`: `vi.useFakeTimers()` with `vi.setSystemTime` for the retain-period tests.
- `beacon-node/test/unit/executionEngine/restCompatibility.test.ts`: `vi.useFakeTimers({toFake: ["Date"], now})` with `vi.setSystemTime`. Only `Date` is faked since these tests talk to a real local HTTP server.
- Real timers are restored in `afterEach`.

Left as is on purpose: the `Date.now` spies in `sync/range/chain.test.ts` and `sync/unknownBlock.test.ts` change the returned time between consecutive synchronous reads to test every clock-read crossing point (#10249, #10250). Fake timers cannot advance time between two reads in the same tick, so those spies stay.

**Testing**

- `promise.test.ts` 5/5 in Node and Chromium. Firefox not run locally (browser fails to launch on this machine), CI covers it.
- `validatorMonitor.test.ts` and `restCompatibility.test.ts` 50/50.
- Mutations: dropping the time jump in the prune test, keeping the REST reprobe jump inside the retry window, and breaking the duration by 1 ms each fail. The two time jumps whose removal stays green (re-register, 404 remembered) also stay green with the original spies, so no coverage changes.
- biome, `check-types` for utils and beacon-node.

title: refactor: use gossip validation for execution payload bids published via api
body:
Follow-up to #10429.

With `--api.disableBidValidation` available, builders running in production are expected to disable validation on the publish path. The validate-on path is then mainly useful for testing, where the full gossip rules are what we want to exercise rather than a lenient subset. This removes `validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` and runs `validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid` on bids submitted via `POST /eth/v1/beacon/execution_payload_bids` instead.

When validation runs, the bid is now also added to `executionPayloadBidPool` and reported to the validator monitor, mirroring the gossip handler. Gossip does not deliver our own published messages back to us, so without this a proposer on the same node as the builder never sees the bid in its pool. This matters for single-node local testing (e.g. kurtosis).

Changes
- `publishExecutionPayloadBid` calls `validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid`, then adds the bid to the pool and registers it with the validator monitor using the returned `proposerIndex`. Nothing is added to the pool when validation is disabled.
- `validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` and `RegenCaller.validateApiExecutionPayloadBid` removed.
- New metric `lodestar_oppool_execution_payload_bid_pool_api_insert_outcome_total`, same shape as the gossip one.
- Existing validator unit tests ported to `validateGossipExecutionPayloadBid` (previously the gossip validator had no direct unit coverage), with additional cases for the gossip-only IGNORE rules. `mockedBeaconChain` gains `seenExecutionPayloadBids` and `getParentExecutionRequests`.

Notes
- The pool insert happens inline before broadcast, not deferred to the next event loop tick like the gossip handler does. There is no validation result to propagate first on the api path, so deferring is not needed.
- Reusing the gossip validator means a successfully validated api bid is recorded in `seenExecutionPayloadBids`, so re-submitting the same bid via the api is IGNOREd as already known. This matches what would happen once the bid arrives via gossip anyway.

body:
We may experiment with 10s slots by having devnets that runs 10s slots against a 12s baseline. This PR adds fraction-of-slot histograms

durations. Every fraction divides by the slot duration of the fork of the measured slot. Seconds
metrics and their buckets are unchanged.

title: fix: avoid legacy column scans during archiving
body:
## Problem

Data columns are written to flat files since #8899, and #10223 clears the legacy hot-column bucket during startup. The archiver still scans that bucket for every finalized canonical block. After bulk deletion, repeated scans over LevelDB tombstones can stall block archiving even when no columns are migrated.

## Changes

- Remove the obsolete canonical hot-to-cold data-column migration.
- Await compaction of the legacy hot-column range after startup deletion, including when the bucket is already empty from an earlier startup.
- Preserve legacy cold-column reads, flat-file storage, retention pruning, and noncanonical cleanup.

A restart on the fixed build performs the compaction automatically; a separate manual compaction is not required for this fix. Startup compaction can take time depending on the existing database.

## Validation

- The regression run failed on the original production code (9 expected failures); all 39 targeted tests pass with the fix.
- Coverage includes Fulu/Gloas canonical archiving, already-archived boundary blocks, empty and multi-batch bucket pruning, awaited compaction, and legacy/flat-file column serving.
- `pnpm lint` passed (1886 files).
- `pnpm check-types` passed across the workspace.
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/db build` passed.

## Spec compliance

Not applicable: internal database maintenance and removal of an obsolete migration. No consensus transition or wire-format changes.

title: fix: skip legacy column scans during startup
body:
**Motivation**

Startup still performs legacy column range scans after #10447 removes them from archiving. Looking up the last archived legacy slot and clearing an empty hot bucket can each take minutes on a database with accumulated LevelDB tombstones. Compacting the hot bucket afterward does not avoid the preceding scan.

**Description**

Skip this work unconditionally, without adding an option:

- Remove the legacy archive slot lookup from `BeaconDb.init()`.
- Stop deleting and compacting legacy hot columns in `pruneHotDb()`.
- Remove the startup slot hint from range serving. When an archived block-root index entry is absent, retain the existing legacy column point-read fallback and skip slots with no columns.

Existing legacy columns remain readable. Hot blob cleanup, flat-file storage, and normal retention/non-canonical pruning remain unchanged. Legacy hot data is left on disk rather than reclaimed during startup. Requests for old slots without a block-root index may perform legacy point reads that the removed startup hint previously avoided.

**Validation**

- Confirmed the startup regression tests fail before the fix.
- 58 targeted tests pass across BeaconDb startup, LegacyDataColumnStore, flat-file req/resp handlers, and block archiving.
- `pnpm lint` passes.
- `pnpm check-types` passes.

title: fix: stop flooring the import-time seen timestamp of a block
body:
## Motivation

`processBlocks` stamps a block with the current time when the caller passes no `seenTimestampSec`, which is the case for unknown-block sync and range sync. That stamp was floored to a whole second. At 12 s slots every deadline lands on a whole second, so flooring never changed the outcome. At 10 s slots `ATTESTATION_DUE_BPS_GLOAS = 2500` becomes 2500 ms, and a block imported at 2.9 s into its slot measures as 2 s and still counts as timely for proposer boost. The same applies to the PTC deadline.

## Description

Keep the fractional import time. Stamping at import time is deliberate for these paths and now says so in a comment: the spec cannot run `on_block` until the parent is known and records timeliness at that moment, so for a block that could not be imported on arrival the import time is the spec's clock. The unknown-block sync delay for already known proposers relies on the same stamp to deny proposer boost, and now carries a note to that effect.

Two unit tests pin the fallback to a fractional stubbed time and the precedence of an explicit opts value.

title: feat(builder): track the canonical head from `head_v2` events
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10379. The bidder fetched the proposer duties on every payload attributes event only to read the dependent root that identifies the proposer preferences of the branch it builds on. The beacon node already announces that root with every head.

**Description**

- `HeadTracker` consumes `head_v2` events and keeps the proposer duties dependent roots per announced head block. `getDependentRoot(parentBlockRoot, proposalSlot)` resolves the root for a proposal in the epoch of that head (`current_epoch_dependent_root`) or the one after (`next_epoch_dependent_root`), keyed by the head's epoch rather than the clock epoch, so skipped slots do not shift it.
- The bidder takes the dependent root of its parent from the tracker. The proposer duties call remains as a fallback for a parent that was not announced as head, e.g. before the first head event after connecting. The fallback result is not stored, it cannot overwrite event data.
- Tracked heads are pruned once they are older than the previous epoch, their dependent roots cannot cover a later proposal.

**Not covered**

Cancelling in-flight builds on a head change. Payload attributes are emitted once per slot, and a late block whose parent is the build parent is a valid build target (`validateBidParent` accepts the head's parent), so a root mismatch alone is not enough to cancel. Needs the parent root of the new head, which `head_v2` does not carry.

title: refactor: carry milliseconds through the fork choice timeliness API
body:
## Motivation

Fork choice measured block receive delay, block import delay, and the time into the proposer's slot in fractional seconds and compared them against millisecond deadlines by multiplying by 1000. The producers already had millisecond resolution, so nothing was truncated, but dividing by 1000 and multiplying back introduces about 50 µs of float error at Unix-timestamp magnitude. That flips the comparison at the exact deadline millisecond: at 1667 ms into the slot `isProposingOnTime` returned false where the spec's `get_time_into_slot_ms(store) <= get_proposer_reorg_cutoff_ms()` says true.

At 12 s slots every deadline is a whole second and the boundary is never hit. At 10 s slots the gloas deadlines land on 2500 ms and 7500 ms and the reorg cutoff on 1667 ms, so exact comparisons matter.

## Description

Pass integer milliseconds end to end and drop the `* 1000` in the predicates. No deadline value changes.

- `onBlock` takes `receiveDelayMs` and `importDelayMs`. `getProposerHead`, `predictProposerHead`, `shouldOverrideForkChoiceUpdate` and the `UpdateAndGetHeadOpt` union take `msFromSlot`.
- `isBlockReceivedTimely`, `isBlockPtcTimely`, `isBlockImportedTimely` and `isProposingOnTime` compare milliseconds directly.
- The beacon node computes `receiveDelayMs` as `Math.round(seenTimestampSec * 1000) - computeTimeAtSlotMs(...)`, and the import and proposer paths use `clock.msFromSlot`.
- Mocks and both spec runners updated. Vector ticks are whole seconds per the test format, so the spec tests cannot exercise sub-second cases; a new `blockTimeliness.test.ts` checks each predicate one millisecond either side of the 2500 ms and 7500 ms gloas deadlines at a 10 s slot, and `getProposerHead.test.ts` gains cases exactly at and one millisecond after the 1667 ms cutoff.
author: ensi321

title: fix: floor slot component durations as the spec does
body:
## Motivation

`getSlotComponentDurationMs` converts a basis-point fraction of the slot into milliseconds with `Math.round`. The spec's `get_slot_component_duration_ms` is `basis_points * SLOT_DURATION_MS // BASIS_POINTS`, floor division. The two differ whenever the product is not a whole millisecond.

At 10 s slots every mainnet basis-point value is exact, so nothing changes. At 12 s slots the product is `bps * 1.2`, and 3333 bps gives 3999.6: the spec floors to 3999 ms, Lodestar rounded to 4000 ms. That is the pre-gloas attestation and sync message deadline, so a block arriving at exactly 3999 ms into the slot was timely for Lodestar and late for the spec. The other mainnet values (1667, 6667, 9167 bps) round and floor to the same number, and every gloas deadline is a multiple of 500 bps and unaffected.

## Description

Switch to `Math.floor`, with a comment pointing at the pinned spec function, and pin the values in a config unit test: 3333, 6667, 1667 and 2500 bps at 12 s, and 3333, 1667 and 2500 bps at 10 s.

The minimal preset moves the same deadlines from 2000 to 1999 ms. No test anywhere pinned the old rounded values; the validator service, fork-choice, and beacon-node chain, API, unknown-block sync and gossip processor suites all pass against the rebuilt config package.

Spec test vectors cannot tell round from floor because their ticks are whole seconds, so the config unit test is the only pin.

title: perf: reuse finalized historical state responses
body:
## Why

Reading several API fields from the same archived state currently queues a separate reconstruction for each field. In a local Builder accounting test, a cold verified read at slot 1649 reconstructed the same state three times and took about 5.93 seconds. Retrying timed-out reads can add more work because cancelling the client does not remove already queued regeneration jobs.

## Change

Reuse the most recently requested historical slot's serialized response. Requests for that entry share its in-flight reconstruction, and each caller receives its own buffer. Retain at most one completed response, capped at 64 MiB; oversized responses are served without retention. Clear the entry on failure or shutdown.

This stays behind the existing finalized-history lookup. It does not retain BeaconState trees, alter canonicality checks, change timeouts, or change Builder payment accounting.

## Checks

- Eight focused tests cover shared reads, eviction, independent buffers and transfer, oversized responses, failure recovery and shutdown.
- Archive-store tests, BN type-check/build and changed-file Biome passed.
- Three cold runs against the saved minimal-network database completed the slot-1649 read in 2.18 to 2.33 seconds with one reconstruction, within the test runtime's three-second deadline. Eight simultaneous readers shared one reconstruction.
- A pinned local two-BN Gloas network published and revealed nonzero bids. The exact first payment was verified through the real REST APIs before and after restarting the publishing BN.

The network restart needed a second restart and peer reconnection after a range-sync batch stalled. This is not a claim of unattended restart recovery or mainnet performance. The heavy slot-1649 measurements used the real worker behind a narrow HTTP adapter, not the full BN REST server. Alternating slots and states above the retention limit can still require repeated reconstruction.

Kept draft for feedback on the cache boundary and retention limit. The accounting reader/runtime changes remain separate.

title: fix: avoid slow LevelDB scans over deleted legacy data column entries
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10447. On `public-hoodi-hzax41-0`, a long-running supernode, LevelDB scans over legacy data column entries that were deleted long ago slowed both startup and every archive job:

- Startup stalled about 20 minutes after `Flat file store initialized`. The reverse lookup in bucket 58 took 712 s and the wipe scan of bucket 57 took 381 s, although both buckets had no live keys. Legacy column entries deleted while long archive scans held a snapshot had stayed in the bottom LevelDB level (224.8 GB). `compactRange` never rewrites the bottom level, so the compaction from #10447 was a no-op there.
- The legacy column prune runs `keys({lt: cutoff})` from the start of bucket 58 on every archive job. The bucket is not written since flat files and only shrinks from the front, so every prune walks all deleted entries LevelDB has not compacted.

**Description**

- At startup, before the first lookup into buckets 57 and 58, check the size of the hot column bucket plus the pruned part of the legacy column archive. Above 1 GiB, write a key at each end of the range, compact, and delete the keys again. That forces the bottom files to be rewritten. On hoodi-0 the same steps took 475 s once, cut the range from 224.8 GB to 0, and startup went from 20 min to 3 ms
- Add `pruneBefore(slot)` to the legacy data column archive repository. It resumes from the slot the previous prune ended at, and the first prune of a process compacts the range it deletes from

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Written with AI assistance (Claude), including the investigation, implementation, tests and description.

title: feat: implement BeaconEngine
body:
demonstrate #9508


This adds `BeaconEngine`, which becomes the only owner of consensus-critical data. `BeaconChain` becomes a facade that coordinates work, emits events and handles DA. Consumers call `BeaconEngine` APIs and no longer touch fork choice or `BeaconState` directly.

```
  network        sync          api
     |             |            |
     v             v            v
+------------- BeaconChain (facade) --------------+
| events/SSE, peer scoring, DA caches, blobs      |
| ChainView (head, checkpoints, blocks)  <-- pull |
|                                                 |
|  +---- BeaconEngine (JS now, Zig later) ----+   |
|  | forkchoice, STF, regen, seen caches      |   |
|  | gossip validation, op pools, BLS         |   |
|  | produce, duties, LC server, metrics      |   |
|  | OWNS blocks + states DB, archival        |   |
|  +------------------------------------------+   |
+------------------------+------------------------+
                         |
                         v
                 ExecutionEngine --> EL
```

```
main-thread (default)        worker (--chain.beaconEngineWorker, hidden)
  *Object() apis               *Bytes() apis (roots + ssz bytes)
  ForkChoiceChainView          ReplicateChainView (pulled snapshots)
  shared db/clock/EL           own db/clock/EL/config/pubkeys
```

**How to review**

Start with these, the rest is mostly callers adapting to them. Paths are under `packages/beacon-node/src/chain/`.

1. `beaconEngine/interface.ts`: the `IBeaconEngine` API surface
2. `beaconEngine/beaconEngine.ts`: main thread side, converts bytes to objects, pulls ChainView, emits events
3. `beaconEngine/beaconEngineCore.ts`: owns forkchoice, regen, caches, db, could be on main thread, or another worker thread. Native will need to implement the same interface.
4. `chainView/interface.ts`: `IChainView`, the read-only view `BeaconChain` uses
5. `chainView/forkChoiceChainView.ts` (main thread BeaconEngine) and `chainView/replicateChainView.ts` (worker/native BeaconEngine)

author: nflaig

title: fix: recompute unrealized checkpoints for blocks with slashings
body:
**Motivation**

`ForkChoice.onBlock` skips `computeUnrealizedCheckpoints()` for a same-epoch child whose parent is already justified in the block epoch, and reuses the parent's unrealized checkpoints instead. That assumes a child can't have lower unrealized checkpoints than its parent. Slashings in the child block break that assumption: they lower the unslashed target balance of the child state, so its unrealized justification can drop. The spec's `compute_pulled_up_tip` always recomputes.

Lighthouse fixed the same shortcut in https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/9471.

**Description**

- Only take the reuse path when the block has no proposer or attester slashings
- Add unit tests: a same-epoch block without slashings keeps the parent's checkpoints, and one with a proposer or attester slashing recomputes them

Verified locally: fork-choice unit tests (319 passing, the new ones fail without the fix), fork_choice minimal spec tests v1.7.0-beta.4 (516 passing), biome and tsc clean.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Implemented and tested with AI assistance (lodekeeper).
author: lodekeeper

title: fix: use the correct PTC duties dependent root for the Gloas fork epoch
body:
The PTC of the Gloas fork epoch is computed by `upgrade_to_gloas` from effective balances that are updated at the end of the last pre-Gloas epoch, so blocks of that epoch can still change it. The dependent root returned for it was the attester decision root two epochs earlier, which does not cover those blocks. A reorg replacing blocks of the last pre-Gloas epoch could change the committee without the validator client noticing, and the fork epoch duties are never polled again after the start of the epoch.

- the beacon node returns the block root at the last slot before the fork as the dependent root of the fork epoch PTC duties
- the validator client matches the fork epoch duties against the head event's current duty dependent root, which carries that root

All other epochs are unchanged. Spec text in https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/671, see https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/670 for the analysis.
author: nflaig

title: test: stop leaking loggers and db mocks per fork choice test case
body:
**Motivation**

The nightly fork-choice compliance workflow has failed since 10-22: a 150 min timeout on [10-22](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/39715664016), then V8 heap OOM (`Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit`) at ~10235/10304 cases on [10-23](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/39893885557) and [10-24](https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/actions/runs/40057373081). No assertion fails; the single vitest worker runs out of heap near the end of gloas.

Root cause is in the test harness, not in fork choice. `forkChoiceTestRunner` builds a fresh `testLogger("executionEngine")` and a fresh `getMockedBeaconDb()` (which builds its own `testLogger()`) for every test case:

- Each winston logger registers a `process.on("uncaughtException")` listener (`handleExceptions: true` on the console transport) that is never removed. Every CI run, green ones included, prints `MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 uncaughtException listeners added to [process]` seconds after start.
- Each mocked db creates ~88 `vi.fn()` mocks, and vitest keeps every mock in a module-level registry forever. `clearMocks` only clears call history.

Measured locally on the altair fork (1472 cases) with forced GC after every 25 cases:

| Build | Retained growth per case | Projected over 10304 cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| f39fad29a (last green nightly) | 331 KB | 3.3 GB |
| 9cb14e338 (first red nightly) | 373 KB | 3.7 GB |
| this PR | 26 KB | 0.3 GB |

Heap snapshots at case 30 and case 90 confirm that chains, states and metric registries are released; only the loggers and mocks grow strictly per case. The suite has run within ~25 min of its timeout since gloas vectors were enabled on 09-11, already GC-thrashing during gloas. #10022 added six explicit mocks and two automocked repositories to `getMockedBeaconDb()`, which raised per-case retention by ~11% and crossed the limit. That PR is not at fault; any change to the mocked db would have done it.

**Description**

Create the execution engine logger and the mocked db once per module in `forkChoiceTestRunner`, and the logger once in `mockedBeaconDb`. The runner never customises the mocks per case and `clearMocks` resets call history between cases, so sharing one instance is safe.

With this change retained heap stays flat across the altair fork (137 MB at case 1450 vs 632 MB before) and the fork runs ~18% faster from less GC pressure. The full suite was not run locally; the next nightly is the end-to-end check.

Follow-ups, out of scope here:
- A `handleExceptions: false` option for `testLogger` would remove the listener leak from the ~100 other per-test logger call sites in beacon-node tests.
- Two `sleep()` calls keep closed chains reachable for 3 to 4 s after `chain.close()`: the half-slot validator-monitor sleep in `BeaconChain.onClockSlot` has no abort signal, and `PersistentCheckpointStateCache` is constructed without one. Bounded, but it inflates peak memory in the suite.

title: fix: treat data availability timeouts of gossip blocks and payloads as unavailable data
body:
A gossip block or payload envelope whose data does not arrive within the availability wait rejects the import with a `TimeoutError`. `processBlocks` wraps it into `BEACON_CHAIN_ERROR`, which the block gossip handler treats as a bad block: the relaying peer is downscored and the error is logged at warn. The envelope handler gets the raw error and logs it at error level. In both cases BlockInputSync is already pulling the data and retries the import, so there is nothing to act on and nothing the peer did wrong.

- the availability waits throw `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` block and payload errors instead of leaking the `TimeoutError`
- both gossip handlers log it at debug without reporting the peer

Range sync is unchanged, `DATA_UNAVAILABLE` is not peer attributable, same as the wrapped error before.

title: fix: retry post-gloas getBlobs after a failed attempt
body:
**Motivation**

Follow-up to #10329. Pre-gloas, every gossip data column re-triggers getBlobs, so a `null` answer is retried up to `MAX_GET_BLOBS_ATTEMPTS` times. Post-gloas, getBlobs is triggered once per block, from the bid after block import, so a `null` answer is never retried.

**Description**

- Post-gloas, every failed getBlobsV2 attempt (`null` or a rejected request) arms the existing trailing retry. That gives the same cap of 3 attempts at least 1 s apart as pre-gloas. Retries stop once the sampled columns are complete
- Pre-gloas behavior is unchanged
- Remove the TODO at the bid trigger, since the retry now lives in `GetBlobsTracker`

Retries are not timed to a point in the slot. On glamsterdam-devnet-8 over the last 24h, the post-gloas `null` rate of the single request depended mostly on the EL: reth 1%, geth, besu and nimbusel about 5%, erigon 16%, ethrex about 30%, nethermind 61%. That points at EL blob pool behavior more than at when in the slot we ask, so it doesn't support picking a slot time yet.

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Written with AI assistance (Claude), including the devnet data, implementation, tests and description.

title: perf: only pre-verify validator deposits sharing an invalid builder deposit's pubkey
body:
with https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10428 the fork only walks the same-pubkey validator deposits (`hasPendingValidator`) for an invalid builder deposit on a key without a validator, a valid builder deposit registers the builder right away. the pre-verify scanner still marked every builder pubkey when queueing the deposit and pre-verified all validator deposits sharing it

marks the pubkey only once the builder deposit verified invalid and has no validator, so validator deposits are only pre-verified where the fork can read them. validator deposits queued behind the builder deposit are now picked up a tick later instead of the same tick

stacked on https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10428
author: nflaig

title: fix: count usable gossip subscribers for subnet coverage
body:
**Motivation**

A peer can advertise subnet membership while lacking an outbound gossipsub stream. Metadata-based coverage can therefore suppress discovery even when attestation publishing has no usable subscribers.

**Description**

- Count healthy, connected subscribers with outbound streams for attestation and sync subnet coverage, using the current fork's topic.
- Prepare coverage counts in `PeerManager` and pass `{subnet, toSlot, peerCount}` to `prioritizePeers`.
- Exclude banned and low-score peers immediately, including while their asynchronous goodbye and disconnection are pending.
- Preserve existing peer pruning priorities, scores, targets, and PeerDAS coverage.

Related to #10476. Outbound stream recovery is handled separately in [libp2p/js-libp2p#3687](https://github.com/libp2p/js-libp2p/pull/3687).

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

author: wemeetagain

title: fix: return each gloas block once from fork choice block summaries
body:
`getBlockSummariesByParentRoot` and `getBlockSummariesAtSlot` return every proto-array node, for a gloas block that is its PENDING and EMPTY variant plus FULL once the payload arrived. `getBlockHeaders` pushes a header per node, so `?parent_root=` returns each gloas child two or three times and `?slot=` does the same for non-canonical blocks at that slot.

Both now return one summary per block, the default variant (FULL pre-gloas, PENDING for gloas). The other caller, `isValidDependentRoot`, only checks that a child exists and is unaffected.
author: nflaig

title: fix: use the envelope's own payload status for `execution_optimistic`
body:
`getSignedExecutionPayloadEnvelope` returns the `execution_optimistic` of the block, which for a gloas block is the status of the payload it builds on (`bid.parent_block_hash`), inherited by the PENDING variant at import. The envelope is the block's own payload, so a SYNCING envelope on a VALID parent was served as `execution_optimistic: false`.

The flag now comes from the block's FULL variant, the fork choice node created when the envelope was imported, and is `false` once finalized. An unfinalized block without a FULL variant has not imported its envelope yet and returns 404, the same as block lookups for a block that is not in fork choice. Before, an envelope still in the input cache was served with the block's flag.

Related to https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/issues/672.
author: nflaig

title: fix: wait for payload data before taking a serial import queue slot
body:
Closes #10481

`PayloadEnvelopeProcessor` now waits for data before taking a queue slot:

1. DA wait moved out of the job, `processExecutionPayload` wrapper removed, job takes the DA status as an argument
2. Timeouts still surface as `DATA_UNAVAILABLE`

The pre-Gloas block processor is left as is.

Spec tests not run.
author: ensi321

title: fix: keep the engine off an unsatisfied payload at envelope import
body:
At envelope import, step 7 sends the envelope's block hash to the execution engine as forkchoice head whenever the cached head has the same block root. It does not look at the inclusion list verdict recorded a few lines earlier, so an unsatisfied payload becomes the engine head although fork choice does not extend it and the next proposer builds on the parent payload. The engine builds mempool and inclusion list state on it until the next forkchoiceUpdated, the prepare call about 6.7s into the slot on the heze devnet rehearsal, then reorgs.

Skip the update when the payload is recorded as not satisfying the constraints. `isPayloadInclusionListSatisfied` is true for every pre-heze payload and for a VALID payload without a verdict, so nothing else changes. The spec sends no forkchoiceUpdated at envelope import, this one is a Lodestar optimization behind the `disableImportExecutionFcU` chain option.

Independent of #10416, which fixes the beacon head for the same slot.
author: nflaig

title: fix(api): type historical summaries proof nodes as Bytes32
body:
**Motivation**

The proof returned by getHistoricalSummaries is a Merkle branch of 32-byte nodes, but the response type declared ArrayOf(Bytes8).

JSON responses still carried 32-byte hex because ByteVectorType.toJson is toHexString(value) which returns the correct length.

Since every consumer reads JSON, the broken paths were never hit: a client sending Accept: application/octet-stream got a 500 from a RangeError in serialize, and the typed client threw on fromJson of any non-empty proof.

The only test mocked an empty proof, which
exercises none of those.

**Description**

- Change the type from `ssz.Bytes8` to `ssz.Bytes32`
- Use a non-empty proof in the test and add a ssz test path

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

author: spiral-ladder

title: fix(beacon-node): return 400 when sync committee signature validator is not in committee
body:
**Motivation**

According to the [Ethereum Beacon-APIs specification for `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees`](https://ethereum.github.io/beacon-APIs/#/Beacon/submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures), each `SyncCommitteeMessage` should be validated before broadcasting and invalid messages should cause the endpoint to return a `400` `IndexedError` response while valid messages in the same request are still published.

Previously, `submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures` returned early without throwing when `headState.epochCtx.currentSyncCommitteeIndexed.validatorIndexMap.get(signature.validatorIndex)` was `undefined` or empty, causing the endpoint to respond with `200 OK` even when a validator was not in the current sync committee.

**Description**

- Throw `SyncCommitteeError(GossipAction.REJECT, {code: SyncCommitteeErrorCode.VALIDATOR_NOT_IN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, validatorIndex: signature.validatorIndex})` in `submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures` when the validator has no subnets in `currentSyncCommitteeIndexed.validatorIndexMap`, matching the validation performed in `validateGossipSyncCommittee` and collecting the failure into `errors` for the `ErrorAborted` (`400 IndexedError`) response.
- Add unit tests in `packages/beacon-node/test/unit/api/impl/beacon/pool/submitPoolSyncCommitteeSignatures.test.ts` verifying that non-committee validator signatures produce an `ErrorAborted` rejection and that valid signatures in a mixed batch are still validated, inserted into `opPool.syncCommitteeMessages`, and published to gossip subnets.

Closes #10488
author: CG-5228

title: feat: reject gossip envelopes if payload does not match its block hash
body:
**Motivation**

Implements [consensus-specs#5770](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5770). Gossip only checked `payload.block_hash == bid.block_hash`, so a builder could gossip other contents under the committed hash, take the seen entry and get the real envelope ignored.

Draft until #5770 is released.

**Description**

Envelope gossip checks, new ones marked `+`:

```
  block known, not seen, not finalized       IGNORE
  slot, builder index match block            REJECT
+ parent beacon block root == block parent
+ prev_randao, gas_limit == bid
  block_hash, requests root == bid
  load block post-state                      IGNORE if missing
+ parent_hash == state.latest_block_hash
+ timestamp == slot time
+ withdrawals == state expected withdrawals
+ no empty transactions
+ payload hashes to block_hash               INVALID_BLOCK_HASH
  signature
```

- `computeExecutionBlockHash`: keccak256 of the RLP header with MPT roots for transactions and withdrawals and the EIP-7685 requests hash. Bellatrix to heze.
- Empty transactions are trie deletions and don't change the hash, hence the separate check.
- Hash runs before the signature, as in the spec. The signing root hashes every transaction, so the signature check costs more.
- Native `node:crypto` keccak. `@ethereumjs/rlp` is already installed via discv5.
- Metric `lodestar_gossip_execution_payload_envelope_block_hash_seconds` with a dashboard panel.
- Mock EL returns real block hashes.
- Spec gossip runner wired. `valid*` and `ignore_duplicate` are skipped until the pinned vectors get real hashes.

**Verification**

- Hashes match 447 spec `sanity/blocks` payloads (bellatrix to fulu) and 1000 real blocks each from Sepolia, mainnet and Platåberget (see comments). One Sepolia envelope is a test fixture.
- Mean hash time on the main thread (M3 Pro): 0.5 ms Sepolia, 1 ms mainnet, 1.7 ms Platåberget.

body:
**Motivation**

[Biome 2.6](https://biomejs.dev/blog/biome-v2-6/) supports Markdown and YAML. Prettier was only used to format Markdown, so Biome can cover it and we drop one tool.

**Description**

- Upgrade `@biomejs/biome` to `^2.6.3` and include `**/*.md`, `**/*.yml` and `**/*.yaml`.
- Markdown formatter set to Prettier's defaults (`lineWidth: 80`, `proseWrap: "preserve"`), frontmatter parsing enabled for `.claude/skills`.
- YAML is linted and formatted. 7 files were never formatted before (Prettier only ran on Markdown) and get whitespace, indentation and quote fixes. Each one parses to the same data as before.
- Excluded: `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `specrefs/*.yml` (regenerated and diffed by ethspecify in CI) and `test/fixtures`.
- Remove `prettier`, its config (`.prettierrc.js`, `.prettierignore`), the `docs:lint` / `docs:lint:fix` scripts and their CI steps. `pnpm lint` in the Tests workflow runs on every PR and now covers Markdown. Generated docs are gitignored, so both tools skipped them anyway.
- VS Code uses Biome for Markdown and YAML. The Prettier extension is no longer recommended.

Compatibility on our files:

- Markdown: 83 of 86 files identical to Prettier output. Two docs lists get blank lines around fenced code. `packages/cli/README.md` had a table without surrounding blank lines, so GitHub rendered the "Append `--help`" sentence as a table row. Fixed the source.
- YAML: Biome output is identical to Prettier on all 80 files.

Side effects of upgrading from Biome 2.2:

- 37 TS files: 2.6 now sorts exports and changed some line breaking. Applied with `biome check --write`, ordering and whitespace only. Verified the runtime module evaluation order (`import` / `export ... from`) is unchanged in every file.
- New findings on 2.6 fixed in stacked PRs, now merged into this branch: #10493 (`noFloatingPromises`), #10494 (`noMisusedPromises`), #10495 (`noUnsafeOptionalChaining`), #10496 (`noNonNullAssertedOptionalChain`), #10497 (`useMathMinMax`). All rules are back at their original level.
- `useMathMinMax` is off for `packages/state-transition/src`. Its fixes would break bigint operands, which are common there.
- `useImportExtensions` has a false positive on JSON imports through the `spec-tests-version.json` symlinks (its fix rewrites them to `.js`). Suppressed on those 4 imports. Fixed one real `.ts` import.
- `@chainsafe/biomejs-config` uses the deprecated `linter.rules.recommended` key, so Biome prints a deprecation notice. Needs a fix upstream.

**Validation**

- `pnpm lint`: 0 errors, 3 `useOptionalChain` warnings on existing code. A second `biome check --write` is a no-op.
- `pnpm check-types` passes.

title: fix: verify cached envelope signature on publish
body:
The publish flow validates the submitted envelope but then imports the cached `PayloadEnvelopeInput` with `validSignature: true`. If range sync already cached a different envelope for the same block root before verifying it, that envelope is imported with its signature marked as verified and skips the BLS and `executionRequestsRoot` checks at import.

- only pass `validSignature: true` when the cached envelope is the one this request validated, otherwise the import verifies it
- add tests for the submitted envelope and for an envelope cached by another source

Rebased onto https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10500, which removed the `none` level. Every remaining level verifies the submitted envelope, so the gate is just the identity check.
author: twoeths

title: refactor: remove non-spec `none` broadcast validation level
body:
`none` is not a beacon-APIs value. It was added in https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/6308 so the unknown block sync simulation could push a block with an unknown parent through to `processBlock`, back then the only publish path that emitted `blockUnknownParent`. Since https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/9025 the `consensus` level emits it before rejecting with `PARENT_BLOCK_UNKNOWN`, so the test no longer needs it. Nothing else used it, the validator client already rejects it on the command line.

Keeping it was a footgun, blocks were gossiped before any check ran and envelopes were imported with the signature marked as verified.

- remove `none` from `BroadcastValidation`, the simulation uses `consensus` and the unit test `gossip`
- reject unknown levels with a 400 instead of logging a warning and publishing without validation
- drop the hidden `broadcastValidationStrictness` option, it only governed that fallback

title: feat: add `payload_status` to debug chain heads
body:
From Gloas onwards a fork choice leaf is a `(root, payload_status)` node, so `GET /eth/v2/debug/beacon/heads` can return the same block twice, as its `empty` and its `full` node, with nothing in the response to tell them apart. Adds `payload_status` to each entry, `full` for pre-Gloas leaves as in `head_v2`.

Implements https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/pull/673.
author: nflaig

title: fix: return 400 when sync committee message validator is not in the sync committee
body:
**Motivation**

Lodestar's `POST /eth/v1/beacon/pool/sync_committees` returns 200 and drops a message whose `validator_index` is out of range or not in the current sync committee. The [beacon-APIs spec](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/bc3384f9cb1f02169d4fcb81e7da4da329b857ee/apis/beacon/pool/sync_committees.yaml#L9-L11) requires a 400 with details of which messages failed and why. A message with an out-of-range index fails the gossip rule `[REJECT] The validator index is valid`. A message from a validator that is not in the sync committee fails `[REJECT] The subnet_id is valid for the given validator`. 

**Description**

- Replace the early `return` with `throw new SyncCommitteeError(GossipAction.REJECT, {code: VALIDATOR_NOT_IN_SYNC_COMMITTEE, validatorIndex})`. Gossip validation throws the same error in `validateGossipSyncCommitteeExceptSig`. The existing `catch` adds the error to the `IndexedError` failures, so the endpoint returns 400. The handler still adds the valid messages in the same request to the pool and publishes them.
- Add unit tests for an out-of-range index, a valid validator that is not in the sync committee, and a request with one invalid and one valid message. Each test fails without the fix.

Closes #10488

author: dependabot

title: fix: allow builders to raise their bid by a minimum increment
body:
The `execution_payload_bid` gossip validation ignores every bid after the first from a builder for a slot and parent, and requires any bid to exceed the pool's best bid by a 3% increment. https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5776 changes this: a builder's later bid propagates if it is higher than any bid seen and exceeds the builder's last propagated bid by at least the increment, a bid from another builder only needs to be higher.

- add `MIN_BID_INCREMENT_PERCENT`, `MIN_BID_INCREMENT_FLOOR` and `MIN_BID_INCREMENT_CAP` to the chain config
- track the value of the last valid bid per builder, slot and parent instead of a seen flag
- apply the increment only to a builder's own re-bid, before state regen and again after signature verification
- require a bid to be strictly higher than the pool's best bid

Should only be merged once the spec change is released.
author: nflaig

title: fix: keep genesis block and state when pruning history
body:
**Motivation**

`chain.pruneHistory` deletes slot 0 along with the rest of the old history, so a pruned node no longer has the genesis block or state. `/eth/v2/beacon/blocks/genesis` returns 404 and checkpointz cannot fetch its genesis bundle from a pruned upstream (it requests block id `genesis`, then the state by that block's state root). We want to enable pruning on our public nodes, including the ones behind checkpointz.

**Description**

- Start pruning blocks, payload envelopes and archived states at slot 1, so the genesis block and state stay in the archive. The genesis block is then served by `blocks/genesis`, the genesis state by root, and `states/genesis` when `--serveHistoricalState` is enabled
- Historical state regen now checks that the first archived block after the nearest state extends it. With the genesis state kept but the following blocks pruned, a request for a pruned slot would otherwise load the genesis state and process every slot up to the next archived block before failing on the parent root. It now fails before doing any work, as it did before this change when no state was found

Notes:

- Nodes that already pruned genesis keep getting 404s for it until they resync
- On a chain younger than `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS`, archived states are still pruned but no blocks are, so historical regen for a slot below the oldest kept state now replays from genesis instead of failing

**AI Assistance Disclosure**

Written with AI assistance (Claude), including the implementation, tests and description.
author: lodekeeper

title: fix: record the inclusion list verdict when a payload turns VALID on forkchoiceUpdated
body:
Stacked on #10436.

A payload imported while the engine was SYNCING is recorded as satisfying the inclusion list constraints and stays that way, even though the VALID `forkchoiceUpdated` response that later validates it carries the engine's verdict. heze `optimistic-sync.md` requires that verdict to be recorded when the payload transitions to VALID.

`onForkchoiceUpdated` now records `inclusionListSatisfied` on the Syncing to VALID transition, before flipping the execution status. The verdict belongs to the FULL variant that owns the block hash, so for a PENDING or EMPTY head that only inherits the hash it is recorded on the ancestor whose payload it is. No head recompute, same as at envelope import: the next recompute moves the head of an unsatisfied payload to the EMPTY variant through the own-slot tiebreaker (#10416).

Closes #10401. The same lines move into `OptimisticExecutionEngine` if #10442 is taken.
author: nflaig

title: fix: retain inclusion lists one slot past the request window
body:
Implements ethereum/consensus-specs#5785.

The lists of slot N are read when the payload of slot N + 1 is imported, which may happen during slot N + 2 while the previous-slot tiebreaker still decides on that payload. The store pruned them as soon as slot N + 2 started, so a payload revealed that late was checked against nothing and recorded as satisfied. Keep the lists one slot longer. Serving over `InclusionListsByIndices` is unchanged.
author: nflaig

title: feat: re-prepare the next slot payload on the PTC verdict
body:
`prepareForNextSlot` prepares the payload for the next slot once, at 67% of the slot, before the PTC votes are due at 75%. When the committee then votes the parent's payload absent or its blob data unavailable, `shouldBuildOnFull` flips to the empty parent at block production, the payload id cache misses and the block is built on a fresh `forkchoiceUpdated` with 500ms lead time instead of 4s. Same when a timely payload of the current slot's block is imported after the run. ethereum/consensus-specs#5763 added the guidance to call `prepare_execution_payload` again once the parent's payload attestations are in.

- re-run the payload preparation on `forkChoicePtcQuorum` for the current slot's block, and on `execution_payload` import of a payload seen before the payload deadline with all its data (a later one will be voted absent, so wait for the verdict). The re-run is skipped when head, parent choice and fee recipient are unchanged, so the quorum in favour on a normal slot is a no-op
- a re-prepare requested while a preparation is in flight runs after it
- record when a payload was requested from the engine, block production waits out the remaining 500ms generation time for a cached payload prepared right before the slot instead of skipping the wait
- `beacon_block_payload_reprepare_total{reason,result}` counts the re-runs

Keeps the scheduled run at 67%, after the payload deadline and before the PTC deadline.
author: nflaig

title: feat(api): serve block root proofs against historical summaries
body:
Adds `GET /eth/v1/lodestar/historical_summaries/block_roots/{slot}`, which returns the block root at a slot with its Merkle branch to the `block_summary_root` of the historical summary covering it, built from the block archive slot index and checked against the summary in the head state. Complements the existing `historical_summaries` endpoint so a client can prove any archived block against a recent state root in two calls instead of collecting all 8192 roots of a period itself, as requested by corpus-core for colibri-stateless (see the commit message for links to their current workaround). Only served for periods the node has fully archived since its checkpoint anchor; `/eth/v0/beacon/proof/state` could produce the same branch but needs the period-boundary state, which the default archive frequency keeps for one period in four.

> This PR was written primarily by Claude Code.
author: spiral-ladder

title: refactor: add native component seams for fork choice, state engine and validation
body:
## Motivation

Prepare the beacon node to move its consensus core to lodestar-z one component group at a time, instead of swapping a whole `BeaconEngineCore` at once as proposed in #10464 (issue #9508). Each group gets a TS interface, a JS implementation wrapping today's code, and a factory that will pick a native implementation behind a flag. Same pattern as `IBeaconStateView` / `BeaconStateView` / `NativeBeaconStateView` in `@lodestar/state-transition`.

## Who calls which seam

Callers stay JS. Block verify and import stay on the chain and report into the validation engine. Every pool and seen cache read or write goes through `IValidationEngine`; every state goes through `IStateEngine`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph callers [Callers, stay JS]
    G[Gossip handlers]
    A[API routes]
    P[Block production]
    S[Sync and req-resp]
  end

  subgraph chain [BeaconChain]
    I[Block verify and import]
  end

  subgraph ve [IValidationEngine]
    V[validateGossip* validateApi* import*]
    R[get* is* has* reads]
    H[lifecycle hooks]
    C[(pools and seen caches)]
  end

  subgraph se [IStateEngine]
    RG[regen]
    SC[(block, checkpoint and shuffling caches)]
  end

  FC[(IForkChoice)]

  G --> V
  A --> V
  A --> R
  P --> R
  S --> V
  S --> R
  I --> H
  I --> FC
  I --> RG
  V --> C
  R --> C
  H --> C
  V --> FC
  V --> RG
  RG --> FC
  FC -. stateGetter, fast confirmation only .-> SC
```

## The interfaces

What each seam exposes, and how they depend on each other. Exact signatures are in `chain/validationEngine/interface.ts`, `chain/stateEngine/interface.ts` and `packages/fork-choice/src/forkChoice/interface.ts`.

```mermaid
classDiagram
  direction TB

  class IForkChoice {
    <<interface>>
    getHead() updateAndGetHead() updateTime()
    getBlockHex*() hasBlock*() getCanonicalBlockAtSlot()
    iterateAncestorBlocks() forwardIterateDescendants()
    getFinalizedCheckpoint() getJustifiedCheckpoint()
    getCheckpointBalances(cp)  NEW
    onBlock(block, state, ...)
    onAttestation() onAttesterSlashing() notifyPtcMessages()
    onExecutionPayload() validateLatestHash() prune()
    fast confirmation: getConfirmedBlock() pause() resume()
  }

  class IStateEngine {
    <<interface>>
    init() close() canAcceptWork()
    getPreState() getBlockSlotState() getState()
    getStateSync() getCheckpointStateSync() getClosestHeadState()
    processState() addCheckpointState() updateHeadState() onCheckpoint()
    getShuffling() getShufflingSync() hasShuffling() processShufflings()
    getBeaconCommitteeOrNull()
    regenStateForAttestationVerification()
    getPersistedCheckpointState()
  }

  class IValidationEngine {
    <<interface>>
    per topic: validateGossipX() validateApiX() importX()
    per topic reads: getX() getPooledX() isX() hasX()
    validatorSeenAtEpoch()
    onSlot() onEpoch() onNewHead() onFinalized()
    onBlockVerified() onBlockImported() onBlockAttestationImported()
    pruneOperations() init() persist() close()
  }

  IStateEngine --> IForkChoice : builds it, regen walks ancestors
  IForkChoice ..> IStateEngine : stateGetter, fast confirmation and balances fallback only
  IValidationEngine --> IForkChoice : block lookups, votes, slashings, PTC messages
  IValidationEngine --> IStateEngine : head state, shufflings, regen for attestation verification

  note for IValidationEngine "topics: attestation, aggregate, syncCommitteeMessage, contributionAndProof, operations, payloadAttestation, executionPayloadBid, proposerPreferences, inclusionList, block, executionPayloadEnvelope, blobSidecar, dataColumnSidecar"
```

The arrows are also the migration order: native fork choice needs the native state in `onBlock`, the native state engine walks native fork choice, native validation reads both and writes fork choice votes. The JS `ValidationEngine` still takes `IBeaconChain` for config, clock, BLS, logger, metrics and the two block assembly caches; a native engine takes those as explicit handles, see "Not in this PR".

## What it takes to build each one

The constructor inputs of each seam, as the JS factories take them today (`initializeForkChoice`, `createStateEngine`, `createValidationEngine` plus `createValidationCaches`). The colour says where a native build gets each input from.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  classDef native fill:#d9f2d9,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#000
  classDef value fill:#dde8f7,stroke:#1565c0,color:#000
  classDef missing fill:#f9d6d5,stroke:#c62828,color:#000

  subgraph fc [IForkChoice]
    fc_cfg[BeaconConfig]:::native
    fc_anchor[anchor state + isFinalized]:::native
    fc_slot[current slot]:::value
    fc_opts[ForkChoiceOpts]:::value
    fc_events[events: justified, finalized, fast confirmation, PTC quorum]:::value
    fc_state[stateGetter from IStateEngine]:::value
    fc_fast[fast confirmation rule]:::missing
    fc_obs[metrics, logger]:::native
  end

  subgraph se [IStateEngine]
    se_cfg[BeaconConfig]:::native
    se_anchor[anchor state]:::native
    se_stf[state transition]:::native
    se_fcf[initForkChoice factory]:::value
    se_blocks[block source for replay: db, seenBlockInputCache]:::value
    se_store[checkpoint state datastore: file or db, dataDir]:::value
    se_clock[clock, abort signal]:::value
    se_caches[block, checkpoint, shuffling caches + regen queue]:::missing
    se_obs[metrics, validatorMonitor, logger, emitter]:::native
  end

  subgraph ve [IValidationEngine]
    ve_cfg[BeaconConfig]:::native
    ve_bls[BLS verifier]:::native
    ve_fc[IForkChoice]:::value
    ve_se[IStateEngine, head state]:::value
    ve_clock[clock, genesis time, opts]:::value
    ve_assembly[seenBlockInputCache, seenPayloadEnvelopeInputCache reads]:::value
    ve_bid[predictProposerHead, getParentExecutionRequests for bids]:::value
    ve_db[db for persisted pools]:::value
    ve_kzg[KZG for blob and column sidecars]:::missing
    ve_pools[pools and seen caches]:::missing
    ve_obs[metrics, logger]:::native
  end

  se --> ve
  fc --> ve
  se -. builds .-> fc

  L1[native in lodestar-z today]:::native
  L2[plain value, or a JS object passed in or called back]:::value
  L3[not in lodestar-z yet, has to be written]:::missing
```

Reading it per seam:

- `IForkChoice`: lodestar-z has `src/fork_choice/` (unbound, no fast confirmation). A native build needs the four event callbacks into JS, and either runs fast confirmation in JS on top or refuses `fastConfirmation` with `nativeForkChoice`.
- `IStateEngine`: lodestar-z has `BlockStateCache` and `CPStateDatastore` (unbound), no regen and no KV store. A native build still gets blocks for replay and persisted checkpoint bytes from JS. Native state lifetime (refcount versus scoped borrow) has to be decided before any native cache hands states to JS.
- `IValidationEngine`: BLS and config are native; the pools and seen caches are new Zig; KZG is missing. The per-topic shape lets a native engine own some topics while the rest stay JS, routed by `TopicRoutedValidationEngine`.

## One message end to end

A gossip attestation, showing why validate and import are two calls on the same interface.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant H as Gossip handler
  participant E as IValidationEngine
  participant S as seen caches
  participant P as attestation pool
  participant F as IForkChoice

  H->>E: validateGossipAttestationsSameAttData(fork, attestations)
  E->>S: seenAttestationDatas, seenAttesters
  E-->>H: BatchResult (verdicts returned to gossipsub first)
  Note over H: next event loop tick
  H->>E: importAttestation(result, addToPool, addToForkChoice)
  E->>P: add (error logged, never skips the vote)
  E->>F: onAttestation(indexedAttestation, attDataRoot)
  E-->>H: InsertOutcome or null
```

## Flags

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  ST[nativeStateTransition] --> FC[nativeForkChoice] --> SE[nativeStateEngine] --> VT[nativeValidationTopics]
  FC --> f1{initializeForkChoice}
  f1 -->|false| FCJS[ForkChoice, JS]
  f1 -->|true| N1[NOT_IMPLEMENTED]
  SE --> f2{createStateEngine}
  f2 -->|false| SEJS[StateEngine, JS]
  f2 -->|true| N2[NOT_IMPLEMENTED]
  VT --> f3{createValidationEngine}
  f3 -->|empty| VEJS[ValidationEngine, JS]
  f3 -->|topics| N3[NOT_IMPLEMENTED, later TopicRoutedValidationEngine]
```

Each flag requires the one before it, checked by `assertNativeComponentOpts` in the `BeaconChain` constructor, because native fork choice reads the native state, the native state engine walks native fork choice, and native validation reads both. No CLI flags yet.

## Behavior deltas worth a look

- Attestation and payload attestation pool errors on the API routes are logged and the fork choice vote still happens, instead of failing that message. Same as the gossip path already did.
- The justified balances fallback no longer throws when the checkpoint block is not in the proto array, and the `descendant_state_latter_epoch` branch now returns the descendant state it found (it returned the block state before).
- `validateApiSyncCommittee` does the committee membership lookup itself; it used to live in the pool API route.
- The proposer preferences API route no longer re-adds to the pool after validation already did.
- The four ops topics are one `operations` topic: they share `OpPool` and its block-production read.
- Pool size metrics are collected on scrape by the pools' owner instead of set by the chain; names unchanged.
- The unreachable "n-historical-state flag is not enabled" throw in `getPersistedCheckpointState` was dropped.

## Not in this PR

- The JS `ValidationEngine` and the validators in `chain/validation/*.ts` still take `IBeaconChain`, for config, clock, BLS, fork choice, state engine, head state, logger, metrics, the two block assembly caches, and the pools and seen caches as `chain.<pool>` aliases. A native engine cannot take a chain, so the follow-up gives both engines the same explicit dependency set (`ValidationContext`: config, clock, bls, forkChoice, stateEngine, caches, logger, metrics) and drops the chain aliases. 16 validators and 34 tests of plumbing.
- Light client finality and optimistic updates stay direct: they validate against the light client server, which stays JS.
- Native state lifetime (refcount in Zig versus scoped borrow) must be decided before any native state cache; today nothing calls `release()` and states are freed by GC.
- KZG before the sidecar topics can go native.
- Fork choice spec tests and `fast_confirmation.test.ts` were not run locally (vectors not downloaded); the runners go through `BeaconChain`, so CI exercises the seams.

## Verification

- `check-types` for `@lodestar/fork-choice` and `@lodestar/beacon-node`: clean.
- `pnpm lint`: clean except 3 pre-existing warnings in untouched files.
- `packages/fork-choice` unit tests: 322 pass.
- `packages/beacon-node` `test/unit/chain test/unit/api test/unit/network test/unit/node test/unit/sync test/unit/execution`: 1923 pass.
- e2e `test/e2e/chain/proposerBoostReorg.test.ts` and `test/e2e/chain/stateCache/nHistoricalStates.test.ts` on a real chain: pass.

title: fix: bound the envelope transaction count by the bid's gas limit
body:
Implements https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5786.

The `execution_payload` gossip validation gets a new REJECT rule, `len(payload.transactions) <= bid.gas_limit // MIN_TRANSACTION_GAS`. `MIN_TRANSACTION_GAS` is a lower bound on the gas used by a single transaction, so the transaction count is bounded by the gas limit the proposer committed to in the bid.

- add `MIN_TRANSACTION_GAS` to the chain config
- read the transaction count from the SSZ offsets and run the check before the envelope is deserialized, deferring to the full validation if the data is malformed or one of the IGNORE conditions that precede the rule applies
- run the same check in `validateExecutionPayloadEnvelope` before the signature verification

Should only be merged once the spec change is released.

title: feat: reduce block retention window to 8192 epochs in heze (EIP-8383)
body:
Implements [EIP-8383](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8383) for heze, which lowers the block serving and retention window from 33024 to 8192 epochs (~36 days on mainnet).

Builds on #10120, which adds `config.getMinEpochsForBlockRequests(epoch)`, uses it for the `--chain.pruneHistory` cutoff and the `BeaconBlocksByHead` lower bound, and caps the blocks pruned per run on a running node. The gloas reduction from #10120 is left out for now per https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10120#issuecomment-6513977110, this PR only changes the window from heze.

- add `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS_HEZE` (8192 on mainnet and minimal), `getMinEpochsForBlockRequests` returns it from heze and `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS` before
- update `--chain.pruneHistory` help text and data retention docs

There is no consensus-specs PR for EIP-8383 yet. The EIP sets `MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOCK_REQUESTS = 8192` on the existing key, gives no minimal value and says no hard fork is required. The `_HEZE` key and the heze gate are our choice so that mainnet is unchanged before Hegotá, and the minimal value is a placeholder. From heze the window is below the 14299 epochs the pinned spec (v1.7.0-beta.4) requires from gloas, which is intended by the EIP. Both will be aligned once the spec PR exists.
