title: feat: implement EIP-8148 custom sweep threshold in heze
body:
**Motivation**

EIP-8148 (custom validator sweep threshold) was CFI'd for Hegotá at ACDC #190. The spec is merged in consensus-specs as `specs/_features/eip8148` on top of Heze, but not yet folded into `specs/heze`, so no release carries Heze vectors with it. This PR implements it in Heze ahead of that fold-in.

**Description**

Implements EIP-8148 as part of Heze, following the `specs/_features/eip8148` text as amended by https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5790 (threshold stored in the withdrawal credentials, per https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12598).

- `SetSweepThresholdRequest` and `SweepThresholdRequests` SSZ types and `sweep_thresholds` on the Heze `ExecutionRequests`. The Heze containers embedding `ExecutionRequests` (`BeaconBlockBody`, `ExecutionPayloadEnvelope`, header envelope, `NewPayloadRequest`, `BlockContents`) are redefined, and the gloas-pinned envelope and requests call sites in beacon-node, builder, validator and the API now resolve the type by fork. The Heze `BeaconState` is unchanged
- the sweep threshold is read from and written to bytes 1..2 of the compounding withdrawal credentials (`getSweepThreshold`, `withSweepThreshold`), with `MAX_EFFECTIVE_BALANCE_ELECTRA` stored as zero and out-of-range values read as the default
- `process_set_sweep_threshold_request` runs from `parent_execution_requests` and rewrites the credentials; the validator sweep and `process_effective_balance_updates` use the threshold; new compounding validators store their threshold in canonical form with the initial effective balance capped at it; `switch_to_compounding_validator` and `upgrade_to_heze` clear the bytes
- `SWEEP_THRESHOLD_REQUEST_TYPE` (0x05) in the EIP-7685 engine encoding and in the config constants
- `MAX_SET_SWEEP_THRESHOLD_REQUESTS_PER_PAYLOAD` preset (16)

**Gloas to Heze boundary**

The feature's fork.md leaves open how the first Heze block validates a FULL pre-fork parent, since the parent bid's `execution_requests_root` commits to the 5-field Gloas `ExecutionRequests` whose root differs from the 6-field Heze type. This PR validates `parent_execution_requests` against the Gloas type when the parent block's epoch is before `state.fork.epoch` (the Heze fork epoch after `upgrade_to_heze`), and requires `sweep_thresholds` to be empty in that case. The same rule is in the spec fold-in branch below. If the fold-in settles on something else, this needs to follow.

**Spec vectors**

v1.7.0-beta.4 has no EIP-8148 Heze vectors, so the Heze suites are skipped in `specTestIterator.ts` except `ssz_static` for containers EIP-8148 does not touch, which now includes `BeaconState` (same approach as #10314 for EIP-8015). The skip is lifted when a release containing the fold-in is pinned.

Verification ran against Heze minimal vectors generated from a consensus-specs branch that folds EIP-8148 into Heze and adds tests for it: https://github.com/ensi321/consensus-specs/tree/eip8148-heze-v2 (commit 79af2c91d: consensus-specs#5790 cherry-picked on master plus the fold-in; generated locally with `make test reftests=true preset=minimal fork=heze`; once Actions is enabled on that fork, `pnpm download-spec-tests latest ensi321/consensus-specs eip8148-heze-v2` works too). With the Heze skip lifted locally, the complete Heze minimal vector set from that branch gives:

| suite | result |
| --- | --- |
| operations (incl. 12 `set_sweep_threshold_request`, 3 `parent_execution_payload` sweep cases, custom-threshold withdrawals, consolidation clearing the bytes) | all pass |
| sanity, epoch_processing (incl. `pending_deposits` initial thresholds with capped effective balance, `effective_balance_updates` cap), fork (incl. the bytes cleared at the fork), transition (incl. the two first-Heze-block cases), fork_choice, networking, light_client, rewards, random, ssz_static | all pass |
| fast_confirmation | 12 failures |
| total | 10748 passed, 12 failed, 26 skipped |

The 12 fast confirmation failures are not EIP-8148: ten of them are tests that do not exist in v1.7.0-beta.4 and come from consensus-specs#5670 (precise committee weight), #5783 and #5788, which Lodestar's fast confirmation does not implement yet, and the other two were modified by the same PRs. A gloas fast confirmation run from the same branch, which EIP-8148 does not touch, is in progress to confirm they fail the same way; the result will be posted here.

**Checks**

- `pnpm check-types`, `pnpm lint`, `ethspecify check --path=specrefs`
- unit tests: types, params, config, api, state-transition, builder, and the beacon-node engine, db, archive, reqresp, validation and produceBlock suites
- v1.7.0-beta.4 minimal spec tests: gloas fully green (10372 passed), heze `ssz_static` fully green with the skip list applied (8450 passed)

title: perf: parallelize balances leaf hashing
body:
**Motivation**

Moved from ChainSafe/lodestar-z#815 now that lodestar-z is merged into Lodestar (#10513).

At every epoch boundary `processRewardsAndPenalties` rebuilds the balances list through `setBalances`. On mainnet that is about 9k `ChunkedLeaf` nodes with lazy roots, and the next state-root computation hashes them one by one on a single thread, which is nearly all of the epoch's state-root cost.

**Description**

Hash the balances `ChunkedLeaf` roots in parallel on the `std.Io` pool right after `setBalances`.

- `Node.Id.computeChunkedLeafRoots`: hashes the lazy roots of the given chunked leaves, 64 per `std.Io.Group.async` task
- `hashChunkedLeaves(io)` on `ListBasicTreeView` and `ProgressiveListBasicTreeView` (Gloas+ balances)
- `processRewardsAndPenalties` takes `io` and calls it after `setBalances`; callers pass `io` through
- `expectConsensusInvalid` treats `error.Canceled` as an infrastructure error

| ReleaseSafe | `unstable` | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| `bench_process_epoch` epoch, Apple M5 | 98.8 ms | 71.8 ms |
| `bench_process_epoch` epoch, EPYC 9634 | 110.2 ms | 93.1 ms |
| 128-block mainnet replay, per epoch boundary, EPYC 9634 | 136.8 ms | 123.0 ms |

State roots are unchanged. This saves wall time only; total CPU time is the same.

title: perf: reuse epoch transition buffers
body:
**Motivation**

Moved from ChainSafe/lodestar-z#817 and ChainSafe/lodestar-z#819 now that lodestar-z is merged into Lodestar (#10513).

Every epoch transition allocates and frees two validator-count `u64` arrays (18.5 MB each on mainnet): the cached balances built in `processRewardsAndPenalties`, and the inactivity scores `processInactivityUpdates` reads with `getAll`. Release bindings are ReleaseSafe, where `Allocator.alloc` and `free` fill the whole buffer with `0xAA`, about 2.6 ms per fill on an EPYC 9634. The cached balances also had no spare capacity, so the first new validator in `processPendingDeposits` reallocated and copied the whole list.

**Description**

Keep both buffers in `ReusedEpochTransitionCache`, next to rewards and penalties.

- Reserve `MAX_PENDING_DEPOSITS_PER_EPOCH` spare balances so `applyPendingDeposit` uses `appendAssumeCapacity`
- `balances_buffer`: borrowed by `EpochTransitionCache`; `processRewardsAndPenalties` builds `cache.balances` over it with `ArrayList.initBuffer`, and `deinit` no longer frees it
- `inactivity_scores_buffer`: filled with `getAllInto`; `processInactivityUpdates` no longer takes an allocator

Each thread that runs an epoch transition keeps two more validator-count arrays alive (37 MB at 2.3M validators), as it already does for rewards and penalties.

128-block mainnet replay on an EPYC 9634, ReleaseSafe, median per epoch boundary: 131.1 ms on `unstable`, 116.4 ms with this PR.

title: test: reuse one node pool across Zig spec test cases
body:
Every Zig spec test case allocates its own `Node.Pool` sized for the largest state, 1M nodes for the ssz tests and 10M nodes for the mainnet state transition tests. At 44 bytes per node that is 44 MB and 440 MB per case, and safe builds fill the whole buffer on allocation and again on free. This setup dominates the runtime: ssz_static minimal runs 56,826 cases in ~35 min (~36 ms per case) and mainnet operations runs 2,562 cases in ~20 min (~0.45 s per case), both close to 1 GB/s of pool churn. The generated sanity, random and finality tests also allocated the pool before skipping cases that don't exist for the preset.

Cases now share one pool per test binary. A case that leaves nodes behind drops the pool, so the next case still starts from an empty one.

- add `acquirePool` / `releasePool` to the spec and ssz test case helpers
- use the shared pool in the ssz cases, the operations, epoch processing, rewards, fork and transition runners, and the generated sanity, random and finality tests
- run ssz_static spec tests in ReleaseSafe for both presets

title: fix: compute exact committee weight in fast confirmation
body:
## Motivation

[consensus-specs#5670](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5670) replaced the fast confirmation committee weight estimate with an exact computation. The estimate derived `total_active_balance // SLOTS_PER_EPOCH` per slot and bumped the result by a safety factor for ranges crossing an epoch boundary; its accuracy depended on stake consolidation. The spec now takes the union of the head state committees over the slot range and sums the balances of those validators as seen by the balance source. [consensus-specs#5788](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5788) followed up by turning the `compute_safety_threshold` underflow guard into an assertion, since the discount can no longer exceed the maximum support.

## Description

- `estimateCommitteeWeightBetweenSlots` → `computeCommitteeWeightBetweenSlots`. `COMMITTEE_WEIGHT_ESTIMATION_ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR` and `adjustCommitteeWeightEstimateToEnsureSafety` are removed.
- The committees are gathered with a backwards sweep from the end slot (`CommitteeSweep`), built once per end slot and extended on demand. All call sites in a run share a handful of end slots (mostly `current_slot - 1`) with many start slots, so this avoids rebuilding a union of up to ~1M validators per evaluated block. A validator is recorded at the latest slot it is assigned to, so committees overlapping across an epoch boundary are counted once.
- The sweep replaces the previous `committeeBySlot` cache. `getNodeSupportBetweenSlots` and `getEquivocationScore` read the participant list as a prefix of the sweep instead of building a `Set` per call.
- `computeSafetyThreshold` throws if `supportDiscount > maximumSupport` (spec assertion); the runner already reverts to the finalized root on a throw.
- specrefs updated for the renamed function and the removed constant and helper.

Mainnet-shaped timing (1M validators, 92 range queries as in an epoch-boundary chain walk): spec-literal per-call union ~3 s, sweep 14 to 31 ms.

## Testing

- fork-choice unit tests: 171 passed, including new tests for cross-epoch dedupe, inactive validators, the full-epoch case and memo ordering
- Nightly `fast_confirmation` vectors (consensus-specs master at 1bdf4b8, includes #5670): 1484 passed, 2 failed. The two failures are the fulu and gloas copies of `is_one_confirmed_fails_recently_activated_validator_voting_in_empty_slot`, whose vector skipped a per-slot FCR run; fixed upstream in [consensus-specs#5783](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/5783) and verified passing with regenerated electra and heze vectors
- Pinned `v1.7.0-beta.4` vectors predate #5670 and are not expected to agree on the new committee-weight cases
- `pnpm lint`, `pnpm --filter @lodestar/fork-choice check-types`

Follow-up: consolidate the remaining per-balance-source caches (`voteWeightBySource`, `totalActiveBalanceByKey`, sweep weights) into one map keyed by state reference and drop `ancestorRoots`.

title: fix(api): keep timeout signals local to retry attempts
body:
**Motivation**

With `retries > 0`, a timed-out request can prevent later attempts from reaching the server. `_request` stores its controller's signal in the `init` object shared by retries. Once that signal is aborted, the next attempt treats it as caller cancellation and returns `ErrorAborted`.

**Description**

Pass the attempt-local signal only to `createApiRequest`, without replacing `init.signal`. Retry counts, backoff, wire formats and caller cancellation are unchanged. The default retry count remains zero.

The new tests cover recovery after one timeout, repeated timeouts, and global/local caller cancellation. On unmodified `unstable`, the two timeout tests fail with `ErrorAborted`; both cancellation controls pass. With the fix, all four pass. They use fake timers and an injected fetch implementation, with no external services.

**Validation**

Node 24.22.1, pnpm 11.0.0. Built the native binding with Zig 0.16.0 and `pnpm --filter @lodestar/native run prepare-mainnet -j2` for the standard test setup.

- `pnpm exec vitest run --project unit packages/api/test/unit/client`: 43 tests passed across 8 files.
- `pnpm --filter @lodestar/api check-types`: passed.
- `pnpm lint`: passed with seven warnings in untouched files.

No native sources changed. The full monorepo, spec and e2e test suites were not run.

title: chore: let Lerna publish the native wrapper package
body:
publish-dev has failed on every unstable push since https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10513. zapi published `@lodestar/native` seconds before `lerna publish from-package` checked the registry. npm still reported the version as unpublished, so Lerna ran the wrapper's `prepublishOnly` guard and the job failed. Only the 7 native packages reached npm, and the Docker publish was skipped.

This bumps zapi to 4.3.0 (https://github.com/ChainSafe/zapi/pull/88) and splits publishing by package type:

- zapi builds and publishes only the platform packages, with `--skip-existing` so a failed release can be re-run from any point.
- Lerna publishes the wrapper with the other packages. Its `prepack` script (`zapi prepublish --main-only`) pins the platform packages as `optionalDependencies`, replacing the throwing guard.

Verified locally with fake artifacts:

- `zapi publish --platforms-only --skip-existing --dry-run` would publish all 6 platforms for an unpublished version and skips all 6 for `1.51.0-dev.122e5d5f21`.
- `lerna publish from-package --dry-run` found only `@lodestar/native@1.50.1` unpublished, ran `prepack`, and the packed tarball lists all 6 platform `optionalDependencies`.
author: nflaig

title: chore(ci): key the Zig cache by host glibc and kernel
body:
Build takes 2.3 to 3.2 min since https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10513, up from about 1 min. 108 s of that is compiling the native bindings, even when no Zig code changed.

setup-zig keys its cache by job id only, so the `build` jobs of Tests, Sim tests and Check docs share one cache and restores pick the newest. Check docs runs on `ubuntu-latest` (glibc 2.39) and finishes last, while the other two run on Warp (glibc 2.35). Zig's native target includes the host glibc and kernel versions, so the Warp builds never hit that cache. On https://github.com/ChainSafe/lodestar/pull/10527, Build restored the Check docs cache from f2b568e3d0 and recompiled from scratch.

This adds the host glibc and kernel release to the setup-zig cache key, so jobs only share caches built for a matching host. The build cache key reuses the same glibc detection.

The first run on this branch starts from empty caches. The effect shows from the next commit without Zig changes, which should bring Build back to about 1 min.
author: nflaig

title: chore(ci): build release binary bindings for an explicit glibc target
body:
The Linux release binaries bundle `bindings/zig-out`, which zapi loads before the platform packages. setup-and-build compiles it for the host, so it links against the runner's glibc and requires `GLIBC_2.34` (`pthread_create`, `pthread_join`, ...). The npm platform packages, built by zapi with an explicit `-Dtarget`, only require `GLIBC_2.30`. Before the lodestar-z merge the binaries used the npm prebuilt, so the next release would stop starting on Debian 11, Ubuntu 20.04 and RHEL 8.

This rebuilds the bindings for `<arch>-linux-gnu` before packaging, matching the zapi build. The rebuild runs after setup-and-build saves its build cache, so the cached host build is unaffected.
author: nflaig

title: chore: resolve pnpm catalog dependencies when publishing
body:
lerna-lite only reads the catalog in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` when `npmClient` is `pnpm`. Without it, `catalog:` specs are published unchanged. Every release since the pnpm migration (1.47.0 to 1.50.1, 1.51.0-rc.0) ships `"@chainsafe/lodestar-z": "catalog:"` in beacon-node, cli, state-transition and others, so `npm install @chainsafe/lodestar@1.50.1` fails with `EUNSUPPORTEDPROTOCOL`. lodestar-z left the catalog with the merge, but `@lodestar/spec-test-util` still ships `"vitest": "catalog:"`.

Tested with `lerna publish from-package --dry-run` at a temporary version: spec-test-util packs `"vitest": "^4.0.7"`, and the native wrapper's `prepack` still adds its 6 platform `optionalDependencies`. `npmClient` does not change how lifecycle scripts run, and `lerna version` does not touch the lockfile without `--sync-workspace-lock`.

title: feat: migrate native networking into Lodestar
body:
## Native networking in the unified repository

Continues @wemeetagain's ChainSafe/lodestar-z#782 after the native-code repository migration in #10513. The source head is `f4c65173c6d5d3ef379e864867f687478c14a1db`; its history and authorship are preserved by merging it into `unstable`.

The native stack provides DiscV5 discovery, QUIC transport, request/response, gossip scheduling, and the Node binding's admission, delivery, and completion lifecycle. This port preserves that implementation rather than revising protocol behavior or ownership rules.

### Repository integration

- Expose the existing facade as `@lodestar/native/network`, alongside the existing native exports.
- Move network declaration checks and lifecycle tests into the `bindings` workspace. Resolve subprocess fixtures from the repository root rather than the caller's working directory.
- Keep independently pinned libp2p peers and the published response decoder in a private `test/interop` workspace. They must not silently resolve to the local Lodestar implementation.
- Integrate discovery, interoperability, policy, lifecycle, and fuzz checks with the consolidated CI. Supply the Rust, CMake, libclang, and LLVM prerequisites to native builds, release jobs, and Docker build stages.
- Retain the destination's package layout, release flow, and already-landed native changes. No TypeScript consumer package is changed here.

The beacon-node adoption remains separate in #10375. That branch still needs its imports and dependency wiring adapted to the unified package; this PR does not enable a new networking backend in the beacon node.

### Draft boundary

This is a migration draft, not a claim that the imported feature is merge-ready. A fresh build of the original source reproduces three stock-binding failures: local request-capacity refusal, terminal peer scoring, and same-fork BPO gossip delivery. The network benchmark also fails to compile because its 13-element policy arrays no longer match the 17-kind inventory. Those failures are retained rather than mixed with behavior-changing fixes in this port. Supported-platform and packaged-artifact qualification remain outstanding.

Refs ChainSafe/lodestar-z#782, #10375.

### AI assistance disclosure

The original implementation was primarily authored with OpenAI Codex under maintainer direction, as disclosed in the source PR. This repository migration and its verification were performed with Hermes Agent. The draft remains subject to human review.
